repair.epic_title: compat(app): Electron app lifecycle, single-instance, session facts and process shim over host-owned lifecycle
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
Electron v44.4.5 (tag commit 694f45852a0f1726cd23bfd379854de489cccb65) `app` module (115 members: 75 methods, 30 events, 10 properties), `CommandLine` (5), `Dock` (11, macOS) and the main-process `process` surface (29): 160 members. Each one is assigned to an F01 ticket, a ticket in another unit, the never list, out of scope, or not yet specified. Coverage was checked mechanically against the v44.4.5 API model: 0 members are unassigned.

FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1, read 2026-10-07): these are live today: `app.whenReady/isReady/quit/on/off/removeListener`, the `ready` and `window-all-closed` events, the default quit on last-window-close when no listener is registered, `process.type = 'browser'` and `process.versions.electron = '0.0.1'` (landed KEL-72). Every other member is TARGET.

## Corpus demand (direct grep of the pinned clones; token-scan counts rejected)
Sites are given as draw.io @2edf9fb / Zettlr @e6c7fd8:
- whenReady 2/1, window-all-closed 2/1, activate 1/1, quit 5/10, exit 3/2
- getPath 3/40, getVersion 4/6, name 3/0, getName 0/2, getLocale 1/2, isPackaged 0/7
- requestSingleInstanceLock 1/1, second-instance 1/1, app.on('open-file') 1/1 (draw.io registers it inside will-finish-launching)
- before-quit 1/1, will-quit 0/1, relaunch 0/4, setPath 0/1, setAppLogsPath 0/1, setAppUserModelId 0/1
- disableHardwareAcceleration 1/1 (both behind a CLI flag), web-contents-created 1/1, process.defaultApp 1/0
- app.commandLine 0/0, app.dock 0/0

electron-quick-start uses whenReady, activate, window-all-closed and quit, once each.

These earlier claims are retracted: 'focus/show (Zettlr 26/18)' was bare-member attribution from BrowserWindow/WebContents (direct grep finds 0 app.focus/app.show). 'app.exit 7/14' and 'open-file 20 sites' were also wrong.

Ecosystem packages that draw.io imports at module top level:
- FACT, source fetched 2026-10-07: electron-store v11.0.2 main-process initialisation calls `app.getPath('userData')` and `app.getVersion()` synchronously and registers an `ipcMain` listener.
- FACT, source fetched 2026-10-07: electron-context-menu v5.1.0 calls `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` and `app.on('browser-window-created')`.
- FACT, source fetched 2026-10-07: electron-log v5.4.4 reads `app.name/getName/getPath/getVersion/isPackaged`, registers `web-contents-created`/`session-created`, and uses `app.once('ready')` only when it exists.
- UNKNOWN: which of these package calls run at import. PANEL-P3 settles it.

## Pull order and tier
Tier labels stay on the arch 04 §4 taxonomy. Pull order comes from milestone labels:
- First proof (drawio-desktop, macOS, explicit legacy profile, authority_profile LegacySandboxOff): F01-T1 → F01-T2; F01-T1 + PANEL-P3 → F01-T4 → F01-T5.
- Next (Zettlr tranche): F01-T3, F01-T7, F01-T8, F01-T10, F01-T11.
- Parked: F01-T6, F01-T9.

## Maturity ladder (exit criteria)
- L0: every family member either works or throws a typed `KELD-COMPAT` unsupported error with a scoreboard row; never a silent no-op. The owner is F01-T6, which is parked.
- L1: electron-quick-start and draw.io boot on macOS. This needs session facts synchronous at import, `whenReady` resolving after host Ready before any app window, a real single-instance verdict, and `window-all-closed` keeping draw.io alive. `activate` arrives at the next milestone (F01-T10).
- L2: the `before-quit → close(each window) → will-quit → quit` sequence and its cancellation pass conformance cells citing pinned v44.4.5 sentences, with negative controls. `second-instance` is delivered exactly once, after ready.
- L3: draw.io and then Zettlr primary workflows exercise the family under `keld dev`. KEL-74 records carry the authority profile. Claims are stated only as `{passed}/{N} of {panel} corpus {id}@{digest} ({kind})`.

## Linear owners consumed (live status: Linear, fetched 2026-10-07)
- KEL-72 Done, unassigned: landed facade lifecycle shim, consumed as an artifact, not a live owner.
- KEL-142 Done: AC4 is the host-Ready gate for whenReady.
- KEL-139 Done (completed 2026-09-29): AC5 covers recovery; AC6 covers the single ordered quit owner. Amending it needs the repository owner.
- KEL-96 In Progress, assignee GYLDLAB: §4.4/§4.5 boot and quit order; keld.boot.json schema v1.
- KEL-75 In Progress, unassigned: role spawn contract and supervisor.
- KEL-78 In Progress, assignee GYLDLAB: strict containment.
- KEL-143 Backlog, unassigned: generation recovery and window retention.
- KEL-141 Backlog, unassigned: macOS installed artifact.
- KEL-237 In Progress, unassigned. Its lifecycle corpus is pinned to Electron 44.3.0, and its non-goals exclude compatibility-surface expansion.
- KEL-74 Done, assignee GYLDLAB: evidence schema and Verdict vocabulary.
- KEL-15 Done, GYLDLAB: four-file config contract.
- KEL-19 Done, GYLDLAB: packaging is tracked on it by owner direction.
- KEL-135 In Progress, Amisha Ramani: engine profile roots.
- KEL-132 In Progress, unassigned: GPU policy.
- KEL-127 Todo, unassigned: program entry reading.

No live KEL issue's scope covers the new F01 conformance cells, the single-instance primitive, the macOS reopen hook, deeplink admission or app.exit. FACT (GitHub #517, owner decision comment recorded 2026-10-07; X06-D7): each repo-writing ticket is claimed on the nearest live Linear issue whose scope covers it; otherwise its GitHub issue is the tracker of record (the `## Agent claim` comment, status, handoffs and evidence live there), no Linear issue is created, and the nearest live Linear issue for the surface (fallback KEL-127) carries a link to it. The owner record names root AGENTS.md and the workflow claim protocol as still Linear-only and makes #517 plus map #391 the documented exception agents cite until that separate instruction amendment lands. A missing Linear owner is therefore not a hold on any F01 ticket; each ticket states its tracker of record.

## Design facts (labelled)
- FACT: the keld-core primary router emits lifecycle `Ready` on the first host-created window's NavigationReady. KEL-96 §4.4 orders authenticate → CreateInitialWindow → Ready. The `LifecycleEvent::Ready` wire doc already says 'The host is ready for the app process to create windows / run', so the re-base (F01-T2) changes the emission point, not the wire.
- INFERENCE: the KEL-237 when-ready cell stays green after the re-base. F01-T2 must run it to prove this.
- FACT: keld-core already replays Ready to a recovered generation (test 'G2 Ready replay' at 8678c0d1). For facade boots, what a recovered generation means is a missing decision: the compat main-role loss policy, X06-D1 correction (c).
- FACT: two window-count owners coexist: a test-only LifecycleSession counter, and the keld-wv backend one-to-zero transition consumed by the primary router. activate(hasVisibleWindows) waits on F02-T2's single registry owner.
- FACT: Quit is a one-shot correlated Call with no veto. No applicationShouldTerminate/windowShouldClose/applicationShouldHandleReopen hook exists in the crates at 8678c0d1.
- FACT (browser.cc v44.4.5): a close veto during quit cancels the quit. `window-all-closed` is not emitted while quitting. After a vetoed will-quit, a second app.quit() re-emits before-quit.
- FACT: app.exit cannot be process.exit. The supervisor recovers nonzero Bun exits, and an unrequested post-ready status-zero exit is KELD-RUNTIME-012. `keld dev` collapses a non-success host status into its own exit 1/2.
- FACT: on macOS and Windows the role environment is inherited from the host minus removals; Linux strict passes an explicit list. No facade may read HOME/APPDATA/XDG; host-minted session facts are the only path source.
- FACT: draw.io constructs electron-store at module top level inside try/catch, falling back to `store = null`. Its direct `getPath('userData')` call runs after ready. It reads process.argv/env/platform at module top level.
- FACT: no-flag boot never parses keld.config.ts (KEL-96-D3). Every host-consumed declaration (single-instance, role environment) reaches the host through the compiled keld.boot.json schema v1, whose fields are closed. Adding one is a public-contract change.
- FACT: 'boot descriptor' already names keld.boot.json (CLI→host). The host→app facts are therefore called 'session facts', a distinct name.
- FACT: keld-pack is not name-only. It owns the Windows package producer and the ExpectedAppIdentity container. What is missing is an Info.plist/.desktop/MSIX declaration emitter (F01-A5, parked).
- FACT: the receipts in electron_api_app.cc v44.4.5 give the exact post-ready throw texts for enableSandbox and disableHardwareAcceleration.

## Platform lanes
macOS first: 44 members are macOS-tagged (Dock, open-file/open-url, activate, Handoff). Windows has 20 members (jump lists, AppUserModelId, toast activator); Linux has 4 (badge, desktop name). Windows/Linux cells are recorded `unknown` until their lane runs. `before-quit/will-quit/quit` are not emitted on Windows shutdown or logoff; this is documented ▲.

tickets.current_behavior: FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1): the KEL-237 lifecycle corpus 'electron-lifecycle-v0' has three cells (host-ready gate, window-all-closed policy, quit return contract). It is pinned to Electron 44.3.0, and its validator accepts only expected verdicts pass and fail, where fail requires a named intentional divergence. No cell covers session facts, Ready-before-window or the single-instance verdict.
tickets.what_to_build:
Land Keld-owned conformance cells for the first-proof app surface in an F01 family manifest. The manifest is parsed, digest-checked and admitted by the X01-T4 shared corpus-manifest owner (the migrated KEL-237 validator), adds no second corpus format or parser, and carries the single pin the X01-T3 pin rule sets for new corpora: Electron v44.4.5 (tag commit 694f458…). Each cell cites the exact pinned app.md sentence and one observable sequence.

Cells:
1. `ready` is emitted once, before any app window exists.
2. `whenReady()` resolves iff `isReady()` is true. A `ready` listener registered after the event fired is not called, while `whenReady()` still resolves. INFERENCE from EventEmitter semantics and the whenReady sentence; X01-T2's recorded transcript confirms it.
3. Session facts are synchronous before ready: `getPath('userData')` equals Electron's documented default for the app name; `getVersion`, `getName`/`name`, `getAppPath` and `getLocale` return without awaiting; `isPackaged` is false under keld dev. The (argv, defaultApp) and resourcesPath cells are X03-T3's, not this manifest's.
4. `requestSingleInstanceLock()` returns true for the first instance and false for a second instance of the same declared app; `hasSingleInstanceLock()` agrees.

Red-until-implemented: this ticket adds no runner rule of its own. Each pending cell is recorded in the X01-T3 red-until-implemented representation: expected verdict `fail` with its implementing-ticket key, and a mapped test that asserts today's behaviour and passes; the implementing change inverts the test and flips the cell to `pass` in the same diff. The implementing tickets are F01-T2, F01-T4 and F01-T5. `unknown` is used only for uncited, observed-only or unrun-lane cells (here, the Windows and Linux records). No cell is skipped, ignored or retried.

The three electron-lifecycle-v0 cells, its corpus digest and its committed receipts stay byte-unchanged at their 44.3.0 pin. FACT, recorded so a later deliberate re-pin is mechanical: the ready, window-all-closed, before-quit, will-quit and quit sentences are byte-identical between 44.3.0 (07e4607) and v44.4.5.

Ownership: F01-T2, F01-T4 and F01-T5 implement against these cells. The quit-ordering cells belong to F01-T3, the activate cells to F01-T10 and the delivery cells to F01-T8, so this first-proof ticket carries no next-milestone cells.

tickets.title: feat(app): re-base host Ready to "host initialized, window module available" before any app window for facade boots (KEL-96 §4.4/§4.5 and KEL-139 amendment)
tickets.current_behavior: FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1): the keld-core primary router emits Ready on NavigationReady of the host-created initial window (KEL-96 §4.4 step order: authenticate → CreateInitialWindow → Ready). keld-core replays Ready to a recovered generation (test 'G2 Ready replay'). keld.boot.json schema v1 has closed required fields, including `renderer`.
tickets.what_to_build:
This ticket owns one atom: who creates window #1, and what Ready means per generation.

For a facade boot (an @keld/electron main), the host emits Ready after authenticated HELLO and creates no initial window; the app creates windows through F02-T2's create Call. The wire enum is unchanged. Its doc already reads 'ready for the app process to create windows / run'.

The spec amendment (KEL-96 §4.4/§4.5, KEL-139) must decide two things:
(a) How a facade boot is declared to the host. `renderer` is a required schema-v1 field, so this is a schema change.
(b) Whether renderer-declared boots keep CreateInitialWindow before Ready. INFERENCE: if Ready moves for them too, KEL-139/KEL-142 fixtures that treat Ready as 'renderer navigated' must re-sequence on a window-specific event.

Recovered generations: for facade boots, a recovered generation must never produce a second window for a document the lost generation opened. Whether the session ends or windows are adopted is the compat main-role loss decision (X06-D1 correction (c): default Electron-faithful, meaning role loss ends the session under legacy). That decision does not exist yet, so its cell stays `unknown`. The existing non-facade replay is not changed.

Adjacent atoms: F02-T2 is blocked by this ticket and builds no transitional adoption shim (the edge is recorded by the F02 owner). KEL-143 is consumed only if adoption is ever chosen.

The cold-start delta (HELLO → module evaluation → first window create) is measured under X05-T1's registered metric. It is not an acceptance criterion here.

tickets.title: feat(app): host-minted session facts at spawn for synchronous app getters (getPath, getVersion, getName/name, getAppPath, getLocale, isPackaged) and the declared role environment — legacy path values
tickets.current_behavior: FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1): @keld/electron exposes nothing synchronous at import beyond process.type and process.versions.electron. The role spawn builder injects KELD_APP_LINK and applies configured environment pairs. On macOS/Windows the child environment is the host's, minus removals.
tickets.what_to_build:
This ticket is the single owner of the session-facts payload, its delivery to the Bun role at spawn (beside KELD_APP_LINK, under the KEL-75 role spawn contract), its fail-closed contract and the synchronous app.* getters. X03-T4 consumes the payload and is the sole owner of every process.* observable (argv/defaultApp as one atom, resourcesPath, type, versions); X03-T3 entry (c) owns the (argv, defaultApp) cell. This ticket asserts no process.* value.

Naming and schema: the payload is named distinctly from KEL-96's keld.boot.json 'boot descriptor'. `name` derives from the schema-v1 `name` field. `version`/`productName` do not exist in schema v1, so adding them is a KEL-96/KEL-15 schema change.

Field set: PANEL-P3's pre-ready call list decides it. The minimum comes from verified facts:
- electron-store v11.0.2 reads getPath('userData') and getVersion() synchronously at import;
- electron-log v5.4.4 reads name/getName/getPath('userData'|'logs'|'appData')/getVersion/isPackaged (timing UNKNOWN);
- draw.io reads process.argv/env/platform at module top level and calls getVersion/getPath/getLocale/name after ready.

Values:
- userData under legacy is Electron's documented default (appData + app name), minted by the host, per the F01-A4 resolution. The strict location is F01-T9.
- The facade never reads HOME/APPDATA/XDG.
- The payload carries the raw inputs X03-T4 maps: the user argument vector and the resources path. Whether the host forwards OS user arguments to the role today is UNKNOWN; this ticket makes their presence in the payload a contract, and X03-T4 owns how they appear in process.argv/defaultApp.
- isPackaged is false under keld dev. The true half is unknown until a macOS installed artifact exists (KEL-141 Backlog).

Declared role environment (this ticket is its single owner): app-declared key/value pairs the host applies to the Bun role at spawn, for example the update-disable variable `keld migrate` writes for draw.io per PANEL-D14. X02-T1 maps the key to this ticket, X02-T3 writes the value, and F09-T1 covers the env-present and env-absent boots.
- FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1): the KEL-75 RoleConfig already has an explicit per-key environment setter applied before KELD_APP_LINK is set; production boot uses it only for removals and test variables, and no boot-descriptor field carries an app-declared environment. Delivery reuses that setter; no second environment path is added.
- The contract is an explicit KEL-75 role spawn spec amendment. Because no-flag boot reads only the compiled keld.boot.json (KEL-96-D3), its carrier is a new schema-v1 field consumed by that amendment.
- KEL-75 keeps KELD_APP_LINK as the sole child bootstrap variable, and forbids a capability exception arising from an environment value. Declared keys are default-deny:
- The declared list is a closed set of exact literal names: an uppercase letter followed by uppercase letters, digits or underscores, with no pattern or wildcard. Only names listed in the reviewed artefact are applied (X02-T3, permission-model gate). For the first proof that list is exactly DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE (PANEL-D14). The host hard-codes no app name.
- Beneath that list the host enforces a reserved-name floor that no declaration can override. Any name starting with KELD_ (KEL-75 keeps KELD_APP_LINK as the sole bootstrap variable), BUN_, NODE_, DYLD_ or LD_, or equal in any letter case to HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY or NO_PROXY, is rejected before spawn with a typed KELD-* error naming the key. No role process is created.
- INFERENCE: loader-, runtime- and network-affecting names (NODE_OPTIONS, BUN_OPTIONS, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, the proxy variables) could re-enable preload or install behaviour or redirect traffic, undoing X03-T6's fail-closed guarantee.
- UNKNOWN: the full set of environment names Bun 1.4.2 honours. Before approval, the spec cites Bun's primary documentation for that set and adds to the floor any honoured name outside these prefixes.
- No declared value changes any guard decision or role-policy record. Role behaviour outside keld-guard is proved by the X03-T6 cell, where a spawn with a declared key still fails closed.

tickets.title: feat(app): host single-instance lock verdict — requestSingleInstanceLock/hasSingleInstanceLock read a host-acquired lock with Electron call-time behaviour (first-proof slice)
tickets.current_behavior: FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1): no single-instance concept exists. The facade's app.on accepts any event name, so second-instance/open-file listeners can already be registered but are never emitted. keld-native lists deeplink as a name only.
tickets.what_to_build:
First-proof slice only.

Corpus facts: draw.io calls requestSingleInstanceLock() inside whenReady, after its export, --version and --help paths, and quits when it returns false. Zettlr calls it at top level after handling exit arguments.

The mechanism is determined by evidence. The call returns a boolean synchronously, and Bun cannot block on kipc today (PANEL-P1 open). So the host acquires the OS lock before spawn for an app that declares single-instance, and delivers the verdict in F01-T4's session facts. The loser host still spawns Bun; exiting before spawn would break `drawio --version` and export while a GUI instance runs. The call returns the verdict before and after ready.

Recorded divergence (▲ cell): a declared instance holds the lock from spawn even before it calls (for example a draw.io export-mode instance).

An undeclared call throws a typed KELD-COMPAT error naming the missing declaration and the `keld migrate` fix-it, never a silent true or false.

The declaration reaches the host through the compiled keld.boot.json, because no-flag boot never parses keld.config.ts (KEL-96-D3). That makes it a schema-v1 change. X02-T3 emits the declaration key (that edge is recorded by the X02 owner), and draw.io's activation depends on it.

additionalData is accepted and stored; delivery belongs to F01-T8. The macOS lock primitive is chosen in the spec. Windows/Linux lock identity is UNKNOWN.

tickets.title: feat(app): app.exit(exitCode) as a host-authorized exit Call with a recovery-ownership amendment and exit-code propagation
tickets.current_behavior: FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1): app.exit is absent. The supervisor recovers a nonzero Bun exit with a fresh generation and Ready; an unrequested post-ready status-zero exit surfaces KELD-RUNTIME-012. `keld dev` maps any non-success host status to its own exit 1/2.
tickets.what_to_build:
An approved spec naming the new invariant: an app-requested exit is host-authorized and never recovered. app.exit is a host Call; it is never process.exit.

Electron oracle (FACT, browser.cc and electron_api_app.cc v44.4.5):
- app.exit skips before-quit/will-quit;
- after the message loop is ready, it destroys windows without asking and then emits 'quit' with the exit code;
- before the loop is ready, it exits directly with no 'quit' event.

The exit code must reach the shell under keld dev, which needs a CLI exit-status contract change. KEL-96 §4.5 step 4 'exits' carries no code today.

Corpus: draw.io has 3 sites (export and error paths); Zettlr has 2 (lock loser and startup failure). Not on the first-proof workflow.
tickets.key_interfaces: Lifecycle channel exit Call; supervisor exit classification; KEL-96 §4.5 step 4; keld dev exit-status contract.

app.exit(7) after ready emits no before-quit or will-quit, emits quit with code 7, and the host exits 7 with no successor generation

tickets.title: feat(app): second-instance, open-file and open-url delivery — exactly-once after-ready handoff, pre-ready file/URL queue after will-finish-launching, untrusted argv
tickets.current_behavior: FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1): there is no delivery path. @keld/api connects the app link lazily, only from whenReady() or quit().
tickets.what_to_build:
Delivery:
- At the loser's requestSingleInstanceLock() call, the host notifies the primary with the loser's OS argv, cwd and additionalData.
- The primary receives second-instance strictly after ready, exactly once. Zettlr drops pre-ready second-instance events.
- open-file and open-url are queued from process start and flushed after will-finish-launching and before ready. draw.io registers open-file inside will-finish-launching.
- The facade connects the link on first app.* touch. INFERENCE: KEL-142 AC4 forbids import-time ready, not import-time connect; re-check against the spec text.

Bounds: keld-ipc MAX_FRAME_LEN is 16 MiB, below Electron's 32 MB. An oversized handoff mirrors Electron: the loser gets false and the primary emits nothing. The cap is a keld-ipc owner decision (▲).

Trust (research 186 row 2): every handoff field is untrusted data. OS user-intent sources (Finder open, dock drop) may become host-scoped one-shot read intents through the dialog-grant flow. argv-derived paths never mint authority.

Also covers releaseSingleInstanceLock. Not designed further until scheduled.

An open-file event fired before ready reaches a listener registered inside will-finish-launching
A path taken from second-instance argv cannot be read through the guard unless a dialog or user-intent grant exists
A handoff over the documented cap returns false to the loser, and the primary emits nothing
negative_controls: Delivering second-instance before ready fails the after-ready criterion
Delivering the same handoff twice fails the exactly-once criterion
Minting a read grant from an argv path fails the untrusted-argv criterion

unapplied_findings.finding: critic yagni F01-T3: milestone first-proof for the slice 'host-initiated quit must not bypass the per-window veto'
unapplied_findings.reason: Three sources conflict with it. The first-proof denominator (panel synthesis) ends at a single-window close-with-unsaved-prompt. On macOS, draw.io's window-all-closed listener keeps the app alive without calling app.quit, and the landed electron-lifecycle-v0 cell covers that. The PANEL-D23 packet, which is newer and source-derived, says the first proof does not exercise quit. X06-D2 and X06-D3 semantics corrections park cancelable before-quit/will-quit to the Zettlr tranche. Consistent with that, menu roles split as follows. Role close: F06-T4. Role quit: F06-T16, which consumes F01-T3. In the first proof, F06-T4 records a KELD-COMPAT diagnostic for role quit and never terminates, and the F06-T1 role-quit cell stays expected `unknown` with implementing ticket F06-T16, not a scored first-proof cell (cross-check option (a)). The data-loss risk is real but lies outside the scored cells, so F01-T3 is milestone next and the proof report must record 'Cmd+Q or menu Quit with a dirty window: not scored, unknown'. The slicing part of the finding is applied.

repair.epic_title: compat(window): BrowserWindow over a host window registry — host-minted identity, cancelable close, constructor triage (macOS first proof)
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
32 Electron v44.4.5 entities, 606 raw members. Classes: BaseWindow (187 members), BrowserWindow (204, of which 126 are inherited), View, WebContentsView, BrowserView, ImageView, TouchBar and its 10 item classes. Structures: BaseWindowConstructorOptions (52 fields), BrowserWindowConstructorOptions (2), WebPreferences (46), Point, Rectangle, Size, WindowOpenHandlerResponse, WindowSessionEndEvent, WindowStatePersistence, JumpListCategory, JumpListItem, Task, ThumbarButton, ScrubberItem, SegmentedControlSegment. FACT (the published family model, counts re-checked 2026-10-07).

What exists today. FACT (keld at origin/main 8678c0d1, read 2026-10-07):
- The host creates one primary window per app session, after the authenticated HELLO and before any Bun code runs.
- The macOS loop runs over tao 0.35.3. tao's windowShouldClose: already returns NO and emits CloseRequested. The loop then removes the bridge and the view unconditionally and emits LastWindowClosed when no views remain, so no veto path exists.
- The app-window vocabulary is {NavigationReady, LastWindowClosed} plus {Quit, Fatal}. No window id crosses kipc.
- No backend has chrome options or a hidden-creation option.
- No spec and no Linear issue owns the destination window registry. A search of Linear for "window registry" on 2026-10-07 found none, and the specs index has no registry spec.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, not token-scan leads)
- draw.io main window (FACT, corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb). It is created visible with backgroundColor, width/height/x/y, icon and webPreferences {preload, spellcheck, contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, webviewTag:false, webSecurity:true, disableBlinkFeatures, additionalArguments}. Then:
  - it calls maximize and setFullScreen when the saved state says so;
  - it forwards maximize, unmaximize and resize to the renderer;
  - getFocusedWindow parents dialogs, and getAllWindows is the fallback;
  - the 'close' handler calls preventDefault on every close, sends isModified, records getSize, getPosition, isMaximized and isFullScreen, and later calls destroy();
  - a 'closed' handler does registry bookkeeping;
  - will-navigate, setWindowOpenHandler and will-attach-webview are registered only inside app 'web-contents-created'.
- draw.io and show:false (FACT). draw.io's main window never uses show:false or ready-to-show. ready-to-show appears only in its updater progress bar.
- Zettlr (FACT, grep 2026-10-06/07). It has 14 ready-to-show sites and 15 show:false files, plus hiddenInset, vibrancy, Windows/Linux frame:false + titleBarOverlay and parent/modal windows. That is demand for the next milestone, not the first proof.

## Maturity ladder
- **First proof (draw.io, macOS, explicit legacy profile):** draw.io's window path is green on KEL-74 cells. That path is construction with its option set, the getters and maximize state, the creation events, and cancelable close → destroy → tombstone → closed. Tickets: F02-T6 (spec), F02-T1 (cells), F02-T2, F02-T4, F02-T3.
- **L1:** electron-quick-start runs unmodified on macOS.
- **L2 (next):** Zettlr's macOS window path works: show:false/ready-to-show (F02-T9 after F02-A3), the rest of the registry members (F02-T8), chrome (F02-T5), the full option table (F02-T10), and close under role park and recovery (F02-T11).
- **L3 (parked):** the Windows/Linux lane (F02-T12 after F02-A6).

The published L2 criterion "mirror coherent under a 10k-event stream" is deleted. It had no metric id, census, clock or oracle. If a facade-overhead claim is ever made, it goes through a registered X05-T1 metric.

## Linear owners consumed (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07)
- **Tracker of record (X06-D7, owner decision on GitHub #517, comment 6024917784, 2026-10-06).** Each repo-writing ticket aligns to the nearest live Linear issue whose scope covers it. Otherwise its GitHub issue is the tracker of record: the '## Agent claim' comment (earliest wins), status, handoffs and evidence live there, and no Linear issue is created. A link titled with the GitHub number goes on the nearest live Linear issue, falling back to KEL-127.
  - FACT (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07): no live issue's scope covers F02. KEL-237 (In Progress, unassigned) excludes compatibility-surface expansion. KEL-75 (In Progress, unassigned) is the Bun-role spec. KEL-96's non-goals exclude registry wiring. KEL-25 (In Progress, GYLDLAB) is the hello-world window. So every F02 ticket's tracker of record is its GitHub issue (#448, #449, #450, #455, #456; T6–T12 at publish), and the Linear reference goes on KEL-127 (Todo, unassigned).
  - Residual gap (FACT, the #517 record): root AGENTS.md and the workflow claim protocol still describe Linear-only tracking. Until they are amended through the instruction-change protocol, the #517 record and map #391 are the documented exception these tickets cite. The amendment is a separate owner-authorized change and does not gate F02.
  - Remaining holds unrelated to ownership: the Electron pin for new cells (KEL-237; F02-T1, F02-T7) and the KEL-135 session/partition extension (F02-T10).
- KEL-75 (In Progress, unassigned): its approved spec makes the app-session registry the minter of WindowGeneration. Its T4a window-bound state model landed at 60842b16. T4 (window-bound roles plus a real close) is still open.
- KEL-96 (In Progress, GYLDLAB): the host-created primary window and boot.
- KEL-139 (Done 2026-09-29): an approved spec. F02 consumes AC5 (the same window survives recovery), AC6 (one ordered quit owner) and the T1b rule that nothing may fabricate a native completion. These are constraints, not predecessors.
- KEL-142 (Done): the macOS isolated-world injection seam.
- KEL-143 (Backlog, unassigned): recovery that keeps the same window. It is a named blocker for F02-T11 only.
- KEL-74 (Done, GYLDLAB): the evidence schema.
- KEL-78 (In Progress, GYLDLAB): its approved rule says the Electron sandbox option is not a profile key.
- KEL-135 (In Progress, Amisha Ramani): profile identity. Mapping session/partition needs a KEL-135 extension; no such mapping exists yet.
- KEL-102 (In Progress, unassigned): guard enforcement. Window operations that start from a webview principal stay denied until the per-window grant amendment (decided F04-A1) lands.
- KEL-98 (Done): echo codegen only. Its approved non-goals exclude general contract authoring.
- KEL-64 (Done): F02 reuses only its double-rAF technique; the instrument is an external benchmark beacon.
- KEL-25 (In Progress, GYLDLAB), KEL-27 (Done) and KEL-28 (Backlog, GYLDLAB): per-OS windows.
- Removed: KEL-132 (no F02 ticket consumes GPU/media) and KEL-79 (renderer beforeunload is not part of its secure-origin scope).

## Design facts (labelled)
- **Identity.** DECIDED: the host mints an opaque (WindowId, WindowGeneration). The facade keeps a synchronous mirror that ordered host events update before any user listener runs.
  - FACT (Electron v44.4.5 source, refuter receipt): Electron's getAllWindows order comes from an unordered map, so Keld's creation order is recorded ▲-stronger, never parity.
  - FACT: Electron's getFocusedWindow also returns a window whose DevTools pane is focused. That is ▲ in Keld.
- **Four distinct identities.** Ticket text must not use the bare word "generation":
  - the Bun RoleInstance generation (KEL-75);
  - the WindowGeneration (KEL-75);
  - the navigation generation, whose only minter is the host navigation state and which rotates on commit (decided, F04-A4);
  - the guard webview-principal generation, which is bumped on navigation.
- **Window #1.** Who creates window #1, and what Ready means for each Bun role incarnation, is one atom owned by F01-T2. F02 adds no adoption shim.
- **Close.**
  - FACT (Electron v44.4.5 Cocoa window delegate, PANEL-D5/PANEL-P2 receipts): windowShouldClose: calls NotifyWindowCloseButtonClicked and returns NO. The main process decides the close synchronously. MarkDestroyed runs before Emit('closed').
  - INFERENCE: Keld's asynchronous equivalent keeps the window open with no host timer.
  - DECIDED (PANEL-D19, closed): a close request has exactly three exits: the role's reply; a terminal outcome on generation loss (a recoverable loss keeps the window); or the terminal end of the session (ordered Quit, or no successor role will be provisioned). The host never completes a close on a timer.
  - The tombstone flips before 'closed'. destroy() skips 'close' and guarantees 'closed'.
- **draw.io modified-document branch.**
  - FACT: an unmodified document closes with no dialog.
  - UNKNOWN (PANEL-P1): the modified-document branch needs showMessageBoxSync. If that call throws, draw.io's modal guard never clears and the window can never close. That coupling runs PANEL-P1 → the blocking-CALL transport PANEL-P1 selects → F06-T7 → the X02-T6 scoring run.
  - BLOCKER (coverage gap): no repaired unit owns the implementation ticket for that transport. F02-T11 names it as an external blocker. The map orchestrator mints it in the kipc transport family; X05-T3 is already taken by the parked perf-lane ticket.
- **WebPreferences.**
  - Six escalating values fail at construction, with no quirk, flag or profile opt-in: nodeIntegration, nodeIntegrationInWorker and nodeIntegrationInSubFrames set to true, contextIsolation:false, webSecurity:false, allowRunningInsecureContent:true.
  - Engine-only knobs (enableBlinkFeatures, disableBlinkFeatures, experimentalFeatures, v8CacheOptions, enableWebSQL, plugins, spellcheck) are accepted and ignored with one diagnostic (▲). draw.io sets disableBlinkFeatures on every window, so refusing it would refuse draw.io.
  - sandbox:false is ignored with a diagnostic and never selects a Keld profile (KEL-78).
  - offscreen is ✘.
  - FACT: enableRemoteModule is not a v44.4.5 WebPreferences field.
- **View model.** One BaseWindow implementation: BrowserWindow is BaseWindow plus exactly one host-created content view. Destroying the view together with its window is a Keld ownership choice (▲), not an engine impossibility. The View tree, BrowserView and multiple views are Tier 3 and ✘ until they ship.
- **Hidden paint.** FACT: the KEL-64 beacon is an external benchmark instrument, and the only host injection seam is macOS's KEL-142 world. A ready-to-show reporter is new work on each engine (F02-A3).
- **Popups.** FACT (refuter): with no handler, macOS/Linux popups are dropped implicitly by the engine default rather than denied by Keld. The explicit deny belongs to F03-T4.

## Platform lanes
- **macOS:** the first proof and L2.
- **Windows and Linux:** parked in F02-T12. No Windows/Linux chrome option is Tier 1 without receipts (F02-A6, parked).
  - FACT: WebKit's CSS property registry has no app-region.
  - FACT: WebView2's non-client-region setting starts at SDK 1.0.2420.47; the minimum Runtime is UNKNOWN.
  - FACT: Electron's own docs disagree on whether symbolColor is Windows-only or Windows+Linux.

tickets.what_to_build:
Land KEL-74 cells for the window behaviours the draw.io first proof exercises.

Each cell:
- cites the pinned Electron v44.4.5 API doc sentence it asserts. Where the doc is silent, it cites a labelled v44.4.5 source receipt instead.
- names its ordered observable.
- is recorded in the X01-T3 red-until-implemented representation: expected verdict `fail` with its implementing-ticket key, and a mapped test that asserts today's behaviour and passes; the implementing change inverts the test and flips the cell to `pass`. The implementing tickets are F02-T2, F02-T3 and F02-T4. `unknown` is used only for uncited, observed-only or unrun-lane cells.
- carries the corpus pin set by the X01-T3 pin rule (the v44.4.5 tag commit), and the manifest is validated by the X01-T4 shared owner.
- is never silently red, skipped, ignored or retried.

Cells:
1. `new BrowserWindow(options)` returns an object whose `id` is the id delivered by the host.
2. App 'browser-window-created' and 'web-contents-created' fire exactly once per created window, with the window and its webContents. Ordering against the constructor's return is recorded as unknown until checked against the v44.4.5 source.
3. getAllWindows and getFocusedWindow return synchronously. getAllWindows order is recorded ▲-stronger, because Electron's order is unspecified.
4. isMaximized() is true inside a 'maximize' listener after maximize(). isFullScreen() is true after setFullScreen(true).
5. Constructor triage:
   - draw.io's exact webPreferences set creates a window.
   - Each of the six escalating values refuses construction, and no window is created.
6. 'close' is emitted on a native close request, and preventDefault keeps the window open. The doc's ordering before the DOM beforeunload/unload events is not a cell here: it is cited but has no implementing ticket (renderer beforeunload has 0 corpus demand and no owner), and X01-T3 admits a cited pending cell only with an implementing-ticket key. F02 lists it as not yet specified.
7. destroy() emits no 'close' and guarantees exactly one 'closed'.
8. isDestroyed() is true inside the 'closed' listener (tombstone before closed: PANEL-D6, and MarkDestroyed before Emit('closed') in the v44.4.5 source).
9. Reading a member after destruction throws the exact 'Object has been destroyed' text.
10. A second close() after a vetoed close, or destroy() after a vetoed close, yields 'closed' exactly once.

Windows and Linux cells are recorded explicitly as unknown (unrun).

Moved to F02-T7: ready-to-show, the minimize/restore/focus/blur/move/full-screen event sequences, fromId and fromWebContents.
acceptance_criteria: Every cell names the pinned v44.4.5 doc sentence, or a labelled v44.4.5 source receipt, plus its ordered observable.
The runner asserts every cell's recorded expected status. A cell whose actual outcome differs from its recorded status fails the required gate.
Every cell has one negative control naming the single mutation that makes it fail.
No cell compares wall-clock timing.
The existing lifecycle cells for ready and window-all-closed still pass unchanged.

Every pending cited cell carries expected verdict `fail` with its implementing-ticket key (F02-T2, F02-T3 or F02-T4) and a mapped test that asserts today's behaviour and passes, and the manifest passes the X01-T4 validator.
Every cell's oracle revision equals the corpus pin set by the X01-T3 pin rule (the v44.4.5 tag commit).
negative_controls: Emitting 'closed' before the tombstone flips fails cell 8.
Emitting 'close' from destroy() fails cell 7.
Updating the isMaximized mirror after the 'maximize' listener runs fails cell 4.
Marking an expected-fail cell as skipped or ignored fails the runner's expected-status assertion.
Removing a pending cell's implementing-ticket key makes the X01-T4 validator reject the manifest.
Changing one cell's oracle revision to the 44.3.0 commit fails the X01-T4 pin-consistency check.

Make the host window registry live on macOS for windows the facade creates, as the F02-T6 spec defines it.

@keld/api mirror primitive. F02-T2 owns its single implementation; F06-T5 reuses it for the display and theme mirrors.

- `new BrowserWindow(options)` creates a host window.

- App 'browser-window-created' and 'web-contents-created' are emitted once per window. That makes reachable the will-navigate, setWindowOpenHandler and will-attach-webview registrations owned by F03-T3, F03-T4 and F07-T2.

tickets.title: feat(window): macOS two-phase cancelable close — host holds tao's CloseRequested, facade close/preventDefault, destroy, tombstone-before-closed, three exits and no host timer
tickets.current_behavior: tao 0.35.3's windowShouldClose: returns NO and emits CloseRequested. On that event the macOS loop destroys the bridge and removes the view unconditionally, then emits LastWindowClosed. Close cannot be cancelled. The gap is host policy, not a missing AppKit hook.
tickets.what_to_build:
Implement the close state machine from the F02-T6 spec on macOS, checked against the PANEL-P2 Electron transcript.

The flow:
1. On tao's CloseRequested the host keeps the view and emits CloseRequested{WindowId, WindowGeneration, seq}.
2. The facade emits 'close' synchronously.
3. The reply, allow or veto, carries the seq.
4. On allow, the host runs page unload, destroys the view before the window, and emits destroyed.
5. The facade flips the tombstone, then emits 'closed'.

Rules:
- destroy() skips 'close' and guarantees 'closed'.
- Every native close attempt re-emits 'close'; draw.io keys each attempt with a fresh id. Replies are matched by seq, and a stale seq is ignored with a diagnostic.
- Exits, per decided PANEL-D19:
  - the role's reply;
  - a terminal outcome on generation loss: the pending request gets exactly one terminal outcome and is never replayed to a successor role;
  - the terminal end of the session: ordered Quit, or no successor role will be provisioned.
- The host never completes a close on a timer.
- A throwing 'close' listener still produces exactly one reply for its seq, plus one diagnostic. Whether Electron parity means allow or veto is UNKNOWN until an Electron 44.4.5 observation exists. It is recorded as an explicit unknown cell.
- After the last window is destroyed, the existing LastWindowClosed → window-all-closed path applies unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: The F02-T1 close, destroy, tombstone and closed cells flip from their recorded expected status to pass in this change.

Unmodified document: the close button produces 'close' with preventDefault, then a renderer isModified round trip, then destroy(). The result is exactly one 'closed', and the host's native window count reaches zero.
Vetoed close: after preventDefault the window stays open while the fixture advances an injected, controllable clock arbitrarily far. It closes only when the app calls destroy(). No sleep is used.
isDestroyed() is true inside the 'closed' listener, and a later getSize() throws 'Object has been destroyed'.
close() called twice yields one 'closed'. destroy() after a vetoed close emits exactly one 'closed' and no 'close'.
A throwing 'close' listener produces exactly one reply for that seq and exactly one diagnostic.
Killing the Bun role while a close is pending: the request is never delivered to any successor role, and the window closes only through the session's terminal path.
The existing KEL-237 window-all-closed policy cell still passes.
negative_controls: Any host-side completion of a pending close driven by a timer fails the vetoed-close criterion once the injected clock advances past the timer's bound.
Removing the view on CloseRequested before the reply, as today, fails the vetoed-close criterion.
Emitting 'closed' before the tombstone flips fails the isDestroyed-inside-'closed' criterion.
Accepting a reply that does not carry the current seq, so a stale allow from an earlier attempt closes the window, fails the stale-seq cell.
Replaying the pending CloseRequested to a successor role fails the role-death criterion.

tickets.title: spec(window): first-proof window registry, window wire contract, two-phase close state machine and constructor-option triage (macOS)
tickets.current_behavior: No spec owns the destination window registry or the close protocol. The KEL-75 approved spec defines WindowGeneration but nothing implements it. KEL-98's approved non-goals exclude general contract authoring.
tickets.what_to_build:
Write one spec under the repository spec template, covering only what F02-T2, F02-T3 and F02-T4 need for draw.io on macOS.

(a) Identity.
- The host mints an opaque WindowId plus WindowGeneration per window incarnation, consistent with KEL-75's approved spec (the app-session registry owns the counter; a window is never identified by a native window number) and its frozen T4a model.
- The spec names the three other identities and forbids the bare word 'generation': the Bun RoleInstance generation; the navigation generation, whose only minter is host navigation state and which rotates on commit (decided, F04-A4); and the guard webview-principal generation.

(b) Wire.
- Window-state events and commands on the app link, with a channel id allocated by X05-T2's rule.
- Record the contract-authoring owner. The options are: extend the existing thin lifecycle codec adapters over the KEL-136 shared transport (INFERENCE: the reuse path, recommended); amend KEL-98; or wait for the separately specified schema generator.

(c) Window #1. Consume F01-T2's rule for who creates window #1 and what Ready means for each role incarnation. No adoption shim.

(d) Mirror primitive. The ordering contract (host event before user listener), zero traffic per read, and the staleness contract for a blocked role. F02 owns it; F06-T5 consumes it.

(e) Close state machine.
- CloseRequested{WindowId, WindowGeneration, seq} → 'close' → a reply carrying the seq → unload → view destroyed before window → destroyed → tombstone → 'closed'.
- The three PANEL-D19 exits. No host timer.
- Re-emission on every native attempt.

(f) Triage. Constructor triage for draw.io's field set and the six escalating values, with no quirk opt-in.

(g) Guard. In the first proof, window operations come only from the app-process principal. Webview-originated window operations stay denied until KEL-102's per-window grant amendment (decided F04-A1).

(h) Drift. Name the change that corrects the core crate's registry ownership claim.

Rejected alternatives to record: a per-read synchronous RPC, ids minted by the facade, and a host close timer.
acceptance_criteria: The spec is approved under the repository spec template, with sections (a) through (h) and the three rejected alternatives recorded.
Every section has at least one binary acceptance criterion paired with a named negative control.
The spec text contains no use of the word 'generation' that is not one of the four qualified names.
The spec names the chosen contract-authoring owner and records the rejected options.
negative_controls: A draft that lets the facade mint WindowId fails approval against section (a)'s host-is-sole-minter criterion.
A draft that adds any host timer to the close state machine fails section (e) against PANEL-D19.
A draft that admits a quirk accepting an escalating value fails section (f).

Closing the window on role loss when a successor will be provisioned fails the recovery criterion.

repair.epic_title: compat(webContents): navigation events, guard-first navigation policy, window-open handler, executeJavaScript (consuming the F04-T11 endpoint value codec); devtools/print mapping
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
FACT (Electron v44.4.5 API model): 34 entities / 381 members; `WebContents` alone carries 195. Entities: WebContents, webContents (module), WebFrameMain, webFrameMain (module), webFrame (renderer), NavigationHistory, Debugger, sharedTexture, plus 26 structures (ColorSpace, InputEvent, KeyboardInputEvent, MouseInputEvent, MouseWheelInputEvent, NavigationEntry, OffscreenSharedTexture, PostBody, PreloadScript, PreloadScriptRegistration, PrintToPDFMargins, PrintToPDFOptions, PrinterInfo, Referrer, RenderProcessGoneDetails, the seven SharedTexture* structures, UploadData, UploadFile, UploadRawData, WebSource). Each entity is either covered by a ticket below or listed in never / out-of-scope (with its owning key) / not-yet-specified.

FACT (Keld origin/main, read 2026-10-07): there is no webContents facade. The keld-wv `WebEngine` trait offers create, navigate, eval (fire-and-forget; the module doc defers the completion callback to the keld-core command-queue design), bounds, devtools, destroy. The only navigation observable is the host page-load-finished event. keld-wv wires only the page-load handler on the pinned wry 0.56.1. Two wry defaults matter on WKWebView. With no navigation handler, every navigation is allowed (FACT, wry 0.56.1 source). With no new-window handler, no web view is returned, so every window.open is denied (FACT, same source). The KEL-142 macOS bridge (landed 9e43edc9) has one per-WebView navigation generation. It rotates when the host navigates and when wry reports the WK commit callback.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, static read of drawio-desktop@2edf9fb and zettlr@e6c7fd8)
- FACT, draw.io activation path: the main window loads a file:// index with `loadURL`. Its `did-finish-load` listener sets `zoomFactor` and calls `setVisualZoomLevelLimits(1, appZoom)` before it counts the load. `appZoom` defaults to 1. That count is one of the two events the app waits for before it sends `args-obj`. A missing zoom member therefore throws inside the listener and activation never completes.
- FACT, draw.io: `executeJavaScript` is awaited at three main-process sites. Two are one-shot localStorage migrations at did-finish-load (result: string or null). One collects config-readable paths (result: array of strings), and the read-path gate awaits it on file open. `destroyed` and `did-navigate` listeners drop file watches. `before-input-event` with `pasteAndMatchStyle` intercepts Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V. `openDevTools` runs only under `__DEV__` or on an `openDevTools` ipc message.
- FACT, draw.io: `will-navigate` (an unconditional preventDefault) and `setWindowOpenHandler` (allow `about:blank` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions`, otherwise call `openExternal` and return deny or undefined) are registered only inside `app.on('web-contents-created')`. F02-T2 owns emitting that event.
- FACT, draw.io: the export path uses a window with `webPreferences.offscreen: {deviceScaleFactor: 2}`, `capturePage`, `print` and `printToPDF`. None of these is on open/edit/save/close.
- FACT: draw.io has 13 `webContents.send` sites. F04-T3 owns send. Zettlr's `window.print()` runs in the renderer. Zettlr calls `toggleDevTools`, `inspectElement`, `startDrag` and `console-message`. Zettlr's `unresponsive` is the BrowserWindow event.
- FACT: electron-quick-start's `openDevTools` line is commented out. The matrix count for it is scanner noise, and so are its `WebContents.replace` and `WebContents.focus` rows, which are String/DOM hits.
- FACT: draw.io and Zettlr have zero sites for NavigationHistory, Debugger, sharedTexture, WebFrameMain frame-tree APIs, registerPreloadScript, renderer webFrame, or webContents static lookups.

## First-proof slice (drawio-desktop, macOS, explicit legacy profile)
F03-T1 (conformance entries) → F03-T2 (facade: id, loadURL(file://), did-finish-load, did-navigate, destroyed, registration-safe members) → F03-T5 (executeJavaScript). F03-T5 also consumes F04-T11, the single endpoint value codec owned by F04. Everything else is next or parked.
- Falsifier for this split: the PANEL-P3 boot/authority trace showing a page-initiated cross-document navigation, a window.open, or a before-input-event dependency on the four workflow steps. If it does, the matching next ticket (F03-T3, F03-T4 or the not-yet-specified input hook) moves to first-proof.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: the webContents facade exists with typed errors; registration of every corpus-registered listener and handler does not throw; never rows are published.
- L1 (first proof): F03-T1 cells pass at their declared expected status for draw.io activation on macOS (did-finish-load, did-navigate, destroyed, id, zoom members, executeJavaScript JSON-domain results).
- L2: the ordered navigation vocabulary (F03-T8), guard ∧ app navigation policy (F03-T3) and the window-open handler (F03-T4) pass the F03-T6 cells on macOS.
- L3: Windows/Linux lanes (F03-T9, parked) and devtools mapping (F03-T10).

## Linear owners and tracker of record (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07)
- FACT (GitHub #517, CLOSED; owner decision comment 6024917784 by the repository owner, 2026-10-06): X06-D7 adopted option D and explicitly superseded the packet's earlier option C recommendation. Rule: align each repo-writing ticket to the nearest live Linear issue whose scope covers it, and claim there per the workflow. Otherwise the GitHub issue is the tracker of record (the `## Agent claim` comment, status, handoffs and evidence live on GitHub, earliest claim comment wins), and no Linear issue is created. The nearest live Linear issue for the surface carries a reference link to every GitHub ticket, falling back to KEL-127.
- Residual gap (FACT, same comment): root AGENTS.md and the agent workflow still describe Linear-only claims. Until they are amended through the instruction-change protocol, which the owner calls a separate, owner-authorized change, the #517 record and map #391 are the documented exception. Every GitHub-tracked F03 ticket cites that exception.
- KEL-79 is Backlog and unassigned ("Webview: secure-origin and resource-transport contract across system engines"). It carries the acceptance bullet "navigation/popup/download/permission policy are explicit". INFERENCE: that bullet covers F03-T3 and F03-T4, so KEL-79 is their tracker of record under X06-D7 rule 1.
- KEL-102 is In Progress and unassigned. It owns guard vocabulary, including the `web.navigate` and `web.devtools` keys and the F04-A1/F04-A4 amendment.
- KEL-127 (program parent) is Todo and unassigned. It is the fallback holder of reference links for GitHub-tracked F03 tickets: F03-T1, F03-T2, F03-T5, F03-T6, F03-T8 and F03-T10. UNKNOWN: whether those per-ticket links exist yet. The orchestrator is the single Linear writer and confirms or posts them.
- KEL-142 is Done (2026-10-01). Its bridge landed at 9e43edc9 and is consumed, not modified.
- KEL-74 is Done (2026-08-19). It owns the evidence schema, landed at 8ff4cd61.
- KEL-237 is In Progress. Its non-goals exclude new Electron API and compatibility-surface expansion, so it does not cover F03 cells.
- KEL-168 is Done (2026-09-08). It installed WebView2 deny-all popups and is consumed by the parked Windows lane.
- KEL-75 is In Progress and is consumed through F02-T2. KEL-143 is Backlog and owned by F08.
- KEL-80 (Backlog) and KEL-132 / KEL-135 (In Progress) are not consumed by any F03 ticket. send and the value codec belong to F04 (F04-T3, F04-T11); session belongs to F05-T5.

## Design facts
- DECIDED (F04-A4, closed): the existing per-WebView host navigation state in the KEL-142 bridge is the single navigation-generation mint. It rotates on cross-document commit and on a host-initiated load request. It never rotates on a same-document navigation. KEL-102 carries the contract text. F04-T1 owns the generation conformance entries. F03 consumes this "navigation generation", which is distinct from WindowGeneration (F02-T2) and from Bun role generation (KEL-75). Tickets never use the bare word generation. The rotation rule follows arch 02 §7.
- FACT: wry 0.56.1 on WK reports `didCommitNavigation` as its page-load "Started" event and `didFinishNavigation` as "Finished".
- FACT: arch 04 §3 layer 4 assigns webContents routing identity to keld-compat (host side). keld-wv delivers only engine-neutral signals. Electron event names and their order are synthesised once, in keld-compat or @keld/electron, keyed by (WebviewId, navigation generation).
- FACT (pinned web-contents.md, sha256 449abadd…, retrieved 2026-10-07): "This event will not emit when the navigation is started programmatically with APIs like `webContents.loadURL`". Electron also documents that an unrecognised setWindowOpenHandler return "will result in a console error and have the same effect as returning `{action: 'deny'}`".
- DECIDED here: navigation policy is guard-first and the app hook can only deny. The app hook runs for every page-initiated cross-document navigation, and the outcome is guard ∧ app. Missing hook ⇒ guard decision stands. `web.navigate` is a new key in the existing per-window `web` block. It is evaluated by the existing arch 03 §2 URL-scope matcher and needs a KEL-102 amendment and the permission-model gate.
- DECIDED here (invariant finding): there is no `windowOpenHandler` quirk. Without a handler the outcome is deny with a diagnostic, recorded as a ▲ against Electron's allow-by-default. Arch 04 §3 layer 5's example is amended in F03-T4.
- DECIDED (F03-D4, closed): the value codec is one TypeScript endpoint codec owned by @keld/electron under keld-compat rules, and the host carries it as opaque bytes. v0 domain: JSON plus undefined, Date, Error and class instances flattened to own enumerable properties with the prototype dropped. Functions/Promises/Symbols/WeakMaps/WeakSets throw. Map/Set/RegExp/TypedArray/Buffer throw a typed KELD-COMPAT error. One owner per atom: F04-T11 implements the codec and its golden vectors, F04-T6 owns the arch 02 §5 "opaque to the host" amendment, and F03-T5 only uses the codec for its executeJavaScript result envelope.
- DECIDED (PANEL-D21, closed, measured world-probe): on macOS the preload and the renderer compat runtime run in a separate named app content world with their own world-scoped handler. F07-T1 owns it. App-supplied executeJavaScript code runs in the page world, never in the bridge world.
- INFERENCE (F03-D6 packet): arch 03 §4.3 already determines devtools: they are dev-only, and a release build without the grant gets a diagnosed no-op. On macOS release, opening the inspector window needs SPI, so a grant can do no more than set isInspectable. Print stays experiment-gated and outside the first proof. F03-D6 is still open.
- KNOWN GAP (FACT + owner): until F03-T3 lands, macOS page-initiated navigations follow wry's allow-all default, so draw.io's will-navigate veto is registered but not honoured. This gap predates F03 and F03 does not widen it. KEL-79/F03-T3 own it, and the first-proof scoreboard records the row with expected status fail. No F03 member may report a veto it did not perform.

## Platform lanes
macOS (WKWebView) is the only first-proof lane. Windows (WebView2) and Linux (WebKitGTK) cells are recorded with expected status unknown, never omitted. F03-T9 (parked) owns them. Known engine facts there: WebView2 ExecuteScript collapses undefined/throw to null (Microsoft receipt via refuter, not re-fetched), and WebView2 already denies all popups (KEL-168).

tickets.what_to_build:
Land KEL-74 cells that cite the pinned Electron v44.4.5 web-contents.md sentence (receipt digest recorded). Each pending cell is recorded in the X01-T3 red-until-implemented representation: expected verdict `fail` with its implementing-ticket key, and a mapped test that asserts today's behaviour and passes; the implementing change inverts the test and flips the cell to `pass` in its own change. `unknown` is used only for uncited, observed-only or unrun-lane cells. The manifest carries the corpus pin set by the X01-T3 pin rule and is validated by the X01-T4 shared owner. A silently red, skipped or retried test is not allowed. Cells (macOS lane, authority_profile LegacySandboxOff; Windows/Linux cells recorded as unknown):
(1) did-finish-load: 'Emitted when the navigation is done, i.e. the spinner of the tab has stopped spinning, and the onload event was dispatched.' The listener fires exactly once per top-level file:// load, and inside it `executeJavaScript('document.readyState')` resolves 'complete'. This sub-cell depends on cell 6 and says so.
(2) loadURL: 'the promise will resolve when the page has finished loading (see did-finish-load)'. The Promise resolves after the did-finish-load listener ran.
(3) did-navigate: 'Emitted when a main frame navigation is done.' plus 'not emitted for in-page navigations, such as ... updating the window.location.hash'. One emission per cross-document main-frame load, zero for a hash change.
(4) destroyed: 'Emitted when webContents is destroyed.' One emission on window destroy, and isDestroyed() is true afterwards.
(5) webContents.id: 'Each ID is unique among all WebContents instances'. Two windows have distinct ids.
(6) executeJavaScript: 'resolves with the result of the executed code or is rejected if the result of the code is a rejected promise'. Covers `1+1`, an array of strings, string-or-null shapes like draw.io's localStorage reads, and a rejected-promise result.
(7) zoomFactor set/get and setVisualZoomLevelLimits(1, 1) ('Returns Promise<void>') do not throw. Keld's engine-applied behaviour is declared ▲ with expected status fail.
(8) Registering will-navigate, will-frame-navigate, before-input-event and setWindowOpenHandler does not throw. Their behaviour cells are expected `fail` keyed to F03-T3 (will-navigate, will-frame-navigate) and F03-T4 (setWindowOpenHandler). before-input-event's behaviour is the declared ▲ row (accepted, never emitted) that F03-T2 records, with its intentional divergence and no implementing key.
All other webContents cells live in F03-T6. render-process-gone cells (webContents and app) belong to F08-T3, and F08-T1 implements them.

Cell 6 asserts equality of the resolved value for the three draw.io-shaped results and a rejection for a rejected-promise result

Windows and Linux cells exist with expected status unknown
Every pending cited cell carries expected verdict `fail` with its implementing-ticket key and a mapped test that asserts today's behaviour and passes, and the manifest passes the X01-T4 validator

tickets.title: feat(webContents): first-proof macOS webContents facade — host-minted id, loadURL(file://), did-finish-load, did-navigate on commit, destroyed, registration-safe members
tickets.what_to_build:
macOS only. For each BrowserWindow, expose a webContents facade object.
- id: the host-minted WebviewId carried by the F02-T2 registry. This ticket does not mint it.
- loadURL(file:// URL): issues the existing host navigation. File:// containment is F05-T4. Returns a Promise that resolves when did-finish-load is emitted.
- did-finish-load: synthesised from the existing host page-load-finished observable.
- did-navigate: synthesised from the cross-document commit signal. FACT: wry 0.56.1 reports WK didCommitNavigation as its page-load Started event. Keyed by (WebviewId, navigation generation) from the single mint decided in F04-A4.
- destroyed: emitted once when the host destroys the webview; isDestroyed() becomes true and later calls throw the typed destroyed-object error.
Electron names are synthesised in keld-compat / @keld/electron, never in keld-wv. This slice adds no WebEngine trait method.

Registration-safe members, each with a recorded ▲ scoreboard row:
- zoomFactor: stores and returns the value (default 1.0). A value other than 1.0 is not applied and logs one diagnostic.
- setVisualZoomLevelLimits: returns a resolved Promise and is not applied. INFERENCE: (1,1) equals the WK default of no magnification; F03-T1 cell 7 records it.
- on('before-input-event'): accepted, never emitted. pasteAndMatchStyle throws a typed KELD-COMPAT unsupported error.
- on('will-navigate') and on('will-frame-navigate'): accepted, not invoked until F03-T3.
- on('will-attach-webview'): accepted and never emitted, because Keld defines no <webview>. Its never-emitted contract is F07-T2's, and its conformance entry is F07-T4's. It has no ▲ row here.
- setWindowOpenHandler: stores the handler, not invoked until F03-T4. The WK backend installs no new-window handler, so window.open returns null and no window is created.

Adjacent atoms and their owners: web-contents-created / browser-window-created emission → F02-T2; webContents.send, ipc-message and senderFrame → F04-T3; render-process-gone → F08-T1; webContents.session → F05-T5; preload world → F07-T1; navigation-generation conformance → F04-T1.

tickets.title: feat(webContents): guard-first navigation policy with deny-only will-navigate/will-frame-navigate hooks invoked for every page-initiated navigation (outcome = guard ∧ app)
tickets.what_to_build:
macOS first. Before engine commit (WK decidePolicyFor, reachable through the pinned wry navigation handler, FACT), evaluate every page-initiated top-level and frame navigation against `windows.<name>.web.navigate`.
- The key is new inside the existing per-window `web` block. It is evaluated by the existing arch 03 §2 URL-scope matcher: no second grammar and no any-host glob. App bundle resources are implicit; remote origins must be named.
- Invoke the app's will-navigate / will-frame-navigate hook for EVERY page-initiated cross-document navigation, so side effects such as Zettlr's openExternal survive.
- Compute the guard decision independently and apply guard ∧ app. With no hook, the guard decision stands. A hook can only deny.
- Emit the KELD-GUARD diagnostic only when the guard denied something the app did not.
- Host loadURL skips the hook but not the guard. Same-document navigations never reach the hook. did-redirect-navigation and will-redirect: the guard evaluates the redirect target.

tickets.title: feat(webContents): executeJavaScript on macOS with a completion-backed result envelope encoded by the F04-T11 endpoint codec
tickets.what_to_build:
Extend the engine eval path with a completion result on the macOS backend. WK evaluateJavaScript completes 'with either the result of the script evaluation or an error' (Apple receipt via refuter). This is a design-reviewed WebEngine change landing with its live backend. The callback plumbing follows the keld-core command-queue owner.
- App code is wrapped in one host-owned async envelope that produces {ok, value} or {ok:false, name, message, stack}. The F04-T11 codec encodes and decodes it. F04-T11 owns the codec module, its golden vectors and its type domain, and F04-T6 owns the arch 02 §5 amendment. This ticket owns only the envelope shape and its Promise mapping, and adds no second encoder.
- App code runs in the page world: never the KEL-142 bridge world, never the PANEL-D21 app world.
- Calls made while the page is loading wait until load completes ('Code execution will be suspended until web page stop loading'). Pending calls per view are bounded, and overflow rejects with a typed KELD code.
- A cross-document commit (new navigation generation) before completion rejects with a typed stale-navigation error.
- A result above the size bound set in the spec rejects with a typed error that names the limit.
acceptance_criteria: F03-T1 cell 6 flips to pass at the same commit

With the pending bound reached on a page that never finishes loading, the next call rejects with the typed overflow code
A result above the spec bound rejects with a typed error naming the limit
executeJavaScript of a probe for the bridge's message-handler name resolves 'undefined'
A result containing a Map rejects with the F04-T11 typed KELD-COMPAT unsupported-type error

Resolving a rejected-promise result fails the rejection criterion

Removing the pending bound fails the overflow criterion
Evaluating in the bridge world makes the probe resolve 'object'
Converting a Map to a plain object fails the unsupported-type criterion

repair.epic_title: compat(ipc): ipcMain/ipcRenderer/contextBridge over host-routed el:<channel> frames, exact-literal per-window guard grants and a lifted renderer floor (draw.io send/on path first)
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
15 entities / 77 members of the Electron v44.4.5 API model: `contextBridge` (3), `ipcMain` (9), `ipcRenderer` (11), `IpcMainEvent` (8), `IpcMainInvokeEvent` (5), `IpcRendererEvent` (2), `webUtils` (1), `MessageChannelMain` (2), `MessagePortMain` (5), `parentPort` (2), `utilityProcess` (1), `UtilityProcess` (10), `IpcMainServiceWorker` (7), `IpcMainServiceWorkerEvent` (7), `IpcMainServiceWorkerInvokeEvent` (4). Two members of other families are consumed here as narrow subsets only: `webContents.send` (routing to one webview principal; the WebContents entity stays with F03) and `WebFrameMain.url` / `WebFrameMain.origin` as reached through `event.senderFrame` (the rest of WebFrameMain stays with F03).

Live today (FACT, Keld origin/main 8678c0d1, read 2026-10-07): one macOS page-world `window.keld.invoke` (channel 1 only, 4096-byte payload, one pending invoke per WebView, host-minted correlation, isolated-world relay, KELD-WV-011 fail-closed); the renderer-bridge endpoint types live in keld-wv and are driven by a keld-core polling pump that admits one application call at a time; `@keld/api` has one echo channel handler; `@keld/electron` ships app lifecycle only (no ipcMain, no preload injection, no renderer shim); keld-guard's `evaluate` denies every non-AppProcess principal (KELD-GUARD006) before any grant lookup, the manifest loader ignores the top-level `windows` key, and `DenyReason::ChannelForbidden` (KELD-GUARD003) exists but is never returned; the Unix virtual-port registry (64-message queue, 4 KiB inline, one-shot transfer) has no renderer route.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb, zettlr@e6c7fd8; literal grep 2026-10-07)
- draw.io (first proof): preload uses `ipcRenderer.send` / `on` / `once` and `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` twice (`electron` = {request, registerMsgListener, sendMessage, listenOnce}, all void-returning, page callbacks passed as arguments including one nested in an object; `process` = {type, versions}); main registers 27 `ipcMain` listeners on 25 distinct string literals (`rendererReq` multiplexer replying `mainResp` via `event.reply`, including an Error instance on the failure path), uses `ipcMain.once` and `ipcMain.removeListener` on the close path (isModified → isModified-result → saveAndClose / saveAndClose-result, removeDraft / draftRemoved), 9 `webContents.send(` sites, and checks `event.senderFrame` (null → reject, else `url` prefix match against the file:// code URL) before acting. 0 invoke, 0 handle, 0 sendSync. Open and save carry file contents through `rendererReq` / `mainResp`.
- Zettlr (next milestone): 186 `ipcRenderer.invoke(` sites, 25 `ipcMain.handle(` sites by literal grep (another scan counted 26 — unpinned), 6 `sendSync(` sites behind synchronously-returning exposed functions, `event.sender` used as a WebContents handle, `webUtils.getPathForFile`, `ipcRenderer.setMaxListeners(100)`, exposed functions that return functions.
- Zero demand in all three corpus apps for MessageChannelMain, MessagePortMain, ipcRenderer.postMessage, utilityProcess, parentPort, IpcMainServiceWorker, exposeInIsolatedWorld, executeInMainWorld (refuter grep). Matrix token-scan counts (e.g. `MessagePortMain.close` 14/82) are token collisions, not demand.

## Maturity ladder and pull order
- first-proof (draw.io, macOS, explicit legacy profile): X01-T3/X01-T4 → F04-T1 conformance → F04-T6/F04-T7 specs → F04-T8 grants, F04-T9 navigation-generation mint, F04-T11 codec (sole codec owner; F03-T5 consumes it), F04-T2 send, F04-T10 on → F04-T12 payload bound → F04-T3 ipcMain facade → F04-T4 contextBridge/ipcRenderer facade (after F07-T1). Conditional on PANEL-P1 passing an arm: F04-T19 transport spec → F04-T18 blocking host CALL transport (consumed by F06-T7 for draw.io's close prompt).
- next: F04-T20 recorded-oracle comparison of observed-only entries (after X01-T1); Zettlr: F04-T13 N pending invokes, F04-T14 invoke/handle, F04-T15 sendSync scaffold, F04-T16 cross-world returns, F04-T17 webUtils.getPathForFile.
- parked: F04-T5 deferred/never rows.
- L0 rows honest; L1 draw.io send/on/reply path on macOS; L2 pinned cells pass; L3 corpus workflow under `keld dev` with overhead only through registered X05 metric ids (no unregistered performance sentence, per PANEL-D11).

## Linear owners consumed (live status, Linear, fetched 2026-10-07)
- KEL-102 — In Progress, unassigned: owns the webview-principal channel-grant task unit and the navigation-generation contract (F04-A1 / F04-A4 decided). Consumed artifact: KEL-102/T3 terminal artifact comment cde25f5e (landed 66ccbbc), the live `dispatch_privileged` route.
- KEL-142 — Done 2026-10-01: the landed renderer bridge seam (wv-link v1 envelope, document nonce, content-world isolation tests). No open Linear issue owns its revision.
- KEL-80 — Backlog, unassigned. ASSUMPTION: intended owner of renderer floor v2. Its 2026-09-26 product-spine slice comment (54a36489) admits only bounded semantics for one renderer call; its 2026-08-20 owner comment says "do not pick up". No task-level artifact exists for floor v2.
- KEL-74 — Done: evidence schema owner. KEL-237 — In Progress: lifecycle corpus; its non-goals exclude "compatibility-surface expansion", so it does NOT own F04 conformance entries.
- KEL-75 — In Progress: utilityProcess / MessagePortMain facade (spec T4/T5 unstarted, AC7 pinned-oracle first).
- KEL-136 — Done (generated app-link transport); KEL-98 — Done (echo-only codegen; scope amendment needed before it generates el control structs); KEL-58 — Done (MCP explain fails closed on `channel`); KEL-79 — Backlog (renderer origin / resource transport; consumed only through F05-T4 for the file:// origin draw.io's `validateSender` needs); KEL-127 — Todo (program parent; entry-reading packet X06-D1 governs when repo-landing facade work may start).
- Tracker of record (FACT, gyldlab/keld#517 owner-decision comment IC_kwDOSwkPJ88AAAABZxzzGA, 2026-10-06T20:32Z, read 2026-10-07): option D is adopted. A repo-writing ticket aligned to a live Linear issue whose scope covers it claims there (F04-T7/T8/T9 → KEL-102; F04-T5 deferred rows → KEL-75). Every other F04 ticket is tracked on its own GitHub issue, with no new Linear issue, and is referenced by a link on KEL-80 (bridge, transport, conformance, specs) or KEL-127 (facade, codec). Remaining precondition per ticket: that reference link exists (orchestrator posts it). Residual gap the owner record names: root AGENTS.md and the workflow still describe Linear-only claims until an `.agents/instructions.md` amendment lands; agents cite the #517 record as the documented exception. KEL-80 (Backlog, unassigned) and KEL-97 (Backlog, unassigned) re-fetched 2026-10-07.

## Design facts (labelled)
- FACT (decided F04-A1, delegated): renderer→main authorization = exact-literal `el:<channel>` entries under `windows.<w>.channels`, KELD-GUARD003 on miss, evaluated only in `dispatch_privileged`; `keld migrate` refuses wildcards. Exact-content approval of the KEL-102 amendment is a separate owner step (F04-T7).
- FACT (decided F04-A4): the existing per-WebView host navigation state is the single mint of the navigation generation; the guard webview principal is built from the generation stamped on the admitted request; rotation at cross-document commit, plus host-initiated load as earlier fail-closed invalidation, never on same-document navigation; u32 with checked increment. FACT (code): two counters exist today (bridge u64 rotating on commit-observed page-load start and on host navigate; guard principal u32 minted as 0).
- FACT (decided F03-D4): the value codec is a host-opaque endpoint codec owned by `@keld/electron`, implemented once by F04-T11 (F03-T7 is a duplicate for F03 to supersede); v0 domain = JSON + undefined, Date, Error (name/message/stack), class instances flattened; Function/Promise/Symbol/WeakMap/WeakSet throw as Electron; Map/Set/RegExp/TypedArray/bulk refs throw typed KELD-COMPAT. Arch 02 §5's "postcard-encoded SCV" sentence must be amended in the F04 ipc spec PR (F04-T6 is the single amendment owner).
- FACT (decided PANEL-D21, option A): the app preload and renderer compat runtime run in a named content world separate from the KEL-142 bridge world, with a world-scoped handler that accepts only compat envelopes (F07-T1 owns world placement and the isolation re-run).
- FACT (design, research + refuters): carriage = one fixed generated kipc control channel per direction; Electron channel string, kind and codec bytes are payload fields; no runtime-minted channel ids. Arch 02 §2 "string names never travel per-call" must be amended explicitly (F04-T6).
- FACT (pinned doc, ipc-main-event.md v44.4.5): `senderFrame` "May be null if accessed after the frame has either navigated or been destroyed"; `reply` "will send an IPC message to the renderer frame that sent the original message".
- INFERENCE (source receipts by a refuter, not doc text): a reply after the frame is gone is dropped (`sendToFrame` returns false); a reply with unserializable args throws; replies survive same-document navigation because Electron keys on the frame host. Recorded in F04-T1 as uncited cells with expected status unknown (X01-T3 rule); compared with a recorded oracle in F04-T20 (next).
- INFERENCE (no v44.4.5 doc sentence found): per-channel FIFO of `ipcRenderer.send`; unknown cell in F04-T1, BEHAVIOR_MATCH-capped oracle comparison in F04-T20.
- FACT (pinned doc, ipc-renderer-event.md): `IpcRendererEvent.sender` is the IpcRenderer instance, `ports` the transferred MessagePorts.
- FACT (decided PANEL-D8): sendSync stays a deadline-bounded blocking CALL in the contract and is SCAFFOLDED (typed throw, fix-it to invoke) until the F04-A5 experiment passes; draw.io has 0 sites. Main-side blocking: the showMessageBoxSync facade is F06-T7; the worker-owned blocking host CALL transport it needs is F04-T18 (spec F04-T19), both gated on PANEL-P1. FACT (park-probe receipt, not re-run): a parked Bun main thread stalls the link after 8 KiB.
- UNKNOWN: which channels the populated draw.io webapp passes to `sendMessage` / `registerMsgListener` (webapp submodule empty in the clone; PANEL-P3 settles). UNKNOWN: draw.io open/save payload size distribution (PANEL-P3 / F04-T12).

## Platform lanes
macOS WKWebView is the only lane with renderer bridge code and the only first-proof lane. WebKitGTK and WebView2 have no renderer bridge in-tree; their cells are recorded `unknown` with an explicit documented gap, never inferred from macOS (KEL-79: one engine's pass cannot stand in for another). Future WebView2 work: single world gives synchronous calls natively but isolation is ▲; preload injection must use the async completion form; `chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync` is the only documented synchronous page→host primitive among the three engines (refuter receipt, Microsoft docs fetched 2026-10-06).
