tickets.title: feat(ipc): host-opaque endpoint value codec v0 in @keld/electron with shared golden vectors — sole codec owner (F03-D4 resolution)
tickets.current_behavior: No value codec exists; the bridge carries opaque bytes with endpoint codecs for the echo channel only.
tickets.what_to_build: One TypeScript codec module in @keld/electron used unchanged by the Bun facade and the renderer compat runtime and the F03-T5 executeJavaScript result envelope; the renderer copy is built from the same module, never hand-written: v0 domain = JSON values plus undefined, Date, Error (name, message, stack; custom properties dropped) and class instances flattened to own enumerable properties; Function, Promise, Symbol, WeakMap, WeakSet throw at the call site as Electron does; Map, Set, RegExp, TypedArray/Buffer throw a typed KELD-COMPAT error. Decoders treat bytes as hostile: bounded size and depth, no prototype writes, typed errors on malformed tags. The tag grammar is private to this module. This ticket is the only codec owner on the map; the arch 02 §5 'opaque to the host' amendment is owned by F04-T6, and the envelope shape that F03-T5 wraps around the encoded value is owned by F03-T5. The host never decodes.

undefined versus null, Date, Error (name, message, stack; the draw.io mainResp error shape) and a class instance flattened without its prototype round-trip
Map, Set, RegExp and TypedArray values throw a typed KELD-COMPAT error naming the type rather than degrading
A payload with a `__proto__` key, a malformed tag, or nesting beyond the depth bound is refused with a typed error, Object.prototype is unchanged and the stack is not exhausted
No Rust crate decodes the codec bytes

repair.epic_body:
## Scope
FACT (family model of Electron v44.4.5, recount 2026-10-07): 43 entities and 368 members. tickets.what_to_build:
A spec, then an implementation.

Scheme table:
- A static host-owned scheme table carrying scheme names only, consumed by keld-wv at engine construction.
- `keld migrate` lifts scheme names. Neither corpus app calls registerSchemesAsPrivileged, so every CustomScheme privilege bit is recorded ▲/✘ per engine pending demand.
- Hardening opt-outs (bypassCSP, allowServiceWorkers) are never config bits. If ever demanded, they are named, linted grants in the generated permissions manifest.
- `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` in app code is a check: names present in the table with no privilege bits are accepted; anything else fails before ready with a typed error naming the config patch.

Handler:
- `protocol.handle(scheme, handler)` registers the Bun role as producer behind the arch 05 resource adapter. The flow is: engine request → adapter bound to the active WebView and navigation generation → keld-guard → routed kipc to the Bun handler → bounded response.
- The scheme mints no filesystem authority. Bytes the handler reads go through the role's own fs grants.
- Responses above the live ceiling are a declared ▲ or a streaming/range lane selected in the spec.
- `unhandle` and `isProtocolHandled` follow.
- The deprecated register*/intercept* methods are either facaded onto handle or ✘. That choice is recorded in the spec.

Per-engine privilege behavior is recorded as ▲, never as a silent pass. INFERENCE from the refuter probe (not re-run): WKWebView resolves relative URLs, serves fetch and exposes storage on an unprivileged scheme.

The custom-scheme privilege and traversal matrix that X04-D3 originally carried belongs to this ticket's spec, with Zettlr as the demand.

tickets.what_to_build:
A macOS-only spec slice, then an implementation, that makes host policy enforce what draw.io's two webRequest listeners enforced in Electron.

(1) Read containment: a file:// application load is confined to its code directory as read root, and any file:// request outside it is refused before bytes reach the page.

(2) CSP injection: the host injects the CSP profile selected by X04-D3, which admits draw.io's directives including 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. The policy value has exactly one source: the generated per-window `web.csp` entry of the permissions manifest (arch 03 §2). The spec names its schema owner, because the guard parser ignores `windows` today. No second schema and no hard-coded string.

(3) Mechanism: X04-D3 decides between an injected meta policy over a contained file-URL load and a host scheme handler with a header policy. Constraint: the committed document URL must stay equal to the requested file:// URL. INFERENCE: this disqualifies any mechanism that changes draw.io's page origin, because its sender check would then reject every IPC channel.

repair.epic_title: compat(native): first-proof dialog, application menu and display/theme facts for draw.io on macOS (legacy profile); shell, clipboard/nativeImage, Tray and the remaining native modules as tracked next/parked slices
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
FACT: 38 entities / 350 members of the pinned Electron v44.4.5 model (family F06: Menu 13, MenuItem 21, Tray 36, dialog 8, Notification 30, clipboard 7, ClipboardItem 4, shell 7, screen 12, Display 19, globalShortcut 7, powerMonitor 16, powerSaveBlocker 3, nativeTheme 9, nativeImage 8, NativeImage 16, systemPreferences 28, safeStorage 8, pushNotifications 3, inAppPurchase 8, ShareMenu 3, desktopCapturer 1, plus 16 structures). Every module is main-process (renderer clipboard was removed in Electron 44.0, not deprecated; pinned breaking-changes).
FACT (keld@b4b907c3): keld-native implements only the retained FsBroker; its declared module-name list is window, menu, tray, dialog, notify, clipboard, shortcut, screen, power, shell, fs, secrets, deeplink, autostart, dock. Architecture 05 section 3 lists a `capture` (Tier 3) row that the list lacks and the 'does not yet include' sentence does not name (code/spec mismatch, F06-T13). Architecture 05 section 3 has no row that owns theme facts for nativeTheme (spec gap, named in F06-T5). `@keld/electron` exports only `app` and a default object.
FACT (experiment, Bun 1.4.2 macOS arm64, 2026-10-07, scratchpad probe): an ESM named import of a binding the facade does not export fails module linking with `SyntaxError: Export named ... not found` and exit 1. draw.io's main is an ES module that imports Menu, shell, dialog, screen, ClipboardItem, clipboard, nativeImage and nativeTheme from `electron`, so those bindings must exist before draw.io can boot at all (F06-T8).

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites)
- draw.io@2edf9fb main (FACT, re-read 2026-10-07): dialog.showMessageBox 6 sites; dialog.showMessageBoxSync 1 site, on the unsaved-changes close path inside an async listener; showOpenDialog 1 and showSaveDialog 1, both reached from the renderer request dispatcher and parented to the focused window; showErrorBox 0. Menu: buildFromTemplate + setApplicationMenu on macOS with 12 role items (hide, hideothers, unhide, quit, close, undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, pasteAndMatchStyle, selectAll) plus click items (About/Support open URLs; update and zoom actions); setApplicationMenu(null) off macOS. screen.getAllDisplays() work areas, screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea and nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors read at window construction; no themeSource and no `updated` listener. shell.openExternal 3 sites (two fixed Help-menu hosts; the window-open handler gated by a scheme regex admitting http, https, mailto, tel, callto), the promise is dropped at all three. clipboard.writeText/readText/write([ClipboardItem]) and nativeImage.createFromDataURL().toPNG() sit in one renderer-requested action; UNKNOWN whether the edit step reaches it (the web-app submodule is empty in the clone; PANEL-P3 decides). electron-context-menu is invoked at module top level; which Menu/MenuItem members it touches at import is UNKNOWN until PANEL-P3.
- Zettlr (second corpus, Electron ^43.6.0; research receipts, not re-opened in this repair): showMessageBox 24 sites, Tray, Notification, Menu.popup, platform menus with many accelerators, themeSource writes and `updated`, getDisplayMatching, synchronous clipboard.readText and the removed writeImage, openPath/showItemInFolder/trashItem, openDirectory picks.
- Zero resolved call sites in all three clones (FACT): globalShortcut, powerMonitor, powerSaveBlocker, safeStorage, pushNotifications, inAppPurchase, ShareMenu, desktopCapturer.

## Milestones (YAGNI test: draw.io on macOS, explicit legacy profile, install + activation + open, edit, save, close-with-unsaved-prompt)
- first-proof: F06-T1 (cells), F06-T8 (import surface), F06-T2 (open/save/message dialogs returning paths), F06-T7 (synchronous unsaved prompt, gated on PANEL-P1), F06-T4 (application menu with host-side roles; role quit records a diagnostic and never terminates), F06-T5 (display work areas and dark-mode fact).
- next: F06-T3 (shell, exact literal origins), F06-T6 (scoreboard rows), F06-T9 (menu click dispatch and item state), F06-T16 (role quit into the F01-T3 quit path), F06-T11 (screen/theme events and remaining getters), F06-T12 (clipboard + nativeImage for draw.io's clipboard action; pulled forward only if PANEL-P3 shows the edit step reaches it), F06-T14 (remaining dialog members).
- parked: F06-T10 (Tray, popup), F06-T13 (capture row reconciliation), F06-T15 (strict-profile user-intent filesystem grants).

## Maturity ladder
- L0: every F06 binding draw.io imports exists at import; unimplemented members raise a typed KELD-COMPAT unsupported error naming their ticket; every entity has a scoreboard row (F06-T8, F06-T6).
- L1: the first-proof slice passes its pinned cells on macOS under LegacySandboxOff (F06-T2, F06-T7, F06-T4, F06-T5).
- L2: next slices pass pinned cells on macOS (Zettlr demand).
- L3: product-corpus cells defined by the X02-T4 manifest and scored by the X02-T6 run, with KEL-74-schema records; Windows/Linux lanes.

## Linear owners consumed (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07, read-only)
- KEL-102 In Progress, unassigned: permission model and privileged dispatch. Task artifact consumed: KEL-102/T3 terminal artifact comment cde25f5e (PASSED/LANDED at 66ccbbc, CI 37313738834), the pattern for a guarded privileged channel. No KEL-102 task unit owns dialog or menu channel admission yet.
- KEL-212 In Progress (Amisha Ramani): inert-grant deny text and doctor; the shell spelling must not contradict it.
- KEL-237 In Progress, unassigned: manifest/runner pattern reused; its non-goals say 'no compatibility-surface expansion', so it is not the owner of F06 cells.
- KEL-74 Done (GYLDLAB): the evidence schema reused (cells carry an expected verdict and a negative control).
- KEL-127 Todo, unassigned; its only attachment is the #391 map link (fetched 2026-10-07): non-goal 'No shared memory, CEF, broad Electron API expansion, additional native-module names, or updater implementation before G2'. G2 task state: KEL-142 Done; KEL-140, KEL-141, KEL-143 Backlog, unassigned; KEL-144 Backlog.
- KEL-80 Backlog, unassigned (fetched 2026-10-07): bounded channels; candidate (unconfirmed) Linear reference for the PANEL-P1 follow-on transport. KEL-97 Backlog, unassigned (fetched 2026-10-07).
- KEL-78 In Progress (GYLDLAB): strict profile; owner of the parked strict-profile work.
- KEL-103 In Progress (Amisha Ramani) and KEL-135 In Progress (Amisha Ramani): packaging/app identity prerequisites for parked Notification and safeStorage rows.
- Not owners: KEL-130 Done (FsBroker; its spec lists 'dialog grant' as a non-goal), KEL-16 Done, KEL-208 Done, KEL-209 Duplicate, KEL-19 Done (the CLI RFC, not Windows AppUserModelID), KEL-72 Done (facade bootstrap), KEL-89 In Progress but it is keld-auth (authentication), not secret storage.
- Tracker of record (X06-D7 owner decision, GitHub #517 owner comment 6024917784, 2026-10-07): no live Linear issue's scope covers F06 conformance cells or the native dialog/menu/screen brokers (team KELD searches 'dialog' and 'menu', 2026-10-07; KEL-102's spec leaves per-module broker tracking open), so each F06 GitHub issue holds the claim, status and evidence, and no Linear issue is created. Linear holds references only: KEL-102 is the recommended reference for the channel tickets (F06-T2, F06-T3, F06-T4), KEL-127 the fallback for the rest. FACT: KEL-127 carries only the #391 link today; the per-ticket links are an orchestrator write. Residual gap named in the owner record: root AGENTS.md and workflow.md still describe Linear-only claims; the #517 record is the documented exception until they are amended through the .agents/instructions.md protocol (a separate owner-authorized change, not a gate for these tickets).
- BLOCKER (owner reading): repository landing of F06 implementation waits for the KEL-127 owner to record whether the draw.io first-proof slice is outside 'broad Electron API expansion' before G2 (X06-D1 correction options A/C). Analysis, specs and scratchpad prototypes may proceed.

## Design facts (labelled after batch-2 refutation)
- FACT (F06-D3 decided A): resource-less capabilities are literals in `app.system`, evaluated by the existing matcher as (system, literal); a probe on the live guard allows a granted literal, denies an ungranted one with followable fix text, and no wildcard matches a literal. The first proof adds only the `dialog` and `menu` literals and registers only those channels; the spelling is reviewed as an architecture 03 amendment under KEL-102's D9 permission-model gate, and X04-T1 (next) records the row afterwards without gating the first-proof tickets. INFERENCE from the same decision: the display/theme facts of F06-T5 carry no literal and reach only roles F02-T2 admits to its mirror stream; F06-T5's spec records that ruling under its permission-model gate. The earlier wording 'the guard's accepted operation set is hard-coded to fs.read/fs.write' is withdrawn: evaluate has no operation allowlist; what is limited is which channels are registered. The legacy profile is still authenticated and guarded, so a missing grant is a deny and no keld-native allowlist may grant anything implicitly.
- FACT (F06-D1 parked): under LegacySandboxOff a dialog returns paths and the app's later file I/O is ambient node:fs, recorded as forfeited containment. The FsBroker-registration mechanism, the `<name>.*` sibling glob and the dialog-only/never-persisted lifetime are refuted (draw.io's siblings are prefix-named `.$`/`~$` with `.dtmp`/`.bkp`; its blessed set persists for Open Recent; it also blesses argv, open-file and second-instance paths). Reopened only as F06-T15.
- FACT (F06-D4, duplicate of X04-D4, resolution A): shell.openExternal opens exact literal origins only; every other URL is a typed refusal recorded as a declared divergence; confirm-class tokens and scheme-wide globs are rejected.
- SURVIVES with corrections (research decision F06-D2): Menu/MenuItem/Tray/popup handles are host-main-thread resources with host-assigned ids; Bun-side item state is authoritative for synchronous getters and the host is a projection; Electron role strings map to generic keld-native menu actions and never live in keld-core or keld-ipc; role close enters the vetoable close path in the first proof (F06-T4) and role quit enters the quit path only with F06-T16 after F01-T3; until then role quit records a diagnostic and never terminates (neither is 'no round trip'); the default menu is built in the facade; the pinned implementation falls back to `click` when role execution fails; macOS popup order is menu-will-close, then click, then the popup callback (pinned Cocoa menu controller).
- REFUTED parts of research decision F06-D5: NativeImage is mutable (setTemplateImage, addRepresentation); createFromPath is a synchronous multi-file DPI-suffix probe; createFromDataURL(png).toPNG() re-encodes rather than passing bytes through; the `clipboardLegacySync` quirk is deleted and 43-era synchronous clipboard is unsupported with a typed fix-it; the blocking-CALL rule is architecture 02 text about renderer sendSync, not KEL-127. The W3C promise shape is the baseline (pinned model: readText/writeText/read/write/has return Promise, clear returns void, no writeImage).
- SURVIVES with corrections (research decision F06-D6): safeStorage is a host secrets-module facade, Tier 2, parked; the secrets-module spec owner is UNKNOWN; on Linux the default basic_text path matches Electron (isEncryptionAvailable false, encryptString throws), the only divergence is refusing setUsePlainTextEncryption(true); the synchronous trio needs the PANEL-P1 transport, the async trio is the baseline.
- FACT (panel probe): the Bun kipc client cannot block and a parked Bun main thread stalls the link after 8,192 bytes, so every synchronous main-process member that needs the host (showMessageBoxSync, sync open/save, host-decoded NativeImage results, the safeStorage sync trio) depends on PANEL-P1. FACT (repaired map): no ticket yet implements the worker-owned transport PANEL-P1 selects; the recommended key is F04-T18 (F04 owns IPC); F06-T7 and F06-T14 name it as an external predecessor.
- FACT (refuter experiment, Bun 1.4.2, 2026-10-06): an unhandled promise rejection exits a stock Bun process with code 1, while Electron's main installs a do-not-quit handler that shows an error box. draw.io drops the openExternal promise, so a typed refusal can end the main role. Owner: the lifecycle unit (F01); no published key yet.
- FACT (pinned v44.4.5 source): openExternal's `activate` maps to the macOS open configuration's activates flag; invalid accelerator strings are logged and ignored, not thrown; safeStorage before ready throws on encrypt/decrypt and returns false/'unknown' for the availability/backend getters.
- UNKNOWN: macOS pasteboard privacy-alert behaviour for programmatic reads; Windows/Linux popup event order; how system webviews reflect themeSource; whether strict containment blocks Bun.Image's built-in clipboard access.

## Platform lanes
macOS first (AppKit on the host main thread). Windows (Win32/WinRT) and Linux (GTK4 + XDG portals, portal-first) backends are not yet specified; no Mac evidence is presented as Windows or Linux proof.

## Decisions governing this unit
Closed: F06-D1 (parked, option A for the first proof), F06-D3 (decided A), F06-D4 (duplicate of X04-D4, option A). Open decisions consumed as edges: PANEL-P1, PANEL-P3, PANEL-D22. Program decision applied without an edge (closed): X06-D7 (tracker of record).

tickets.title: feat(native): guarded async dialog broker on macOS (showOpenDialog/showSaveDialog/showMessageBox) parented to host-minted windows, returning paths only under the legacy profile
tickets.current_behavior: No dialog broker; keld-native implements only the FsBroker. `dialog` is only a declared module name.
tickets.what_to_build: Implement the keld-native `dialog` module for macOS (open panel, save panel, alert) behind a new guarded privileged channel, exposed as a generic `@keld/api` operation and mapped to Electron shapes in the `@keld/electron` dialog facade. The facade passes the host-minted window id from F02-T2; a dialog with a shown parent attaches to it, otherwise it shows as an independent window. Every call is evaluated by keld-guard against the `dialog` literal in `app.system` (closed decision F06-D3 A fixes the literal; X04-T1 records the row afterwards and does not gate this ticket). Under LegacySandboxOff the broker returns paths only: it mints no filesystem authority, and the app's later reads and writes through node:fs are ambient and recorded as forfeited containment. Synchronous variants are owned by F06-T7 (showMessageBoxSync) and F06-T14 (showOpenDialogSync, showSaveDialogSync, showErrorBox, showCertificateTrustDialog). Strict-profile user-intent grants are owned by F06-T15. The approved spec precedes code and names the channel id under the X05-T2 rule and the macOS automation used to drive panels on a real Mac (UNKNOWN today).
acceptance_criteria: The F06-T1 cells for showOpenDialog, showSaveDialog, showMessageBox and window parenting flip from their expected fail to pass in this change
On macOS, with `dialog` granted, choosing a file in draw.io's open request returns {canceled:false, filePaths:[<chosen path>]}; cancelling returns {canceled:true, filePaths:[]}
showSaveDialog returns {canceled:false, filePath:<chosen path>}; cancelling returns {canceled:true, filePath:""}
showMessageBox resolves {response:<clicked index>, checkboxChecked:false} when no checkboxLabel is set
Without the `dialog` literal, the call rejects with a typed KELD-GUARD denial whose fix text names /app/system, and no panel appears
A dialog given a window attaches as a sheet to the native window F02-T2 minted for it; an id from a previous Bun generation is rejected with a typed error

tickets.current_behavior: No menu module; `menu` is only a declared module name.
tickets.what_to_build: Menu.buildFromTemplate builds a Bun-side Menu/MenuItem tree (Bun state is authoritative for synchronous getters; the host is a projection). setApplicationMenu submits one bounded tree to the host over a guarded channel evaluated against the `menu` literal (closed decision F06-D3 A fixes the literal; X04-T1 records the row afterwards and does not gate this ticket); the host builds the native menu bar on its main thread and assigns command ids. Electron role strings map to generic keld-native menu actions inside the compat seam, never in keld-core or keld-ipc. The roles draw.io uses (hide, hideothers, unhide, undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, pasteAndMatchStyle, selectAll) execute host-side with no host-to-Bun frame. role close enters the F02-T3 cancelable close path of the focused window. role quit (menu item or its default Cmd+Q) does not terminate in this ticket: it records a KELD-COMPAT diagnostic naming F06-T16, closes no window and leaves the app running, because the quit state machine and the host quit-requested path are owned by F01-T3 (next) and a native terminate would bypass draw.io's unsaved-changes veto. F06-T16 routes role quit into the F01-T3 path. setApplicationMenu returns void like Electron, so a guard denial is reported as a typed recorded diagnostic and the menu is not installed. Click delivery for non-role items is owned by F06-T9; until then a click on such an item emits a recorded KELD-COMPAT diagnostic. Tray and popup are owned by F06-T10. The members electron-context-menu touches at import come from PANEL-P3.

repair.epic_title: compat(renderer): app preload in a separate content world, sandboxed-preload require map, renderer process object, zero-<webview> contract (first proof); Zettlr preload extras next; <webview> mapping and browser-quirk ledger parked
repair.epic_body:
## Scope

FACT (families model, Electron v44.4.5): this family is one Electron entity, the `webviewTag` element: 113 members (65 methods, 35 events, 13 attributes). It is renderer-only, Electron's own page warns against using it, and arch 04 §4 puts it in Tier 3. FACT (compat matrix): all 113 rows are UNSUPPORTED today.

This epic also owns the renderer-side runtime that runs an app's preload, even though the APIs that runtime exposes belong to other families (process is F01; webFrame, sharedTexture and PreloadScript* are F03; contextBridge, ipcRenderer and webUtils are F04). The split is one owner per atom:
- F07-T1 owns where the preload runs (content world), when it runs (document start, main frame), the sandboxed `require` map and wrapper bindings, the renderer `process` object, preload-path containment, the KEL-142 isolation re-run, and the one diagnostic metric id for the app-world handler's per-call cost.
- F04-T4 owns the contextBridge value table, ipcRenderer semantics and the draw.io request round trip. It consumes F07-T1.
- F02-T4 owns WebPreferences triage, including accepting `webviewTag` with default false and the `sandbox:false` ▲ row.
- F02-T2 owns emitting `web-contents-created`.
- X03-T1 owns the boot-fact values (version table, platform, arch) that the renderer process object exposes.
- X05-T1 (parked) owns the comparative compat-overhead metric ids and their admission rules; when pulled it adopts F07-T1's diagnostic id rather than redefining it.

FACT (Keld origin/main 8678c0d1; no file in crates/ or packages/ mentions a preload): what is live today is the macOS KEL-142 bridge only. It is a trusted script plus a native handler in a non-page WKContentWorld, a frozen page-world facade exposing only `window.keld.invoke`, main-frame-only, at document start. There is no app-preload injection, no renderer `@keld/electron` shim and no `@keld/web`.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, not token-scan counts)

- FACT (drawio-desktop@2edf9fb, fixed-string grep):
  - The preload does one `require('electron')` (contextBridge, ipcRenderer). It calls `ipcRenderer.on` ×3, `once` ×1 and `send` ×2, and `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` ×2: `electron` = {request, registerMsgListener, sendMessage, listenOnce} and `process` = {type, versions}.
  - It reads `process.argv` for a flag passed through `additionalArguments`, and seeds the `.configuration` localStorage key at document start inside try/catch.
  - It installs a `window.navigation` navigate listener guarded by a null check, to block about: navigations.
  - `webviewTag:false` is set on every window (6 sites). `will-attach-webview` is answered with `preventDefault()`, registered only inside `app.on('web-contents-created')`.
  - The preload path is computed at runtime as an absolute path from `__dirname` (4 windows).
  - Zero sites for sendSync, invoke, removeListener, removeAllListeners, webFrame, ipcRenderer.postMessage, registerPreloadScript and `<webview>`.
- UNKNOWN: page-side callers of `window.electron.*` and readers of `window.process`. The draw.io webapp submodule is empty in the clone. Populating it is a PANEL-P3 prerequisite.
- FACT (zettlr@e6c7fd8):
  - Every window uses one preload, generated by the forge entrypoint config. It calls `exposeInMainWorld` ×5, and `ipcRenderer` invoke 1, send 1, sendSync 4, on 1, off 1, setMaxListeners 1. Its `process` exposure is platform, version, versions, arch, uptime(), getSystemVersion(), a copy of env, and argv. It uses `webUtils.getPathForFile` (3 page call sites).
  - The 186 `ipcRenderer.invoke` occurrences are page-world calls on the `window.ipc` proxy across 63 files, so the load falls on contextBridge function proxying.
  - The two `sandbox:false` windows use the same preload, which imports only contextBridge, ipcRenderer and webUtils. That is a ▲ ignored-with-diagnostic row owned by F02-T4.
- FACT (electron-quick-start@82dbb35): the preload path comes from `path.join(__dirname)`, and the preload requires nothing from electron.

## Maturity ladder (milestone ≠ tier label)

- L0, first-proof:
  - F02-T4 accepts `webviewTag` (default false).
  - F07-T2: `<webview>` stays an undefined element, `will-attach-webview` can be registered and is never emitted, and 113 ✘(tracked) rows exist.
- L1, first-proof:
  - F07-T1: draw.io's unmodified preload runs in a separate app content world on macOS, and the KEL-142 isolation tests and the adversarial-preload test pass with it installed.
  - F04-T4 then completes the contextBridge/ipcRenderer round trip.
- L2, next:
  - F07-T6: the process members Zettlr needs, and Zettlr's already-bundled preload.
  - The WebKitGTK named-world lane.
- L3, next, F04-owned: synchronous-return wrappers and sendSync, gated by F04-A3 and F04-A5.
- Parked:
  - F07-T3: `<webview>` as a host-owned child webview.
  - F07-T5: the browser-quirk ledger.
  - The WebView2 lane.

## Tracker of record (X06-D7, owner decision)

- FACT (GitHub #517, owner-decision comment 6024917784 by @0monish, 2026-10-06T20:32:51Z; #517 is closed): option D is adopted for unaligned work. Each repo-writing ticket is aligned to the nearest live Linear issue whose scope covers it, and the claim happens there. Otherwise the GitHub issue is the tracker of record: the `## Agent claim` comment (earliest comment wins; the assignee mirrors it), status, handoffs and evidence live on GitHub, and no Linear issue is created. Every GitHub ticket is linked from the nearest live Linear issue for its surface, falling back to KEL-127.
- FACT (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07): no live Linear issue's scope covers any repo-writing ticket in this epic. KEL-142 is Done, KEL-237 is lifecycle-only, KEL-79 covers only the origin contract, and KEL-80 covers bounded virtual channels. So each F07 ticket's own GitHub issue is its tracker of record (F07-T1 #484, F07-T2 #485, F07-T3 #486; F07-T4, F07-T5 and F07-T6 get numbers at publish), each linked on KEL-127 (Todo, unassigned).
- FACT (same #517 comment): root `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agents/workflow.md` still describe Linear-only tracking. The #517 record and map #391 are the documented exception that agents on this program cite. The instruction-file amendment is a separate owner-authorized change under the `.agents/instructions.md` protocol, not a predecessor of any F07 ticket.
- So no F07 ticket is held for "missing owner". F07-T1, F07-T3 and F07-T6 are held only by their spec gates.

## Linear owners consumed (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07, read-only)

- KEL-142 Done (completed 2026-10-01; parent KEL-139). Approved spec landed in #344 (fff22722). Bridge and its AC2 isolation tests landed in #351 (9e43edc9). No live Linear issue owns the spec revision that F07-T1 needs; under X06-D7 that revision is tracked on GitHub #484.
- KEL-127 Todo, unassigned. Program convergence issue; the fallback Linear reference that links every F07 GitHub ticket (X06-D7).
- KEL-80 Backlog, unassigned. Bounded virtual channels; the floor-v2 vehicle consumed through F04-T2.
- KEL-79 Backlog, unassigned. Secure-origin and resource-transport contract. It keeps the renderer origin contract only; preload-injection ownership moved off it (X06-D1).
- KEL-74 Done (GYLDLAB). Evidence schema owner for conformance cells.
- KEL-90 In Progress (GYLDLAB). Cross-OS metric-runner standard; the `gyldlab/keld-benches` metric registry is the single source of metric ids (arch 01 §5.1) that F07-T1's diagnostic id is added to.
- KEL-237 In Progress, unassigned. Lifecycle-only corpus; its non-goals exclude compatibility-surface expansion, so it does not own renderer cells.
- KEL-177 In Progress, unassigned. Parent program; migration friction.
- KEL-135 In Progress, Amisha Ramani. One persistent store per app identity; parked `<webview>` partitions need a change to its spec.
- KEL-75 In Progress, unassigned. Role and environment contract; window-bound roles for a parked guest.
- KEL-53 In Progress, Amisha Ramani. Canonical package/update path.
- KEL-19 Done (GYLDLAB). CLI RFC; `keld build`/`keld migrate` are still reserved (KELD-CLI-045).
- KEL-168 Done. WebView2 popups.
- KEL-132 (In Progress) was removed from this list: it owns GPU mutation and media guard installation, not renderer preload.

## Design facts (labelled)

- DECIDED (PANEL-D21, closed, option A):
  - The app preload and compat runtime run in a separate named content world, with their own world-scoped handler on the same per-view user-content controller. The KEL-142 handler and nonce stay unreachable to app code.
  - FACT (measured world-probe, macOS 26.5.1, 2026-10-06): a same-world script reached the handler and captured the document nonce. A named-world script saw neither.
  - Rejected: B (shared world), C (nonce-less DOM relay, which page script can forge), D (hardened shared world).
  - UNKNOWN: the per-call cost of the app-world handler. The probe produced no result in 120 s. F07-T1 records it as a diagnostic under one diagnostic metric id that it registers in the existing keld-benches registry, with no threshold; X05-T1, parked, adopts that id. Also UNKNOWN: how that handler binds to the current document.
- FACT (Electron v44.4.5 sandboxed renderer source, fetched 2026-10-07):
  - The preload `require` resolves `electron`, `electron/common`, `electron/renderer`, `events`, `node:events`, `timers`, `node:timers`, `url` and `node:url`.
  - The electron module list is contextBridge, crashReporter, ipcRenderer, nativeImage, sharedTexture, webFrame and webUtils.
  - The wrapper receives `require`, `process`, `exports`, `module`, plus the globals Buffer, global, setImmediate and clearImmediate.
  - An out-of-map require throws `module not found: <name>`. An uncaught preload error logs `Unable to load preload script: <path>`, sends the preload-error message, and the page still loads.
  - The sandbox tutorial lists six modules (no sharedTexture). Source is the runtime truth; the conformance entry records the difference.
- FACT (web-preferences.md): preload "will be loaded before other scripts run in the page" and "should be the absolute file path to the script"; additionalArguments "will be appended to `process.argv` in the renderer process".
  - Keld resolves the app-supplied path at window creation and refuses any path outside the app package root. There is no migrate-time path rewrite: every corpus value is computed at runtime.
- UNKNOWN / owner gap: no live owner verifies app-package file bytes at launch on macOS.
  - ExpectedAppIdentity carries identity bytes (app id, channel, target), not a content verifier.
  - The KEL-53/keld-pack canonical package path is Windows-production today.
  - The first proof claims path containment only, never byte authentication.
- DECIDED (F07-E1, closed, A): `process.env` is an empty object in every preload.
  - FACT: the role environment holds the app-link possession secret (`KELD_APP_LINK`).
  - A declared allow-list sourced from the main role (never the host), with unconditional `KELD_*` exclusion, is parked until a committed Zettlr cell reads one of the five names Zettlr writes at runtime.
- DECIDED (F07-A6, closed, A): web storage is lost because the engine and data store change (Chromium session store → WKWebsiteDataStore), not only because the origin changes.
  - First launch under Keld starts empty, as a labelled migrate-report divergence (wording owned by X02-T1). Electron session data is never read, moved or deleted.
  - An app-assisted bridge-release export is parked until a bridge release is scheduled.
  - UNKNOWN, routed to F07-T4: whether localStorage persists for a file:// document in the KEL-135 store.
- FACT (draw.io main): every IPC is authorized with `senderFrame.url` starting with the file:// code URL.
  - The document URL reported to the app must equal the loaded file:// URL. F05-T4 owns that observable; KEL-79 owns the origin contract.
  - Any origin change silently kills every draw.io channel.
- INFERENCE (refuter, semantics): contextBridge needs a synchronous, in-renderer, cross-world mechanism that is separate from the asynchronous `window.keld` relay. It is owned by F04-T4 and F04-A3, and macOS contextBridge is SCAFFOLDED until F04's two-world experiment passes.
  - FACT: the existing relay posts with target origin `*`, so app-world data must never ride it.
- INFERENCE: F07-T1 allocates no new kipc channel id. App-world requests carry Electron channel names as data under `el:` grants through the existing wv-link decoder, so the X05-T2 channel table is not an F07-T1 gate. If the KEL-142 revision turns out to need a new kipc channel id, it takes the id from X05-T2's table and the edge F07-T1 ← X05-T2 is added in that revision.
- UNKNOWN: whether the Navigation API is available in a WKWebView content world on the first-proof macOS. Recorded as an F07-T4 observation cell. Host-side denial of about: navigations is owned by F03-T3, independent of the preload.
- `<webview>`: zero call sites in all three corpus apps. It stays Tier 3 and parked.

## Platform lanes

- macOS (first proof): named WKContentWorld, document start, main frame only. Fails closed below macOS 11 (KEL-142 §5.1).
- Linux (next):
  - FACT (webkitgtk.org, since 2.40, receipt from refuter batch 1): the UI-process APIs `register_script_message_handler_with_reply(world_name)` and `evaluate_javascript(world_name)` give isolated-world request/reply without a web-process extension.
  - Prerequisite: replace the wry 0.56.1 scaffold with direct bindings (arch 05 §1).
- Windows (parked):
  - INFERENCE (negative evidence only): WebView2 exposes no isolated-world API.
  - The KEL-142 nonce model does not transfer. Identity must come from the host-side ICoreWebView2 event source plus the host navigation generation; a page-world script may hold nothing that authorizes.
  - Any contextBridge on WebView2 would be a ▲ emulation.

On macOS, inject the app's preload at document start, main frame only, into a named app content world. That world must be separate from both the page world and the KEL-142 trusted bridge world, and it gets its own world-scoped message handler on the same per-view user-content controller (PANEL-D21 option A, decided).

Run the preload as a function body under Electron's sandboxed-preload wrapper contract, derived from the pinned v44.4.5 sandboxed-renderer source rather than the tutorial list:
- `require` resolves exactly `electron`, `electron/common`, `electron/renderer`, `events`, `node:events`, `timers`, `node:timers`, `url` and `node:url`.
- The wrapper receives `require`, `process`, `exports` and `module`, plus the globals Buffer, global, setImmediate and clearImmediate.
- An out-of-map require throws `module not found: <name>`.
- An uncaught preload error logs `Unable to load preload script: <path>` and the page still loads.

The electron module object lists contextBridge, crashReporter, ipcRenderer, nativeImage, sharedTexture, webFrame and webUtils. Members this ticket does not implement throw a typed KELD-COMPAT unsupported error; they are never a silent no-op. contextBridge and ipcRenderer are filled by F04-T4.

Renderer `process` object:
- `type` = 'renderer', `sandboxed` = true, `contextIsolated` = true.
- `versions` deep-equals the main-role `process.versions` that X03-T4 maps from the F01-T4 session-facts payload (one source of truth; nothing is invented in the renderer).
- `argv` has the window's `additionalArguments` appended.
- `env` = {} (F07-E1 decided A).

The app-supplied absolute preload path is resolved and canonicalised at window creation. Window creation is refused with a typed error if the path falls outside the app package root, and the host loads the preload bytes.

The app-world handler feeds the one existing wv-link decoder and app link. It admits nothing the window's enumerated `el:` grant (F04-T3) does not allow; with no grant, that is deny. It never relays through `window.postMessage`.

PANEL-D21 requires the handler's per-call cost to be recorded as a diagnostic. This ticket registers exactly one diagnostic metric id for it in the existing keld-benches metric registry, the single owner of metric ids (arch 01 §5.1; KEL-90). The id has claim class diagnostic, is publication-ineligible, and carries no threshold. No second registry or local metric list is created. X05-T1, parked, excludes this id and never re-registers or redefines it.

draw.io's unmodified preload, injected into the app world, resolves `require('electron')`, finds its `--initial-adaptive-colors=` flag in `process.argv` when the window passes it through `additionalArguments`, and its `.configuration` localStorage seed is visible to the first page script.

A preload that throws at top level produces the console line `Unable to load preload script: <path>`, and the page still finishes loading.

In the preload, `process.type === 'renderer'`, `process.sandboxed === true`, `process.contextIsolated === true`, `process.versions` deep-equals the F01-T4 session-facts payload, as mapped by X03-T4, and `process.env` is an own-property-free object (a fixture role environment containing `KELD_APP_LINK` is not visible).

Every message from the app world passes through the single wv-link decoder. On a window with no `el:` grant, every app-world request is refused with the existing typed error and no host effect, and an app-world message from a document that has since navigated is refused.

An app-supplied preload path that canonicalises (symlinks resolved) outside the app package root makes window creation fail with a typed KELD error naming the path, and the file is never read.

The keld-benches metric registry holds exactly one diagnostic id for the app-world handler's per-call cost, with the registry's required oracle, census, clock and statistic fields and claim class diagnostic. Its recorded samples carry no threshold and no pass/fail outcome.

tickets.what_to_build:
Prove the zero-webview contract that draw.io relies on:
- A `will-attach-webview` listener registered on a window's webContents is never emitted, including when a page inserts `<webview>`. F03-T2's facade accepts the registration, and F02-T2 announces the window through `app.on('web-contents-created')`.
- `<webview>` is never defined, so no custom element and no child webview exist.

Adjacent owners:
- Accepting `webPreferences.webviewTag` (default false) is F02-T4's row.
- Emitting `web-contents-created` is F02-T2's.
- Accepting the listener registration is F03-T2's.
- X02-T6 scores the workflow-wide zero-emission observation.
- The 113 webviewTag scoreboard rows are F07-T7 (next).
- Reporting `<webview>` usage in migrate output is X02-T2's, which classifies against the F07-T7 rows.
acceptance_criteria: The F07-T4 entries for the webviewTag default and will-attach-webview emission are already present with an expected status that the runner asserts.
On macOS, a fixture that copies draw.io's `web-contents-created` handler registers `will-attach-webview` on the created window's webContents without throwing.
On macOS, a `will-attach-webview` listener registered on a fixture window is invoked zero times while that window's page inserts and then removes a `<webview>` element.
A page that inserts `<webview src="https://example.invalid">` gets an element with no shadow content, no child webview, no navigation and no host effect.
negative_controls: Registering a `webview` custom element backed by an iframe fails the honesty entry.
Emitting `will-attach-webview` when the fixture page inserts `<webview>` fails the zero-invocation criterion.
Dropping `will-attach-webview` from the F03-T2 registration-safe set makes the draw.io-handler fixture throw, which fails the registration criterion.

tickets.what_to_build:
Land red-until-implemented KEL-74-schema cells for this family before any F07 implementation. Each cell cites the pinned Electron v44.4.5 sentence or source. Each pending cited cell is recorded in the X01-T3 red-until-implemented representation: expected verdict `fail` with its implementing-ticket key, and a mapped test that asserts today's behaviour and passes; the implementing change inverts the test and flips the cell to `pass`. The implementing tickets are F07-T1, F07-T2 and F07-T6. `unknown` is used only for the observation cells below and unrun engines. The manifest carries the corpus pin set by the X01-T3 pin rule and is validated by the X01-T4 shared owner.

Cells citing a pinned sentence or source:
- preload is "loaded before other scripts run in the page" and "should be the absolute file path".
- additionalArguments are "appended to process.argv in the renderer process".
- The sandboxed require map and wrapper bindings, taken from the sandboxed-renderer source, with the tutorial-versus-source difference (sharedTexture, electron/common, electron/renderer) recorded in the entry.
- An out-of-map require throws `module not found: <name>`.
- An uncaught preload error logs `Unable to load preload script: <path>` and the page still loads.
- The sandboxed process subset (type, sandboxed, contextIsolated, versions, argv, env). env carries Keld's declared divergence {} per F07-E1.
- webviewTag "Defaults to false".
- will-attach-webview is emitted only when a `<webview>` attaches.

Observation cells with status unknown until observed:
- Navigation API presence in a WKWebView content world on the first-proof macOS.
- localStorage persistence across relaunch for a file:// document in the KEL-135 store.
- `<webview>` under Electron with webviewTag false yields an undefined element (observed-only, BEHAVIOR_MATCH-capped).

Explicit ✘ cells:
- session.registerPreloadScript, PreloadScript and PreloadScriptRegistration.
- Sandboxed renderer process members outside the first-proof and Zettlr subsets: crash, hang, getCreationTime, getHeapStatistics, getBlinkMemoryInfo, getProcessMemoryInfo, getSystemMemoryInfo, getCPUUsage, execPath, pid, mas, windowsStore, contextId.
- sharedTexture members.

tickets.what_to_build:
Extend the F07-T1 renderer process object with platform, version, arch, `uptime()` and `getSystemVersion()`. platform, version and arch come from the F01-T4 session-facts payload, as mapped by X03-T4. `uptime()` and `getSystemVersion()` come from the host. Nothing is invented in the renderer. UNKNOWN: X03-T4's member list does not name platform, arch or version, so whether its mapping carries them is open. If it does not, this ticket's spec adds them through F01-T4's field set and X03-T4's mapping, never as a renderer-side constant. Run Zettlr's single bundled preload (its own forge/webpack output) under the same function-wrapper contract.

INFERENCE: Zettlr's build already emits one bundled preload per window, so no Keld bundler is needed for it. `keld build` and `keld migrate` remain reserved (KELD-CLI-045). The out-of-map import diagnostic runs on the bundled artifact and is X02-T2's.

`process.env` stays {}. The F07-E1 option B allow-list (sourced from the main role, `KELD_*` excluded unconditionally) is specified only when a committed Zettlr cell reads one of PANDOC_VERSION, QUARTO_VERSION, GIT_VERSION, ZETTLR_IS_TRAY_SUPPORTED or ZETTLR_TRAY_ERROR.
acceptance_criteria: The F07-T4 process-subset entries for platform, version, arch, uptime and getSystemVersion are present with an asserted expected status, and this change flips them.

Zettlr's bundled preload evaluates past its process exposure with no TypeError: `getSystemVersion()` returns a non-empty string, `uptime()` returns a non-negative number, and platform, arch and version equal the F01-T4 session-facts payload values as mapped by X03-T4.

repair.epic_title: compat(diagnostics): engine process-gone and hang events, F08 scoreboard rows, parked crashReporter / process-stats / getAppMetrics facades (contentTracing never)
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
FACT (Electron v44.4.5 API model, family split F08): 12 entities / 63 members: contentTracing (5 methods), crashReporter (8 methods), and ten structures: CPUUsage (3), CrashReport (2), EnableHeapProfilingOptions (3), GPUFeatureStatus (13), MemoryInfo (3), MemoryUsageDetails (3), ProcessMemoryInfo (3), ProcessMetric (9), TraceCategoriesAndOptions (2), TraceConfig (9).
The tickets also cover diagnostics members that the compat matrix files under other families: WebContents and app `render-process-gone`, RenderProcessGoneDetails, app `child-process-gone`, BrowserWindow/WebContents `unresponsive`/`responsive`, app.getAppMetrics, the process diagnostic getters (getHeapStatistics, getCPUUsage, getProcessMemoryInfo, getSystemMemoryInfo, getBlinkMemoryInfo, getCreationTime, crash, hang, takeHeapSnapshot, setFdLimit), and the GPU getters (getGPUFeatureStatus, getGPUInfo, isHardwareAccelerationEnabled, gpu-info-update). `app.disableHardwareAcceleration` is owned by F01-T6, per the closed F08-D6 ruling.

## Corpus demand (FACT, grep of the corpus clones drawio-desktop@2edf9fb, zettlr@e6c7fd8 and electron-quick-start@82dbb35, re-run 2026-10-07)
- Zero call sites for crashReporter, contentTracing, getAppMetrics, the GPU getters and the process memory/CPU getters in all three clones.
- draw.io registers `render-process-gone` twice: once on the import window and once on the export window. Both handlers only read `details.reason` into an error string. Neither is on the open → edit → save → close workflow window.
- Zettlr registers BrowserWindow `unresponsive` → `destroy()` on its onboarding window.
- draw.io and Zettlr call `disableHardwareAcceleration()` only behind an opt-in CLI flag (F01-T6 owns this).
- **First-proof demand from this family: none.** No F08 ticket is milestone first-proof. Falsifier: the PANEL-P3 draw.io boot trace finds an F08 member on the install, activation or 4-step workflow path.

## Maturity ladder
- **L0 (parked, F08-T2).** Every family member and every covered adjacent member has a scoreboard row with an explicit status: documented-never, typed-unsupported or deferred-to-key. Unsupported `app` members throw under the F01 L0 typed-error rule; there is never a silent no-op.
- **L1 (next).**
  - F08-T1: `render-process-gone` from engine web-content-process termination, macOS first.
  - F08-T4: `unresponsive`/`responsive` from engine hang signals where the engine has one.
  - Both consume conformance entries from F08-T3, which owns the webContents and app render-process-gone cells.
- **L2 (parked).**
  - F08-T5: crashReporter local-state facade.
  - F08-T6: Bun-side process stats.
  - F08-T7: getAppMetrics over the arch 01 §5.1 census.
  - F08-T8: `child-process-gone` for named roles.
  - F08-T9: contentTracing typed rejections.

## Linear owners consumed (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07)
- **KEL-75** (role generations, utilityProcess mapping): In Progress, unassigned.
- **KEL-143** (Bun generation recovery, the Bun-primary successor contract): Backlog, unassigned. Adjacent owner only; no F08 ticket is gated on it.
- **KEL-129** (§5.1 census ruling): In Progress, assignee GYLDLAB. The §5.1 text is landed in architecture 01.
- **KEL-90** (bench runner): In Progress, assignee GYLDLAB.
- **KEL-105** (window-phase Bun crash surfacing): In Progress, unassigned.
- **KEL-116**: Done. It was the ready-then-exit-0 fix, so it cannot own new SelfTerminationRecord fields.
- **KEL-132** (GPU safety): In Progress, unassigned. Owns any future per-engine GPU policy.
- **KEL-98** (echo codegen contract source): Done. Task artifact: merged PR #251, head d45a7bf.
- **KEL-74** (compat scoreboard): Done.
- **KEL-237** (lifecycle corpus): In Progress, unassigned.
- **KEL-78** (strict sandbox): In Progress, assignee GYLDLAB.
- **KEL-79** (secure origin): Backlog.

No open KEL issue owns keld-wv engine process-failure hooks or F08 conformance/scoreboard rows (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07, alignment record). Under the X06-D7 owner decision (GitHub #517, owner decision comment 6024917784), each F08 ticket's own GitHub issue is its tracker of record. Its Linear reference is the nearest live issue: KEL-79 for F08-T1/T4, KEL-237 for F08-T2/T3, KEL-129 for F08-T7, KEL-75 for F08-T8, and KEL-127 for F08-T5/T6/T9.

## Design facts (labelled)
**Engine process termination (render-process-gone)**
- FACT (git grep at origin/main 8678c0d1): keld-wv registers WebView2 `BrowserProcessExited`. It has no ProcessFailed handler, no WKNavigationDelegate and no WebKitGTK signal plumbing.
  - The macOS slice adds the termination callback to the navigation delegate that F03-T2 introduces. F03-T2 owns that one delegate.
- FACT (Apple receipt, retrieved 2026-10-06): `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` carries no reason.
  - INFERENCE: the macOS reason and exitCode policy is a spec ruling. A fabricated exitCode is a never.
- FACT (Electron v44.4.5 docs, retrieved 2026-10-07): webContents `render-process-gone` is "Emitted when the renderer process unexpectedly disappears. This is normally because it was crashed or killed."
- UNKNOWN: whether Electron emits it when the app itself destroys the window. The draw.io comment is a lead, not a receipt; an F08-T3 oracle cell settles it.

**Named-role exits (child-process-gone)**
- FACT (pinned app.md): `child-process-gone` "does not include renderer processes" and fires when the child "unexpectedly disappears".
- FACT (refuter receipt, Electron source): the event comes only from crash/kill paths. A normal exit only drops the metrics row.
- FACT (origin/main):
  - The role revocation event carries no exit status.
  - SelfTerminationRecord has `exit_code: None` for a signal death and no signal number.
  - So 'killed' and 'crashed' cannot be told apart today.

**Bun-primary death**
- Never mapped to any Electron event.
- A status-zero primary exit ends supervision, which matches Electron's main exiting (FACT per refuter receipt, keld-runtime).

**Facade facts settled by Electron source receipts (parked tickets)**
- crashReporter:
  - `start()` throws 'submitURL must be specified when uploadToServer is true'.
  - Key names of 40 bytes or more raise a process warning and are ignored. The pinned doc says "silently ignored": doc and source contradict, and the oracle decides.
  - Value limits contradict in the doc (127 bytes in two places, 20320 in the addExtraParameter NOTE). The source constant is 20320.
  - getLastCrashReport derives from uploaded reports only.
- Memory units are KiB (`>> 10`).
- percentCPUUsage is divided by the processor count.
- On Linux, ProcessMetric.memory is absent.
- getProcessMemoryInfo sets residentSet only on Linux and Windows.

**contentTracing**
- Never, in production and in dev.
- No map ticket owns the @keld/electron structured compat error shape (code, tier status, tracking issue, workaround).
- FACT: the error-code registry test scans only Rust crates and the CLI templates.

**GPU (closed F08-D6)**
- The getters stay typed-unsupported.
- No GPUFeatureStatus value is emitted without an engine signal that proves it.
- Per-engine honouring is parked to KEL-132, behind two primary receipts: Microsoft's ICoreWebView2EnvironmentOptions AdditionalBrowserArguments page and WebKitGTK's hardware-acceleration-policy page.

## Platform lanes
- macOS (WKWebView) first for F08-T1. F08-T4 records a documented gap on macOS: WKWebView has no public hang signal (INFERENCE, a negative claim).
- Windows (WebView2 ProcessFailed beside the existing BrowserProcessExited observation) and Linux (WebKitGTK web-process-terminated and is-web-process-responsive) each need a real-OS handoff or an explicit documented gap.
- CI, mocks or another OS are never native acceptance.

tickets.title: feat(diagnostics): engine web-content-process termination → webContents/app render-process-gone (macOS WKWebView first; WebView2 ProcessFailed beside the existing BrowserProcessExited observation)
tickets.current_behavior: FACT (origin/main 8678c0d1): keld-wv observes only the WebView2 environment-level BrowserProcessExited (browser-process pid and exit kind, for profile release). It has no WebView2 ProcessFailed handler, no WKNavigationDelegate and no WebKitGTK signal connection. @keld/electron exports only `app`; there is no webContents object to emit on.
tickets.what_to_build:
A Keld-native engine-gone observable per backend, carried to the primary as one host-emitted event over the app link, with constants from the X05-T2 generated source. The facade maps it to WebContents `render-process-gone` and to app `render-process-gone` (event, webContents, details).

macOS: add `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` to the WKNavigationDelegate that F03-T2 introduces. F03-T2 owns that delegate; this ticket adds one callback to it.

Windows: add per-webview ProcessFailed beside the existing BrowserProcessExited observation. Reuse that observation; do not add a second observer.

Linux: connect web-process-terminated.

Reason fidelity is ruled per engine in the spec. FACT: WKWebView gives no reason. FACT (research receipts): WebView2 gives Reason and ExitCode; WebKitGTK gives crashed, exceeded-memory and terminated-by-API. INFERENCE: these map to crashed, oom and killed. The ruling is recorded as ▲ rows, and a fabricated exitCode is never emitted.

The host window survives because the host owns it. Bun-primary death is never mapped.
acceptance_criteria: The F08-T3 webContents `render-process-gone` and app `render-process-gone` cells move from their recorded expected-fail status to pass in this change, with no other cell's expected status edited

On macOS, terminating the window's WebContent process in a fixture emits exactly one WebContents `render-process-gone` and exactly one app `render-process-gone` carrying that webContents, and the BrowserWindow afterwards reports isDestroyed() === false

`details.reason` on macOS equals the value the approved spec rules for WKWebView, and the scoreboard row for RenderProcessGoneDetails records the ▲; `details.exitCode` never carries an engine-unreported number
Destroying the window from the app emits `render-process-gone` if and only if the F08-T3 oracle cell recorded Electron emitting it

On the Windows lane, a renderer ProcessFailed for one webview emits `render-process-gone` on that webContents only, the existing BrowserProcessExited observation stays the single browser-process observer, and a RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE failure kind never emits `render-process-gone`. The lane passes on a real Windows device or is published as an explicit documented gap
Killing the Bun primary emits no Electron-shaped event to any surviving listener
negative_controls: Removing the engine termination callback leaves both cells red, and the runner reports the mismatch against the expected status rather than skipping
A constant reason that ignores the engine fails the WebView2/WebKitGTK reason-mapping cell
Destroying the window from the app must match the recorded oracle; emitting the opposite way fails that cell
Registering a second WebView2 browser-process observer fails the single-observer assertion
Mapping RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE to `render-process-gone` fails the Windows hang-kind cell
Forwarding primary death as `render-process-gone` fails the never-row test

repair.epic_title: compat(update): inert electron-updater adapter for the draw.io proof first; Electron-core autoUpdater, host update channel, keld build translation and bridge recipe parked
repair.epic_body:
## Scope

This epic covers Electron's `autoUpdater` module (1 module, 10 members, macOS and Windows only; FACT: v44.4.5 API doc "Currently, only macOS and Windows are supported"). It also covers the ecosystem updater the corpus actually runs: electron-updater, which draw.io resolves at 6.8.9. FACT: draw.io package-lock integrity sha512-ZhVxM9iG…xTkig==, re-hashed from the npm tarball on 2026-10-07. The epic also owns the packaging-translation and bridge-release questions that arch 04 §2 and §7 assign to migrate.

The first proof needs only one slice. That slice is an inert electron-updater adapter that lets draw.io's top-level updater code evaluate without throwing, contacting a feed or fabricating an outcome (F09-T3 conformance cells, then F09-T1). Everything else is parked behind named owners: the Electron-core facade (F09-T4), the host update channel (F09-T5), keld build translation (F09-T2) and the bridge recipe (F09-T6). One spec fix ships with the first proof (F09-T7) because migrate seeding in that proof must not grant a feed network permission.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, not token-scan counts)

- draw.io (FACT, corpus @2edf9fb): imports the electron-updater package's default export and destructures `autoUpdater` at module top level. At import it unconditionally assigns `logger` (then sets the electron-log transports' levels through it), `autoDownload = false` and `autoInstallOnAppQuit`. It registers `error`, `update-not-available`, `download-progress`, `update-downloaded` and `update-available` listeners at module top level. It calls `setFeedURL({provider:'github', owner, repo, channel?})` after ready, outside the disable guard. It calls `checkForUpdates` at boot and from the menu and IPC only when not disabled, and calls `downloadUpdate` and `quitAndInstall` only from inside listeners. With `DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true` the boot check is skipped and the three updater menu items are removed. It calls the Electron-core `autoUpdater` API at 0 resolved sites.
- Zettlr: has its own got/semver/sha256 downloader that calls shell.openPath on an installer and then app.quit. It calls neither autoUpdater nor electron-updater. Not in this family's tickets; see not-yet-specified.
- electron-quick-start: no updater usage.
- The authoritative list of members touched at import comes from the PANEL-P3 boot trace, which F09-T3 and F09-T1 consume.

## Maturity ladder

- L0 (first proof): F09-T3 cells land red-until-implemented with explicit expected verdicts. F09-T1 flips them: the adapter imports, round-trips its properties, records `setFeedURL` as a ▲ no-op and returns an honest `checkForUpdates` outcome.
- L1 (parked): F09-T5 host update channel. The adapter's real check, download and install path runs over the KEL-53 state machine once KEL-53's live feed-orchestration slice exists.
- L2 (parked): F09-T4 Electron-core facade, split by platform. F09-T6 bridge recipe. F09-T2 keld build translation.

## Linear owners consumed (live status fetched 2026-10-07, read-only)

- KEL-53 (In Progress, Amisha Ramani): host-owned updater. Its spec non-goal says no KIPC, renderer-bridge or permission-manifest change, so it does not own the Bun adapter.
- KEL-270 (In Progress, unassigned): Windows activation journal. Machine-UAC T4d slices S2 29a4cd70, S5 b4b907c3 and S8 ca2e3787 have landed; T4d is not complete.
- KEL-254 (In Progress, Amisha Ramani): installed-root boot and ExpectedAppIdentity.
- KEL-19 (Done, GYLDLAB): live tracking issue for packaging work per decision packet F09-A6 (comment c3dded99). ExpectedAppIdentity T1 landed at e330db8f.
- KEL-15 (Done, GYLDLAB): ratified the arch 04 §2 file set but holds no build-config schema (comment d1137b07).
- KEL-17 (Done, GYLDLAB): migrate RFC; the verb is reserved (KELD-CLI-045).
- KEL-74 (Done, GYLDLAB): evidence schema with a closed `kind` set.
- KEL-237 (In Progress, unassigned): lifecycle corpus runner pattern. Its non-goals exclude new API implementation.
- KEL-102 (In Progress, unassigned): guard enforcement.
- KEL-98 (Done, Amisha Ramani): echo-only codegen.
- KEL-103 (In Progress, Amisha Ramani) and KEL-137 (In Progress, GYLDLAB): macOS host and package cells.
- KEL-141 (Backlog, unassigned).
- KEL-75 (In Progress, unassigned): role spawn spec.
- KEL-127 (Todo, unassigned): program; the fallback Linear reference point for GitHub-tracked tickets.

## Tracker of record (owner decision X06-D7, GitHub #517)

FACT (GitHub #517 comment 6024917784, @0monish, 2026-10-07; issue closed): the owner adopted option D for this program. Each repo-writing ticket is aligned to the nearest live Linear issue whose scope covers it, and the claim happens there. Otherwise the ticket's GitHub issue is the tracker of record: it holds the `## Agent claim` comment (earliest comment wins, assignee mirrors it), status, handoffs and evidence, and no Linear issue is created. The nearest live Linear issue for the surface, falling back to KEL-127, carries a reference link to the GitHub ticket.

Applied here:
- F09-T1 (#491) and F09-T3 (GitHub number assigned at publish) have no live Linear issue whose scope covers them. FACT (#517 body): no live Linear issue owns the `@keld/electron` facade beyond lifecycle, KEL-53's non-goals exclude the bridge, and KEL-237's non-goals exclude compat-surface expansion. So GitHub is their tracker of record, with the reference link on KEL-127.
- F09-T7 aligns to KEL-53, which owns the rule it restores. If KEL-53's scope does not cover the edit, its GitHub issue is the tracker of record.
- The parked tickets follow the same rule when they are pulled.

Residual gap, named in the owner record and not hidden: root AGENTS.md and the workflow claim protocol still describe Linear-only tracking. Until they are amended through the agent-instruction change protocol, #517 and map #391 are the documented exception that agents on this program cite. That amendment is a separate owner-authorized change owned at program level (X06), not an F09 predecessor.

## Design facts (labelled)

- FACT (verified at origin/main 29a4cd70): ExpectedAppIdentityPayload carries only app_id, channel, target and update_public_key. No artifact names a feed-base owner or carrier. F09-A2 is CLOSED (park, option D): the facade exposes no feed base, the eventual field is owned by arch 06 §4a under KEL-53, and the Electron-core getFeedURL cell stays `unknown`.
- FACT (electron-updater 6.8.9): `getFeedURL()` returns "Deprecated. Do not use it.". `setFeedURL` only constructs a provider client and does not contact it. `checkForUpdates()` resolves null with no event when the app is not packaged and dev update config is not forced. When a check fails it emits `error` and rejects the same promise. `downloadUpdate` before a check rejects with "Please check update first". `quitAndInstall` with nothing downloaded dispatches `error` and does not quit. On success, `quitAndInstall` emits `before-quit-for-update` on Electron-core's `autoUpdater` object, not on itself.
- FACT (PANEL-D14, closed): setFeedURL is a recorded ▲ no-op and never throws. A throw would route through draw.io's safeUpdaterCall to a user-facing "Update Error" dialog. Migrate writes `DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true` into the host-declared role environment. Updater code never fabricates `update-not-available`. Real activation stays KEL-53.
- Declared role environment, one owner: F01-T4 owns the field, its validation and its delivery at spawn, as an explicit KEL-75 schema amendment behind a permission-model gate. X02-T1's key→owner map points the keld.config.ts key at F01-T4, and X02-T3 writes the value. FACT (keld-runtime at origin/main 29a4cd70): RoleConfig already sets explicit per-generation environment keys and removals. That is a delivery primitive F01-T4 can reuse, not a schema owner. INFERENCE (keld-runtime read at b4b907c3): the macOS non-strict spawn path does not clear the inherited environment, so "not inherited from the operator shell" is not enforced there today.
- FACT: Electron's documented quitAndInstall order (close windows, then app.quit; `before-quit-for-update` first) is the native macOS and MSIX path only. Windows Squirrel calls processStart and then app.quit without emitting `before-quit-for-update`; refuter receipt from Electron v44.4.5 source. Ordering cells are therefore split by facade × platform (F09-T4, F09-T5). draw.io has no demand on that ordering.
- FACT: KEL-53 has no headless health boot. A candidate must start, reach Ready and stay alive for 30 s. electron-updater's install-at-quit without relaunch is therefore a recorded ▲ (F09-T5).
- CONTRADICTION: arch 03 §5 has migrate seed "autoUpdater → net to feed URL", while KEL-53 says application permissions cannot grant update authority and arch 06 §4a makes the host the only feed client. F09-T7 fixes the arch 03 text.
- FACT: KEL-74 has no ecosystem kind, and X03-A6 (closed) puts no package cells in the product denominator. Adapter cells are Keld facade conformance cells in a showcase-panel corpus that uses an existing kind.

## Platform lanes

- F09-T1 and F09-T3 are Bun-only and platform-independent. They run first on macOS, the first-proof lane.
- The Electron-core facade (F09-T4) has separate macOS, Windows-Squirrel and MSIX cells. Linux is out of scope because Electron has no built-in Linux auto-update.
- Bridge rows (F09-T6): Windows x64 NSIS is blocked for draw.io until KEL-270 T4d completes. windows-arm64 has no Keld target cell. macOS is blocked on KEL-137 and KEL-103. Linux AppImage, deb, rpm and pacman each need an owner decision.

tickets.title: feat(update): inert electron-updater 6.8.9 adapter for the draw.io proof (import-time surface, recorded no-op setFeedURL, honest check outcome)
tickets.what_to_build:
Build a Keld-owned package that stands in for the `electron-updater` specifier. Migrate swaps it in as a dependency replacement in the app manifest: X02-T3 owns that swap, under the single-resolver rule closed in X02-A1. The package exposes the AppUpdater subset that draw.io touches, as listed by the PANEL-P3 trace. It must evaluate at import with no host frames and no network or filesystem I/O, and must never fabricate an updater outcome.

Behaviour, mirroring electron-updater 6.8.9 wherever the upstream shape can be honoured without a host updater:
- A default export carrying `autoUpdater`, which is an EventEmitter.
- A `logger` accessor that stores and returns the identical object; null yields a no-op logger.
- `autoDownload`, `autoInstallOnAppQuit` and `autoRunAppAfterInstall` are plain booleans with no side effect.
- `setFeedURL(string or options)` returns undefined. It never throws, constructs no client, and stores nothing any host path reads. This is a ▲: the feed is host-declared and the app feed is ignored.
- `getFeedURL()` returns upstream's deprecated literal.
- `checkForUpdates()` mirrors upstream's packaged gate and reads app.isPackaged from F01-T4. When not packaged it resolves null with no event. When packaged and no host updater exists, it emits exactly one `error` carrying a newly allocated registry code and rejects the same promise.
- `downloadUpdate()` before any update is offered rejects, as upstream's "check first" does.
- `quitAndInstall()` with nothing staged emits one `error` and never quits.
- Never emitted: `update-available`, `update-not-available`, `download-progress`, `update-downloaded`, `checking-for-update`.
acceptance_criteria: Every F09-T3 match cell flips from its recorded expected verdict to pass in this change, and every F09-T3 ▲ cell carries its divergence verdict; no F09-T3 cell is skipped, retried or left silently red
Under Bun 1.4.2, the default-import form followed by destructuring `autoUpdater` yields an EventEmitter, and the app-link frame count attributable to the adapter during import is 0
Assigning an object to `logger` and reading it back returns the identical object (strict equality), so property writes made through it land on the assigned logger
`setFeedURL` called with draw.io's github provider options and with a plain string returns undefined both times, throws nothing, opens no socket and writes no file

A fixture that replays the PANEL-P3-recorded draw.io updater call sequence with `DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true` set explicitly in the role environment makes zero `checkForUpdates` calls and receives zero `error` events
The same replay with the variable absent and app.isPackaged false makes `checkForUpdates` resolve null with zero events

With the variable absent, app.isPackaged true and no host updater, `checkForUpdates` emits exactly one `error` whose code is a registry-allocated code outside KELD-COMPAT-001..009 and KELD-UPDATE-*, and the returned promise rejects
Across every case above, no `update-not-available`, `update-available` or `update-downloaded` event is ever emitted
`quitAndInstall()` with nothing staged emits exactly one `error` and app.quit is never called
negative_controls: Making setFeedURL throw fails the setFeedURL no-throw cell and the replay fixture (draw.io's safeUpdaterCall would open its Update Error dialog)
Returning a fresh wrapper from the logger getter fails the identity cell
Emitting update-not-available from checkForUpdates with no host updater fails the never-fabricate cell
Removing the isPackaged gate makes the unpackaged replay emit an error and fails the unpackaged-check cell
Calling app.quit from quitAndInstall with nothing staged fails the no-quit cell
Reusing a KELD-UPDATE-* code for the no-host-updater error fails the code-provenance assertion
blocked_by_external: Approved spec for the adapter package name and its pinned upstream surface (electron-updater 6.8.9, npm integrity recorded in draw.io's lockfile). It does not exist yet. First action: write it under the spec template and post the `## Agent claim` comment on GitHub #491, the tracker of record

Error-code allocation in the canonical registry for the no-host-updater error. The registry test scans Rust and tool trees only, so the spec must say how the TypeScript emitter is held to the registry

Reference link to GitHub #491 on KEL-127 (Todo, unassigned), titled with the number and 'tracker of record: GitHub', per #517 rule 3. The orchestrator is the single Linear writer; its presence is not verified here. First check: the link appears on KEL-127
tickets.linear_owner: Tracker of record: GitHub #491, per the X06-D7 owner decision (GitHub #517 comment 6024917784, option D). No live Linear issue's scope covers the adapter; the reference link lives on KEL-127 (Todo, unassigned). Adjacent: KEL-53 (In Progress, Amisha Ramani) owns real updater authority
tickets.platforms: Bun-only and platform-independent; run first on macOS (first-proof lane); Windows/Linux run the same Bun tests
electron_members_covered: AppUpdater events: error, update-available, update-not-available, download-progress, update-downloaded (listener registration only)
tickets.current_behavior: No updater surface exists: @keld/electron exports only `app`, and no package in the workspace answers the `electron-updater` specifier (verified at origin/main 29a4cd70).
tickets.key_interfaces: The Keld-owned adapter package; @keld/electron app.isPackaged (F01-T4); the migrate dependency replacement (X02-T3); F09-T3 conformance cells in the KEL-237 corpus-runner pattern.
tickets.out_of_scope: Any host update channel, feed contact, download, staging or activation (F09-T5); the Electron-core autoUpdater facade (F09-T4); feed-base reporting (F09-A2 closed: parked under KEL-53 / arch 06 §4a); comparison of the setFeedURL argument with a build config (no schema and no consumer); declaring or delivering the role environment variable (F01-T4).
tickets.notes:
Adjacent owners (one owner per atom):
- The declared role environment (its field, the validation that rejects KELD_* names, and delivery at spawn): F01-T4, as an explicit KEL-75 schema amendment behind a permission-model gate. KEL-75 is In Progress and unassigned (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07). X02-T1's key→owner map lists the keld.config.ts key as the F01-T4 payload field.
- Writing `DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true` into that field: X02-T3, the migrate output.
- Running draw.io's real boot as product cells: X02-T4, which should take an edge on this ticket.

FACT (keld-runtime at origin/main 29a4cd70): RoleConfig already sets explicit per-generation environment keys and removals. That is a delivery primitive F01-T4 can reuse, not the schema owner.

INFERENCE: delivering this variable as an environment key is consistent with the KEL-75 spec. That spec keeps KELD_APP_LINK as the sole bootstrap variable and forbids grant exceptions arising from an environment value, and the declared variable carries no authority.

INFERENCE (keld-runtime read at b4b907c3): the macOS non-strict spawn path inherits the operator environment. The replay fixture therefore sets or clears the variable explicitly and never relies on the shell.

UNKNOWN: whether the first-proof activation cell runs with isPackaged false (`keld dev`) or true (installed root). It is decided by F01-T4 and X02-T4, which is why both cases are covered.

If the variable is absent and the app is packaged, draw.io's Update Error dialog appears at boot. That is the honest outcome, and it would fail the activation cell, so the env declaration is a product-cell dependency, not an adapter one.
