repair.epic_title: program(conformance): evidence rules and differential oracle harness — one Electron pin per corpus, shared corpus-manifest owner, red-until-implemented cells, pinned Electron recorder, Keld replayer, comparator, lanes
repair.epic_body:
## Scope

X01 owns the evidence machinery that every Electron-compat claim passes through. It works in two layers with different milestones.

1. **First-proof evidence rules** (X01-T3 spec, X01-T4 shared owner; milestone first-proof). These are: one Electron oracle pin per corpus, with the v44.4.5 tag commit 694f45852a0f1726cd23bfd379854de489cccb65 as the default for every new corpus; a per-cell citation of the pinned doc; red-until-implemented cells; the rule that observed-only means `unknown`; the meaning of `artifact.sha256`; the authority-profile label; and one shared corpus-manifest and exact-bytes owner in keld-compat. Every new corpus reuses that owner. The first-proof consumers are the conformance entries (F01-T1, F03-T1, F04-T1), the X02-T5 product cell contract (consumes X01-T3), the X02-T4 product corpus manifest (consumes X01-T3 and X01-T4), and the X02-T6 scoring run, which runs the corpus under the X01-T4 validator. None of these first-proof consumers gates on X01-T1: they need the rules and the helpers, not the two-arm recorder.
2. **Differential oracle harness** (X01-T1 spec and X01-T2 lifecycle tracer at milestone next; X01-T5 scheduled lane parked). Arm A records Keld-owned fixtures under the SHA-256-verified Electron 44.4.5 binary. Arm B replays the same unmodified fixtures under `@keld/electron`. A comparator in keld-compat emits one KEL-74 record per cell. INFERENCE (from their ticket text; edges owned by those units): the next-milestone conformance tickets F03-T6 (recorded undocumented behaviour) and F08-T3 (an UNKNOWN destroy-time render-process-gone oracle cell) genuinely need recorded Electron observations, so they stay on X01-T1.

The oracle is the pinned doc sentence. A golden transcript is only evidence-of-record (decision X01-A1; it survived both refuters).

FACT: X01 owns no Electron API member. The compat matrix assigns all 2,128 members of the 180 entities in the v44.4.5 API model to F01–F09. X01 records evidence for the cells those families define. It never claims coverage itself.

## Corpus demand

- FACT: the first proof is drawio-desktop on macOS under the explicit legacy profile. It consumes two things from X01: conformance entries that cite v44.4.5 sentences (F01-T1, F03-T1 and F04-T1 are first-proof conformance tickets), and a second corpus (`electron-apps-v0`, panel product: X02-T5 cell contract, X02-T4 manifest, X02-T6 scoring run that flips the cells). Neither needs recorded Electron goldens, because product cells reuse the KEL-237 runner pattern. So no edge from X02-T4, X02-T5 or X02-T6 to X01-T1 or X01-T2 is a real gate; their real X01 edges are X01-T3 (rules) and X01-T4 (helpers and validator).
- FACT (package manifests of the pinned corpus clones): the declared Electron ranges are draw.io ^44.2.0, electron-quick-start ^44.4.3 and Zettlr ^43.6.0. Zettlr's range excludes 44.4.5, so the Zettlr proof needs either a second pin or a recorded out-of-range run. That question is parked until Zettlr work starts.
- FACT (recount on the pinned clones, 2026-10-07): literal `app.exit(` call sites are draw.io 3 (export-mode and error paths, not on the four-step workflow) and Zettlr 2. draw.io has no `<webview>` demand: every hit is `webviewTag: false` or a `will-attach-webview` preventDefault. No recorder cell is motivated by either.
- INFERENCE: the token-scan usage files credit a generic event name to every entity that declares it. Deduplicate by receiver type before letting event counts drive cell priority.

## Maturity ladder

The ladder rungs are report vocabulary over the four KEL-74 verdicts. They are never a second verdict set. FACT: the evidence parser accepts only `pass|fail|unknown|waived`, and records reject unknown fields.

- **BEHAVIOR_MATCH**: the Keld transcript equals the golden under declared normalisers on at least one OS. A cell with no doc citation (observed-only) is recorded `unknown`, with its oracle id naming the unspecified path. It is never `pass`.
- **CONFORMANCE_PASS**: a cited pinned sentence, a Keld-owned test independent of any transcript diff, and a named negative control. The cell is `pass` per OS lane. An unrun lane stays `unknown` or carries an explicit ▲.
- **CORPUS_VERIFIED**: the same observable is matched in a committed corpus app through migrate + dev smoke. It goes on panel product only after that corpus id is documented as committed (X02-T6 adds it in the same reviewed change that flips the cells).

Correction: the published epic called this "the ladder every family uses". That contradicted the family epics, which own L0–L3 maturity targets. X01-T3 records the mapping: a family L2 exit requires CONFORMANCE_PASS cells, and a family L3 exit requires CORPUS_VERIFIED rows.

## Tracker of record and Linear owners consumed (Linear and GitHub, fetched 2026-10-07, read-only)

Owner rule consumed as text, not as a blocker: X06-D7 (#517) is CLOSED (closed 2026-10-06T20:32:52Z) with the owner decision recorded by @0monish: align each repo-writing ticket to the nearest live Linear issue whose scope covers it and claim there; otherwise the GitHub issue is the tracker of record (claim, status, handoffs and evidence on GitHub, earliest claim comment wins) and no Linear issue is created; every GitHub ticket is referenced by a link on the nearest live Linear issue for its surface, falling back to KEL-127. The map orchestrator is the single Linear writer for those reference links.

- **KEL-74**, Done (GYLDLAB): evidence schema, parser and `score()`. Consumed unchanged, as landed on origin/main 8678c0d1. The documented committed-product list is empty.
- **KEL-237**, In Progress, unassigned: the lifecycle corpus, landed in b36b0ada (PR #242). It provides the manifest, the exact-bytes digest assertion with its one-byte mutation control, and the execution-admission checks. Its non-goals exclude new Electron API implementation and compatibility-surface expansion. Under X06-D7 it is the aligned tracker of record for X01-T3 and X01-T4. INFERENCE: that work falls inside the manifest contract KEL-237 already owns. If the KEL-237 owner contests this, those two tickets fall back to their GitHub issues as tracker of record, linked from KEL-237. KEL-237 is also the nearest live surface carrying the Linear reference links for X01-T1 and X01-T2 (INFERENCE).
- **KEL-77**, In Progress, unassigned: the VS Code extension-host differential harness. Its spec supplies the shape X01-T1 consumes (§4.1 three-state rule and mirror-oracle rejection, §4.3 fixture-set digest, §4.5 field table). It is not X01's owner.
- **KEL-78**, In Progress (GYLDLAB): profile states `unverified | legacy | strict`. Legacy requires an explicit Keld declaration. `unverified` has no KEL-74 authority value.
- **KEL-81**, Done, unassigned: changed-path CI routing. It is not live, so it cannot be the tracker of record for a new scheduled lane.
- **KEL-127**, Todo, unassigned: the program fallback for Linear reference links under X06-D7 (used by X01-T5).
- **GitHub tracker of record (no covering live Linear issue):** X01-T1, X01-T2 and X01-T5. Each is claimed on its own GitHub issue per X06-D7. Who can act: any agent may post the `## Agent claim` comment on the GitHub issue; the orchestrator posts the Linear reference link.

## Design facts (labelled)

- FACT: the corpus manifest contract is test-local today and has no shared owner. The lifecycle validator:
  - parses a deny-unknown-fields manifest whose corpus-level upstream block carries only an `app` doc URL;
  - hard-asserts the pin 44.3.0 @07e46071;
  - admits exactly two test targets;
  - allows `expected_verdict` only as `pass`, or as `fail` with an intentional divergence.
  No red-until-implemented state exists.
- FACT: the KEL-77 §4.3 fixture-set digest is a private helper inside the keld-runtime test target. In keld-compat, sha2 is a dev-dependency only, and the crate manifest records that a production sha2 dependency was rejected.
- FACT: `artifact.sha256` has two live meanings. KEL-237 records carry the manifest digest; KEL-77 §4.5 uses the fixture-directory digest.
- FACT: the published lifecycle records are bound per OS to hosted-CI receipts of PR #242. Re-pinning that corpus therefore needs fresh receipts on all three OS. It is not a text edit.
- FACT: diffing the `app` doc between Electron commit 07e46071 (44.3.0) and the v44.4.5 tag finds one prose change, in the `getPath` sessionData description. The other hunks are example formatting. The lifecycle sentences the three live cells cite are unchanged.
- FACT: `@keld/electron` exports only `app` plus `isCallError`/`KeldCallError`. keld-cli has no `--headless` flag or verb. No window registry exists. So the Keld arm has no BrowserWindow, preload or renderer, and the first harness cells must be main-process only.
- FACT (pinned ESM tutorial, byte-identical at the v44.4.5 tag, fetched 2026-10-07):
  - an ESM main entry is supported when the nearest package manifest has `"type": "module"`;
  - "Preload scripts will ignore `type: module` fields";
  - sandboxed preloads run without an ESM context;
  - "your app may be `ready` before your code executes".
- FACT (npm registry and the release SHASUMS256, fetched 2026-10-07): electron@44.4.5 has dist.shasum 0be094f8e783febba75d591106f5c61c1e511b70 and no install scripts, so the binary downloads lazily on first run. Zip SHA-256 values: darwin-arm64 a212eee63ba2f45fd83bd28f77a3e3313a336ad17a4c25adf617942eef5e0e2c, linux-x64 04586a0ec46c3283fbdaef85530f561f71f0b5e136ad0cb9ef63683615609780, win32-x64 11c395820a5aaa8ebcc0686b476d0ac98a730274ebfbdc8cf5538a7c2815cb5d.
- FACT (refuter receipt from Electron's pinned test workflow, retrieved 2026-10-06, not re-fetched): Electron reruns its own tests up to three times on every non-ASAN lane. Its macOS lane sets ApplePersistenceIgnoreState, because repeated abnormal exits make AppKit's reopen alert hang `app.whenReady()` (electron#51462).
- FACT: the Keld repository has two workflows and neither is scheduled. `CI required` aggregates PR and push jobs only.
- FACT: the live lifecycle test waits on stdout markers with an 8-second kill-switch timeout, then panics without killing the spawned Bun child. A std child process is not killed on drop.
- UNKNOWN: whether Electron 44.4.5's main-process quit order is identical run to run, and which fields vary. X01-A5 (#411) owns this. Its experiment has not run; #411 holds only the decision packet.
- UNKNOWN: whether renderer rows interleave stably with main rows (X01-A5 arm D, a lead for X01-T1).
- UNKNOWN: the recorder's runner cost and display needs on hosted Windows and Linux.

## Platform lanes

- **PR lane:** the existing three-OS matrix, running manifest validation and Keld-arm replay only, offline and deterministic. Each OS is scored separately. The Electron arm never runs here.
- **Recorder:** a macOS arm64 developer command first (X01-T2), using the verified zip.
- **Parked (X01-T5):** a Linux recorder under a virtual display, a Windows recorder, and the scheduled drift lane with its failure sink.

There is no recorder, replayer, comparator or golden transcript. The KEL-77 fixture-set digest is a private helper in the keld-runtime test target.
tickets.what_to_build:
Write a spec (spec template) for the two-arm harness. It consumes the X01-T3 evidence rules and the X01-A5 receipt, and covers:
(a) Fixture packaging: an ESM main entry with module type; when a renderer exists, a CommonJS preload with the .cjs extension; a static page. Fixtures are partitioned per family so that a missing `@keld/electron` export cannot mask other cells. Lifecycle listeners are registered synchronously before any top-level await.
(b) Electron arm identity: tag commit, npm dist shasum, and per-OS/arch release zip SHA-256 from the pinned SHASUMS256 line. The recorder runs the verified zip directly, never through a lazy npx download, and installs outside the digested fixture tree. The macOS recorder prep is copied from Electron's pinned test workflow.
(c) Transcript row shape: process-local seq, process, kind, name, canonical args. Timing is diagnostic and never compared.
(d) Normalisers are declared per cell, empty by default, and each is justified by an observed X01-A5 raw diff. Comparison is strict within one process's sequence plus declared causal edges.
(e) One owner for the KEL-77 §4.3 fixture-set digest, with the KEL-77 caller migrated, and the meaning of `artifact.sha256` for harness corpora.
(f) Each arm is a child process killed and reaped on timeout. A Keld-arm module-link failure is recorded `fail` with a KELD code.
(g) Lanes: PR replay only. The recorder is a developer command. The scheduled lane is X01-T5. Oracle drift enters the gate only through a reviewed PR that updates goldens, receipts and cells together.
tickets.key_interfaces: KEL-74 evidence records and score(); the shared corpus-manifest owner from X01-T4; the KEL-77 differential spec §4.1/§4.3/§4.5; the existing Keld-arm Bun fixture spawn pattern; X01-A5 receipt.
acceptance_criteria: Every section of the spec template is filled; no section is empty or a placeholder (approval is the PR gate, not a criterion)

The rejected-alternatives section names each of: running or translating Electron's spec tree, the golden transcript as sole oracle, wall-clock timing comparison, re-recording goldens from the Keld arm, a CDP/Playwright driver, TypeScript fixtures behind a transpile step, and lazy npx download at record time
The spec states exactly one meaning of `artifact.sha256` for harness corpora and names the other live meaning as rejected for them
The normaliser table cites an X01-A5 receipt observation on every row, and the spec lists event name, kind, order, Error.message and exit code as never normalised
The Electron identity table lists the tag commit, the npm dist shasum and the zip SHA-256 for darwin-arm64, linux-x64 and win32-x64, and each value equals the pinned release SHASUMS256 line
The fixture-set digest has exactly one named owner, and the spec names the migration of the KEL-77 caller to it
The spec states that a cell with no doc citation is emitted only as `unknown`, and that the ladder rungs never appear as record verdicts

Deleting 're-recording goldens from the Keld arm' from the rejected-alternatives section fails the rejected-alternatives criterion

tickets.what_to_build:
Write a short spec (spec template) under the claim on this ticket's GitHub issue. It fixes the evidence rules that the first-proof conformance entries and the product corpus must share, before any of them lands:
(1) Pin. A corpus manifest carries exactly one Electron upstream pin. Every new corpus pins the v44.4.5 tag commit. A cell's oracle id and revision must match its corpus pin. A pin bump is one reviewed change that re-cites every cell and regenerates its receipts. `electron-lifecycle-v0` stays frozen at its 44.3.0 pin until KEL-237 deliberately re-records it; new v44.4.5 lifecycle cells go in a new corpus id.
(2) Doc citation. Each cell cites the doc page at the pinned commit plus a digest of the quoted sentence.
(3) Red-until-implemented. The cell is `expected_verdict: fail` with the implementing ticket key, kept distinct from an intentional divergence. Its mapped test asserts the current behaviour and passes. The implementing change inverts the test and flips the cell to `pass`.
(4) A cell with no doc citation is emitted only as `unknown`. Ladder rungs are report vocabulary, mapped to family L2/L3 exits.
(5) Each corpus declares which digest `artifact.sha256` carries. First-proof corpora use the exact committed manifest bytes, which is the live KEL-237 convention.
(6) `legacy_sandbox_off` labels a corpus-app row only when the run carries the explicit Keld legacy declaration. A run in the KEL-78 `unverified` state emits no record. No value is invented, and the vocabulary gap is raised with the KEL-78 owner.
(7) Engine identity is declared per corpus.
(8) One shared manifest, exact-bytes and execution-admission owner lives in keld-compat's test support. The rejected alternative is a public keld-compat module, which would add public API and move sha2 into production dependencies.

repair.epic_title: program(migrate): read-only analyzer, one package-manifest alias, a hand-authored draw.io first-proof artefact, a report without percentages, and the electron-apps-v0 product corpus
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
This epic covers `keld migrate`: read-only analysis by default and reversible writes only under `--write`. It also covers the one module alias an app needs (a package-manifest dependency keyed `electron`), the output contract for the Keld config files, the report wording, and the product corpus (`electron-apps-v0`) that scores real apps through the KEL-74 evidence schema. The first proof needs four slices from this epic: the output-contract spec (X02-T1), a hand-authored draw.io artefact that meets it (X02-T3), the corpus contract spec and manifest with red-until-implemented cells (X02-T5, X02-T4), and the scoring run on macOS (X02-T6), which is the only ticket that flips the corpus cells. The analyzer (X02-T7 spec, X02-T2 first slice, X02-T9 remaining blocker classes) and the `--write` generator (X02-T8) are `next`. The first proof does not need them: draw.io's channels and webPreferences can be enumerated by hand from one main file.

X02 owns no rows of the 2,128-member Electron v44.4.5 API matrix. Every API member is assigned to F01–F09. The entities X02 owns are the migration surfaces. Each one is either covered by a ticket below or listed under never / out_of_scope / not_yet_specified.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, not token-scan leads)
- FACT (corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb, grep 2026-10-07): the main file registers 24 distinct literal renderer→main channels through `ipcMain.on/once`. A 25th registration, `log`, is commented out. The preload forwards channel names chosen by the page, so the preload does not constrain the channel set. UNKNOWN: which of the 24 the web app actually sends, because the webapp submodule is empty in the clone. PANEL-P3 produces that list.
- FACT (same commit): `requestSingleInstanceLock()` runs inside the `app.whenReady().then` callback, which is after ready. The published research said "pre-ready, same pattern as Zettlr", which is wrong for draw.io. Zettlr calls it before ready.
- FACT (same commit): `DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE` is read from `process.env` at module top level. `autoUpdater.setFeedURL({provider:'github',…})` is called outside the disable guard. electron-updater, electron-store, electron-log and electron-context-menu all import the bare `electron` name.
- FACT (same commit): `shell.openExternal` has two literal https origins (Help menu items) and one dynamic wrapper. `app.getPath` is called with `userData` and `documents`. `disableBlinkFeatures` is set on every window. The `start` script is `electron .`, five scripts run electron-builder, and the app has no tsconfig.
- FACT (PANEL-D15, resolved counts): draw.io has 0 sendSync and 1 `showMessageBoxSync`, on the close path. Counts from the receiver-blind token scan (for example `WebContents.replace 22`, or the `<webview>` hits that are all `webviewTag: false`) are leads, not demand.
- FACT (refuter receipt): Zettlr's forge config requires a git-hash helper that spawns a shell when the config is loaded, and its `generateAssets` hook spawns the pandoc download while packaging. This is why app configs are never executed.

## Maturity ladder (owned by X01-EPIC)
BEHAVIOR_MATCH → CONFORMANCE_PASS → CORPUS_VERIFIED. Ticket targets: L0 = approved spec; L1 = implemented with tests on macOS; L3 = CORPUS_VERIFIED cells in `electron-apps-v0` (panel `product`), with `authority_profile: legacy_sandbox_off` printed. Analyzer counts never become a cell: `OperationKind` is the closed set install / activation / primary_workflow / full_feature.

## Linear owners consumed (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07; read-only)
- KEL-17 "RFC: Electron compat layer and migration path": **Done** (GYLDLAB, 2026-07-10). The reserved `migrate` verb's tracking issue points here. Its acceptance criterion "`keld migrate` UX specified" closed without a spec file. The only UX text is the architecture 04 §1 sample, which X02-T1 corrects.
- KEL-19 "RFC: CLI design": **Done** (GYLDLAB). Its live comment activity is the Windows ExpectedAppIdentity container (T1 landed e330db8f; T2 is PR #515), not migrate. It is the forward owner of the keld.build.ts schema per the F09-A6 resolution.
- KEL-15 config RFC: **Done** (GYLDLAB). There is no schema text beyond architecture 04 §2 (comment d1137b07).
- KEL-74 evidence schema and scorer: **Done** (GYLDLAB). `DOCUMENTED_COMMITTED_PRODUCT_CORPORA` is empty, so no product percentage can be printed.
- KEL-237 lifecycle corpus: **In Progress**, unassigned. Its non-goals exclude product denominators and any expansion of the compatibility surface, so it is the pattern this epic reuses, not the owner. The orchestrator's bridge comment c13866bd records the separate `electron-apps-v0` manifest.
- KEL-127 program direction: **Todo**, unassigned. Its non-goals say it 'owns sequencing only; each code/spec concern gets its own issue', so it is the Linear reference for X02's migrate tickets, not their tracker of record. Its only attachment is the map #391 link. It carries the sentence "analyzer starts read-only, reports compatibility/security/engine/native-dependency blockers separately and emits reviewable reversible changes only after authorization".
- KEL-72 @keld/electron bootstrap: **Done**, unassigned. KEL-215 native-addon rows: **Done**, unassigned.
- KEL-78 strict profile: **In Progress** (GYLDLAB). Its spec says the `profile: "legacy"` key "does not exist today", and none of its tasks T1–T7 names that key as a deliverable. On the map, X03-T5 owns the key's single location and grammar (a spec amendment under KEL-78) and X03-T7 owns its parser.
- KEL-75 role spawn contract: In Progress, unassigned. FACT (KEL-75 spec at origin/main 29a4cd70): `KELD_APP_LINK` remains the sole child bootstrap variable, and a role-specific capability exception cannot arise from an environment value. KEL-102 guard enforcement: In Progress, unassigned. KEL-141 prebuilt distribution: **Backlog**, unassigned. KEL-103 signed macOS host: In Progress (Amisha Ramani).

### Tracker of record (owner decision #517, adopted as X06-D7)
- FACT (GitHub #517, closed; owner comment by 0monish, 2026-10-06T20:32Z): align each repo-writing ticket to the nearest live Linear issue whose scope covers it and claim there. Otherwise the GitHub issue is the tracker of record: the `## Agent claim` block is posted as a GitHub comment (earliest comment wins, the assignee mirrors it), status and evidence stay on GitHub, and no Linear issue is created. The nearest live Linear issue for the surface (fallback KEL-127) carries a link to the GitHub ticket. This comment supersedes the option-C recommendation in #517's own body.
- FACT (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07): no live Linear issue's scope covers X02. KEL-17 and KEL-19 are Done. KEL-237's non-goals exclude compatibility-surface expansion. KEL-127 owns sequencing only. So every X02 ticket's GitHub issue is its tracker of record. Linear references: KEL-127 for the migrate tickets (X02-T1, T2, T3, T7, T8, T9) and KEL-237 for the corpus tickets (X02-T4, T5, T6). Choosing KEL-237 as the nearest corpus surface is an INFERENCE.
- FACT (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07): neither reference link exists yet. KEL-127's only attachment is the map #391, and KEL-237's is #179. Posting the links is the orchestrator's write (single writer). A missing link does not block a GitHub claim.
- Residual gap, named by the owner on #517: root AGENTS.md ('Features require an approved spec plus Linear (KELD)') and the workflow's claim section still describe Linear-only tracking. Until they are amended through the `.agents/instructions.md` protocol, #517 and map #391 are the documented exception that every claimant must cite. That amendment is a separate owner-authorized change and does not gate X02 tickets.
- Consequence: the X02 specs X02-T1, X02-T5 and X02-T7 are `ready-for-agent`. The feature and task tickets stay `needs-spec` because their specs have not landed, not because an owner is missing.

## Design facts (labelled)
- FACT (X02-A1, closed): there is one resolver, a package-manifest dependency keyed `electron` pointing at @keld/electron. It uses `npm:` once the package is published and `file:`/`link:` before that, with package exports mapping all five specifiers to one entry. There is no Bun plugin. The bunfig `[alias]` is inert on Bun 1.4.2, so migrate never writes it. tsconfig `paths.electron` gives Bun-only, silently wrong resolution and can create two module instances, so migrate never writes it and removes it if present. The arch 04 §2/§3 erratum lands in the X02-T1 spec PR.
- FACT (refuter probes, Bun 1.4.2): @keld/electron is not consumable as a package today. It exports only `.`, as ESM TypeScript, and it imports @keld/api by a relative path outside the package. With no node_modules present, Bun auto-installs the real `electron` package and returns a string with no error. Owner of the self-contained, CJS-requirable entry, the subpath exports and the fail-closed role spawn: X03-T1 (adjacent atom, not X02). X02 owns only the manifest edit and the installed-tree check.
- FACT: the alias applies to the Bun main role only. Renderer and preload `electron` are the injected compat script, owned by F07-T1.
- FACT: replacing `electron` breaks every script that launches the Electron binary or electron-builder. The migrate edit rewrites or removes those scripts in the same edit.
- FACT (keld-guard at origin/main 29a4cd70): the live manifest parser ignores the top-level `windows` key, and `keld_permissions_explain` refuses `channel` with KELD-MCP014. Seeded channel grants grant nothing until the KEL-102 amendment from F04-A1's resolution lands. Under that amendment, entries are exact-literal `el:<channel>`, a miss is KELD-GUARD003, and migrate refuses wildcards. The grant list comes from main-side literal ipcMain registrations; a non-literal registration is reported as unenumerable. X02 owns the migrate side and F04-T3 owns the evaluator.
- FACT: fs scopes containing `$` are rejected as "unexpanded `$VAR` scopes are not serviceable", so migrate never emits them. Under legacy, F01-A4 (closed) keeps `userData` at Electron's default path with raw node:fs and containment forfeited, so the first proof seeds no fs grants. Strict seeding is parked under KEL-78.
- FACT (F09-A6, closed): keld.build.ts is not generated for the first proof. The report prints "not generated: keld build is reserved (KELD-CLI-045)". No keld.compat.ts schema or reader exists, so it is not generated either.
- FACT (PANEL-D14, closed): electron-updater is aliased to the F09-T1 adapter, whose `setFeedURL` is a recorded no-op, and `DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true` goes into a declared role environment.
- FACT (KEL-75 spec at origin/main 29a4cd70): no live schema carries a declared role environment, and `KELD_APP_LINK` is the sole child bootstrap variable. The declared role environment has one owner, F01-T4, as an explicit KEL-75 spawn-contract amendment under a permission-model gate. The amendment rejects names beginning `KELD_`, and the field carries no authority. X02 only writes the declaration and never defines the field.
- FACT (KEL-78 spec): the explicit `profile: "legacy"` key does not exist today. X03-T5 decides its grammar and its single location (it recommends keld.permissions.jsonc). X03-T7 parses the key and stamps `authority_profile` on records. X02 writes the key into whichever file X03-T5 selects and never decides the location.

Write the approved spec for product-corpus cells.

repair.epic_title: program(runtime): Node/Bun runtime layer for migrated mains — one `electron` module, main-role process facts before entry, explicit legacy profile key; native addons and child_process parked
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
What this unit owns for a migrated Electron main running on a Bun role:
(1) the five Electron module specifiers (`electron`, `electron/main`, `electron/renderer`, `electron/common`, `electron/utility`) resolving to one `@keld/electron` object for ESM and CJS, from app code and from node_modules (X03-T1). The mechanism is closed decision X02-A1, consumed as binding text and not re-opened.
(2) the main-role `process.*` Electron facts, installed before the app entry evaluates. These consume the F01-T4 boot payload (X03-T4).
(3) the explicit Keld `legacy` profile key that the first proof depends on (X03-T5 spec, X03-T7 implementation).
(4) the conformance entries for (1) and (2) (X03-T3).
(5) next: Bun auto-install disabled at role spawn (X03-T6).
(6) parked: the native-addon policy record (X03-T2).
Ownership boundaries:
- F01-T4 owns the boot payload's content, its delivery and its fail-closed behaviour.
- F07-T1 owns the renderer/preload `process` object.
- X02-T3 owns the app-side manifest edit (writing the alias, removing tsconfig `paths.electron`).
- F09-T1 owns the electron-updater adapter alias.
child_process under strict is decided and parked (X03-A5, owner KEL-76). The `package` panel is decided against (X03-A6).

Verification stamp: current-behaviour lines were re-checked at Keld origin/main 8678c0d1 on 2026-10-07. The X03 surfaces (the @keld/electron package and its fixtures, role spawn env, keld-compat evidence schema, keld-guard admission, KEL-78 spec, arch 04/05) are byte-unchanged since b4b907c3, where the batch-2 refuters verified them.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites; scanner output is a lead only)
- FACT (drawio-desktop@2edf9fb, static read): the main is ESM and imports named members from `electron`. At module top level it also loads packages that import `electron` in three shapes: electron-store 11.0.2 (ESM default), electron-context-menu 5.1.0 (ESM default), electron-is-dev 3.0.1 (ESM default; pulled in by electron-context-menu, throws TypeError at import when `electron` is a string, reads `app.isPackaged` at evaluation), electron-dl 5.0.0 (ESM named {app, BrowserWindow, shell, dialog}; pulled in by electron-context-menu), electron-log 5.4.4 (CJS require). electron-updater is replaced by the F09-T1 adapter (PANEL-D14).
- FACT: draw.io parses arguments with `if (process.defaultApp != true) argv.unshift(null)` and then `argv.slice(2)`. Its preload exposes `process.type` and the whole `process.versions` object to the page.
- FACT: draw.io ships no native addon. Its only package with an install script, electron-winstaller, is a build-time dependency.
- FACT: draw.io's child_process use is: attrib.exe (Windows only), and one execFile per platform for local fonts (PowerShell on Windows, `fc-list` everywhere else including macOS; 30 s timeout; on error it resolves an empty list). The execFile is reached from the renderer action `getLocalFonts`.
- UNKNOWN: whether the 4-step workflow triggers `getLocalFonts`, and whether the web app reads `process.versions.electron`/`chrome`. The drawio web submodule is empty in the corpus clone; PANEL-P3 populates it.
- Import-time Electron member demand of the five packages is a conformance lead on the owning family tickets, not an X03 deliverable (X03-A6). PANEL-P3 produces the authoritative list. Leads:
  - app.getPath('userData')/getVersion/isPackaged (F01-T4)
  - BrowserWindow.getAllWindows() before ready and app 'browser-window-created' (F02/F01)
  - ipcMain.on/handle registration at import (F04-T3)
  - session.registerPreloadScript (F05/F07)
  - Menu/shell/dialog/clipboard (F06)
  - the electron-dl download surface, demanded only when Save Image actions run (F05)
- Zettlr (second app, waits per PANEL-D12): nodehun (raw .node import), chokidar ^5 (pure JS over fs.watch), and fsevents as a direct optionalDependency with no import site. It has six spawn sites, four of which hard-code `shell: true`.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: X03-T3 entries are recorded as KEL-74 cells with an explicit expected status that the runner asserts.
- L1: draw.io's main evaluates past every import under Bun 1.4.2 on macOS (X03-T1 + X03-T4 + F01-T4).
- L2: the X03-T3 entries pass on macOS arm64.
- L3: the draw.io activation cell (declared in X02-T4) is scored by the first-proof scoring run X02-T6 under the declared legacy profile (X03-T7).
Claims are only of the form `{passed}/{N} of product corpus {id}@{digest} ({kind})`. No percentage appears without a committed denominator, and the committed product-corpus list is empty today.

## Linear owners consumed (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07, read-only)
- KEL-72 Done (unassigned; re-fetched 2026-10-07): shipped @keld/electron v0. No live Linear issue covers packaging it, so under X06-D7 the X03-T1 GitHub issue (#502) is its tracker of record (see Tracker of record below).
- KEL-75 In Progress (unassigned; re-fetched 2026-10-07): role spawn contract, tracker of record for X03-T4 and X03-T6. Its spec task list has no pre-entry installation task.
- KEL-78 In Progress (GYLDLAB; re-fetched 2026-10-07): tracker of record for X03-T5 and X03-T7; profile states and the key, which "does not exist today". Task T6 (reporting surfaces) and T7 (addon worker) are unchecked.
- KEL-215 Done: evidence-row shape for addon claims.
- KEL-76 Backlog (unassigned): titled PTY/ConPTY. The arch 05 spec says it also owns the non-PTY `process` row, but the issue disagrees. The packet records owner STOP comments from 2026-08-19/20.
- KEL-77 In Progress: the VS Code extension-host differential harness (showcase). It is not a general child_process owner. N-API and libuv are spec non-goals.
- KEL-96 In Progress (GYLDLAB): the boot descriptor, the host source of app name (consumed through F01-T4).
- KEL-127 Todo (unassigned; re-fetched 2026-10-07): the program; non-goal 'additional native-module names' before G2. It is the fallback Linear reference (a link only, never a status copy) for the GitHub-tracked X03 tickets.
- KEL-140, KEL-141, KEL-143 Backlog.
- KEL-237 In Progress (unassigned; re-fetched 2026-10-07): not aligned for X03, because its non-goals exclude compatibility-surface expansion (#517 facts); KEL-74 Done; KEL-17 Done (arch 04 owner; the CLI tracks `migrate` there).
- Not owners or blockers for X03: KEL-15 Done, KEL-19 Done, and KEL-89 (In Progress, keld-auth, not secrets).

## Tracker of record (X06-D7)
FACT (gyldlab/keld#517, owner-decision comment by @0monish, 2026-10-06; #517 closed): the program aligns each repo-writing ticket to the nearest live Linear issue whose scope covers it, and claims there. Otherwise the GitHub issue is the tracker of record: it holds the `## Agent claim` comment (earliest wins; the assignee mirrors it), status, handoffs and evidence, and no Linear issue is created. The nearest live Linear issue, falling back to KEL-127, carries a link to the GitHub ticket. That comment explicitly supersedes the body's earlier option-C recommendation.
- X03-T1: GitHub #502 (no live Linear scope covers packaging); link on KEL-127.
- X03-T3: its own GitHub issue (number assigned at publication); link on KEL-127. KEL-237 is not aligned (its non-goals exclude this).
- X03-T4, X03-T6: KEL-75 (live; role spawn scope).
- X03-T5, X03-T7: KEL-78 (live; profile scope).
- X03-T2 (parked): KEL-78 for the outcome tree; new rows on GitHub #503 when pulled.
Residual gap: root AGENTS.md and the workflow claim protocol still describe Linear-only tracking. Until they are amended through the instruction-change protocol (a separate, owner-authorized change), the #517 record and map #391 are the documented exception that every X03 ticket cites. No X03 ticket waits on a Linear owner.

## Design facts (labelled; the batch-2 refuter verdicts are applied)
- FACT (pinned v44.4.5 resolver source and ESM loader patch): all five specifiers map to one builtin. The ESM loader exposes `default` plus every key of the export object as named exports. The pinned process-model page says the subpaths contain TypeScript type subsets and 'have no impact on runtime'.
- FACT (refuter probes, Bun 1.4.2 macOS arm64, not re-run here):
  - a preload plugin's onResolve is never invoked for bare specifiers or `node:` builtins at runtime;
  - preload `build.module` virtual modules resolve the five only when started from the bunfig directory, and are silently absent otherwise;
  - tsconfig paths is a live runtime resolver that outranks node_modules for bare `electron` but not for subpaths, so two module instances become possible;
  - a package-manifest dependency alias keyed `electron` with an exports map resolved 5/5 on Bun and on Node 26.
  X02-A1 chose the dependency alias.
- FACT: Electron documents `defaultApp`/`mas`/`windowsStore`/`sandboxed` as true-or-undefined and `contextIsolated` as undefined in main. It also documents `defaultApp` as useful 'to determine how many arguments will need to be sliced off from process.argv', and as possibly true even when packaged.
- FACT: @keld/electron installs `process.type` and `versions.electron` only when the facade module itself evaluates. A process.type-gated package evaluated first takes the Node path; draw.io only happens to import in a working order.
- INFERENCE: a Bun role's argv is [runtime, entry, ...args], since the role spawn passes its configured args; this has not been measured in a draw.io run. Under that shape, an undefined `defaultApp` makes draw.io treat its own entry path as a file to open.
- FACT: keld-runtime RoleConfig already carries a per-spawn env list, the reuse point for the F01-T4 payload. KEL-78 §4 I/O ('child receives KELD_APP_LINK and fixed-direction log sinks only') and arch 06 §1 ('no parallel KELD_* contracts') need amending, and that amendment is owned by F01-T4. keld-pack ExpectedAppIdentity is not a fact source (app id, channel, target and update key only).
- FACT: the evidence schema accepts panel ∈ {product, showcase}, kind ∈ {install, activation, primary_workflow, full_feature}, and authority_profile ∈ {strict_bun, sandboxed_addon_worker, legacy_sandbox_off, user_approved_tool_child}. There is no `unverified` value, so an undeclared app is unscoreable by design.
- FACT: with no node_modules, Bun 1.4.2 auto-resolved bare `electron` to the global install cache (electron@44.5.1) without error. INFERENCE (untested): it would fetch from the network when the cache is cold.
- Correction: arch 04 §2 names the file bunfig; the `[alias]` table appears only in the §3 v0 note, which already calls treating it as the resolver a defect. The fix is carried by the X02-T1 spec PR (X02-A1).

## Platform lanes
macOS arm64 on Bun 1.4.2 is the only executed lane. Windows and Linux runs of the resolver and argv fixtures are an explicit gap until a lane runs them. The parity of `bun build --compile`, tsc and webpack through the alias is UNKNOWN. On Windows strict, LPAC denies attrib.exe/PowerShell spawns, which is parked behind KEL-76. Oracle skew: draw.io's lockfile resolves electron 44.5.1 against the 44.4.5 oracle.

## Cross-unit edges recorded for other owners
- X02-T6 (the first-proof scoring run, the ticket that flips cells) must be gated by X03-T1, X03-T4 and X03-T7. X03-T1 is already upstream. X03-T4 is missing: draw.io's argv slicing and its preload's process.type/versions read need the main-role facts before entry. X03-T7 is missing: every scored record must carry authority_profile legacy_sandbox_off, and only X03-T7 produces it. Notes elsewhere that say 'X02-T4 consumes ...' should name X02-T6.
- X02-T1 and X02-T3 must be blocked by X03-T5, which selects the profile key's file. X02-T3 should read 'the profile key in the file X03-T5 selects', not keld.config.ts. X02-T1's key→owner row for the profile key should name X03-T5 (spec) and X03-T7 (implementation), not the parent issue KEL-78.
- X02-T3's acceptance line about packages resolving `require("electron")` duplicates X03-T1 and should shrink to 'writes the alias and removes tsconfig paths.electron'. Its ownership line also gives 'the fail-closed spawn without auto-install' to X03-T1; that atom is X03-T6 (milestone next).
- F09-T1 consumes X03-T1's alias mechanism for its adapter.
- F01-T4 should drop process.resourcesPath/defaultApp/argv from its title and delete its process.defaultApp/argv acceptance criterion; its consumer note should name X03-T4, not X03-T1. F01-T4 keeps the payload values, the delivery of OS user arguments to the role, the fail-closed behaviour, the app.* getters and the `assets` path name (Windows/Linux only). X03-T4 is the sole process.* owner, and X03-T3 entry (c) is the only (argv, defaultApp) cell; F01-T1 carries no process.* cell.

## Tracer-bullet tickets
- X03-T3: conformance entries (first)
- X03-T1: one `electron` module
- X03-T4: main-role process facts before entry
- X03-T5: legacy profile key spec
- X03-T7: legacy profile key implementation
- X03-T6: auto-install guard (next)
- X03-T2: native-addon policy record (parked)

tickets.title: feat(runtime): @keld/electron as the single `electron` module — self-contained require()-able entry, four subpath exports, one object for ESM and CJS from app code and node_modules
tickets.what_to_build:
Make @keld/electron consumable as an installed package that is the target of the app's package-manifest dependency alias keyed `electron`. This is closed decision X02-A1: no runtime plugin, no bunfig alias, and tsconfig paths is not a resolver.

The entry:
- maps all five specifiers (`electron`, `electron/main`, `electron/renderer`, `electron/common`, `electron/utility`) through package exports to ONE file;
- is self-contained, with no import that reaches outside the package and @keld/api consumed as a declared dependency;
- is require()-able from CJS, with no top-level await;
- exposes `default` plus every key of the default object as an ESM named export, cloning Electron's ESM loader contract.

In the same change, switch the KEL-72 fixtures from tsconfig paths to the dependency form and delete their inert bunfig [alias] table.

Add a one-instance guard: a second evaluation of the entry inside one role fails closed with a typed KELD-COMPAT error. This makes the leftover-tsconfig-paths split observable.

Adjacent atoms owned elsewhere:
- X02-T3 writes the alias into the app manifest and removes any tsconfig `paths.electron`.
- F09-T1 owns the electron-updater adapter alias, using the same mechanism.
- Each family facade ticket owns the presence and behaviour of individual member names (BrowserWindow, dialog, shell, ipcMain...).
- X03-T4 owns process.* values.
acceptance_criteria: X03-T3's conformance entries for the specifier contract land first. They quote the pinned Electron v44.4.5 process-model sentence ('These aliases have no impact on runtime') and the pinned v44.4.5 resolver set of five names. This change flips them from their recorded expected status to pass.

On Bun 1.4.2 macOS arm64, every combination resolves to the same object (the `app` export is identity-equal across all of them). The combinations are: each of the five specifiers × {ESM default, ESM named, ESM namespace, CJS require} × {app code, a node_modules dependency}.
Under Node 26 the same matrix resolves to the shim, showing node_modules is the single source of truth for every resolver.
The set of ESM named exports equals the set of keys of the default export.

At their corpus-pinned versions, draw.io's five import-time `electron` consumers each receive the shim object, never the npm path string: electron-store, electron-context-menu and electron-is-dev (ESM default), electron-dl (ESM named) and electron-log (CJS require).
Evaluating the entry a second time in one role throws a typed KELD-COMPAT error that names both resolved locations.
negative_controls: Removing the dependency alias makes the electron-is-dev-shaped dependency throw TypeError at import, and the entry fails.
Mapping the import and require export conditions to two different files fails the identity assertion.
Adding a tsconfig `paths.electron` entry beside the alias on Bun fires the one-instance guard.
Dropping `default` from the export set fails the ESM default-import probe with 'Missing default export'.
blocked_by_external: Closed decision X02-A1 resolution text on gyldlab/keld#412. It is consumed as binding text, not as a gate.
tickets.linear_owner: Tracker of record: GitHub #502 under X06-D7 (gyldlab/keld#517 owner decision, 2026-10-06), because no live Linear issue covers @keld/electron packaging. Linear reference: a link on KEL-127 (Todo, unassigned). KEL-72 (Done, unassigned) shipped v0, KEL-17 (Done, GYLDLAB) owns the arch 04 text, and KEL-237 (In Progress, unassigned) is not aligned because its non-goals exclude compat-surface expansion (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07). The claim is the `## Agent claim` comment on #502; the earliest comment wins.

tickets.title: feat(runtime): main-role process.* facts installed before the app entry evaluates — (argv, defaultApp) as one atom, type/versions/resourcesPath, undefined-not-false, honest versions.electron
tickets.what_to_build:
Install the main-role Electron process facts from the F01-T4 boot payload in the role bootstrap, BEFORE the app entry module evaluates. Facade import time is order-dependent and is refuted.

Values:
- `type` = 'browser';
- `versions.electron` = the published Keld shim version constant, never an Electron release;
- `versions.chrome` absent in the main role, recorded ✘;
- `resourcesPath` from the payload;
- `mas`, `windowsStore`, `sandboxed`, `contextIsolated`, `isMainFrame` undefined in the main role. No MAS or MSIX Keld packaging mode exists; whether one is planned is UNKNOWN.

`defaultApp` and `argv` are ONE atom, and the spec picks its shape:
- Option A (recommended, smallest): keep the Bun argv [runtime, entry, ...user] and set `defaultApp` = true. Electron documents defaultApp true 'even if the app is packaged'.
- Option B: rewrite argv to the packaged shape [exe, ...user] and leave `defaultApp` undefined.
Falsifier for A: the PANEL-P3 trace shows a draw.io or dependency path that branches on defaultApp for anything other than argv slicing.

`execPath` keeps Node semantics unless the spec proves otherwise (UNKNOWN; decided together with the argv atom).

The pre-entry mechanism is chosen in the spec as a KEL-75 role-spawn amendment: a role command-line preload, or a host-owned bootstrap entry that then imports the app entry. Constraints: it must not resolve modules (X03-T1 owns resolution), must not add a second link or inherited handle, and must not read any source other than the payload.

Ownership: this ticket is the sole owner of every main-role process.* value and observable, including the (argv, defaultApp) atom; X03-T3 entry (c) is its only cell.

Adjacent atoms owned elsewhere:
- F01-T4 owns payload content, its delivery (including forwarding the OS user arguments to the role) and its fail-closed behaviour, and the app.* getters. It asserts no process.* observable.
- F07-T1 owns the renderer/preload process object.
- X03-T1 owns module resolution.
acceptance_criteria: X03-T3's conformance entries b–f exist with an explicit expected status before this lands, and this change flips them to pass.
A fixture whose entry imports an electron-log-shaped package before importing `electron` sees `process.type === 'browser'` while that package evaluates, and the package selects its main mode.

A draw.io-shaped fixture's `argv.slice(defaultApp ? 2 : 1)` equals the user arguments under `keld dev` on macOS. The installed-launch half is an X03-T3 cell recorded with expected status unknown, naming KEL-141 (Backlog, unassigned; Linear fetched 2026-10-07), until a macOS installed artifact exists.
In the main role, `typeof` is 'undefined' for mas, windowsStore, sandboxed, contextIsolated and isMainFrame, and for defaultApp only if Option B is chosen.
`process.versions.electron` equals the Keld shim constant. The honesty entry fails if it equals the pinned oracle release or any string on the pinned Electron release list.
No process fact is derived from an environment variable, a path heuristic or a source other than the F01-T4 payload.

repair.epic_title: program(security): Electron security surfaces mapped onto their existing Keld owners (keld-guard, KEL-142 bridge, principalized roles, host-owned signed feed): one row, one owner, one negative test per row
repair.epic_body:
## Scope
X04 owns four atoms and nothing else.
1. **X04-D3** (open prototype, first-proof): choose how draw.io's multi-file renderer loads on WKWebView with a content security policy at least as strict as draw.io's own and with reads confined to the app code directory. F05-T4 consumes its result (the chosen arm, the directive list, the outside-code-directory probe list). Following its decision packet, the D3 question is narrowed to this one atom. The custom-scheme privilege and traversal matrix moves to F05-T2, with Zettlr `safe-file://` as the demand. Persisted user-granted roots move to X04-T3 (parked).
2. **X04-T1** (next): the mapping spec. Every Electron security surface maps to exactly one owning Keld mechanism and one owning ticket, with its classification, the pinned v44.4.5 receipt and a negative-test id. X04-T1 also owns the per-engine permission-hook table, which F05-T3 implements. It references the tables other tickets own and does not copy them. F02-T4 owns WebPreferences (including webviewTag). The F04-A1 KEL-102 amendment owns the `el:<channel>` grammar and the arch 03 §3 `el:*` example fix. X04-D3/F05-T4 own the CSP profile. X04-T1 is a recorder, not a gate, for decisions taken elsewhere: the `dialog` and `menu` literals are fixed by closed decision F06-D3 (option A), and the ruling on whether host-pushed screen/theme facts are ungated or gated by an `app.system` literal is owned by the F06-T5 spec under its permission-model gate. X04-T1 records both as rows after the fact, and no first-proof ticket waits for it.
3. **X04-T2** (next): the window-level web grant spec. It covers `windows.<w>.web.<name>` evaluated for the registry-derived webview principal, plus a closed web capability vocabulary that keld-guard enforces at manifest load. No live or specified owner exists for this atom today.
4. **X04-T3** (parked): one contract for runtime-minted filesystem path scopes under a frozen manifest: dialog-derived, OS-delivered and persisted roots. Strict profile only.
Family tickets do all implementation: F01-T5 and F01-T6 (single-instance, open-file/open-url, protocol client), F02-T4, F04-T3, F05-T2, F05-T3, F05-T4, F05-T6 (certificate and net rows), F06-T2 and F06-T4 (dialog and menu literals per F06-D3), F06-T5 (screen/theme facts and their grant ruling), F06-T3 (shell broker under X04-D4 option A), F07-T1 (preload, `process.argv` from additionalArguments), F09-T1 (updater adapter, PANEL-D14), X02-T2 (migrate security report section), and X05-T2 (capability-name allocation).

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites; FACT unless labelled)
- **draw.io @2edf9fb.**
  - All 4 of its BrowserWindow sites set `disableBlinkFeatures: 'Auxclick'`, with contextIsolation true, nodeIntegration false, webviewTag false and webSecurity true.
  - One response-header policy applies to every response: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self'` (plus Google Fonts hosts when enabled); `img-src * data:; media-src *; font-src * data:; frame-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; base-uri 'none'; child-src 'self'; object-src 'none'`. A file-URL request filter cancels anything outside its code directory.
  - It makes no setPermissionRequestHandler, setPermissionCheckHandler, protocol.handle or registerSchemesAsPrivileged calls.
  - shell.openExternal is gated by the scheme regex `https?|mailto|tel|callto`. It is reached from Help-menu literals, the window-open handler and a renderer request. None of these is on the first-proof workflow.
  - The updater is the `electron-updater` npm package. Electron's `autoUpdater` has 0 resolved sites.
  - Its afterPack build script flips seven fuses: RunAsNode=false, EnableCookieEncryption=true, EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable=false, EnableNodeCliInspectArguments=false, OnlyLoadAppFromAsar=true, EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation=false (TODO in source), LoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot=false.
  - The second-instance handler pops the last argv token.
- **draw.io renderer:** the drawio submodule is empty in the clone. Renderer-side permission demand and the renderer's own meta policy are UNKNOWN.
- **Zettlr @e6c7fd8.**
  - `protocol.handle('safe-file')` decodes and reads any absolute path, and there is no registerSchemesAsPrivileged call.
  - sandbox:false is set on 2 of 14 windows. All 14 share one preload whose only Electron imports are contextBridge, ipcRenderer and webUtils, so sandbox:false is ▲ inert, not ✘.
  - Renderer navigator.clipboard read/readText/writeText calls map to Electron's `clipboard-read` and `clipboard-sanitized-write` permissions, which Electron auto-approves.
  - shell.openPath has 16 sites and openExternal has 7.
  - Its updater is hand-rolled: net request, then a file write stream, then shell.openPath on the installer, then quit.
  - Workspace roots are persisted in its config and reopened on the next launch without any user event.

## Maturity ladder
- **L0:** a mapping row with its pinned receipt and a named negative-test id.
- **L1:** a KEL-74 conformance cell recorded with an explicit expected status that the runner asserts (red-until-implemented, never skipped or retried).
- **L2:** the implementing family ticket flips that cell to pass together with its negative control.

X04 tickets stop at L0. L1 and L2 live in the family tickets.
Milestones: X04-D3 is the only first-proof item. X04-T1 and X04-T2 are next. X04-T3 is parked. Because X04-T1 is next, no first-proof ticket may list it as a blocker; a first-proof ticket that needs a security ruling owns that ruling in its own spec (as F06-T5 does) or consumes a closed decision (as F06-T2 and F06-T4 consume F06-D3).

## Linear owners consumed (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07, read-only)
- KEL-102 guard enforcement spec: In Progress, unassigned. It is the permission-model owner. Its D9 row authorizes no manifest-schema change.
- KEL-78 strict-profile sandbox: In Progress, GYLDLAB. Electron `sandbox` is not the profile key.
- KEL-79 secure-origin and resource transport: Backlog, unassigned, no spec in the repo.
- KEL-130 retained filesystem: Done, Amisha Ramani. It landed snapshot-bound literal scopes.
- KEL-132 webview GPU/media: In Progress, unassigned.
- KEL-135 persistent profile identity: In Progress, Amisha Ramani. SAVED-GRANT revocation evidence is still open.
- KEL-142 renderer bridge: Done.
- KEL-53 updater: In Progress, Amisha Ramani.
- KEL-254 Windows installed-root boot: In Progress, Amisha Ramani.
- KEL-19 CLI RFC: Done. Its T1 ExpectedAppIdentity container writer and readers landed at e330db8f.
- KEL-212 inert-grant deny text and doctor: In Progress, Amisha Ramani.
- KEL-74 scoreboard: Done.
- KEL-75 principalized roles: In Progress, unassigned.
- KEL-127 program convergence: Todo, unassigned.
- KEL-208 is Done and is not an owner. KEL-209 is not cited.

Tracker of record: no live KEL issue scopes X04-T1, X04-T2 or X04-T3, so under the owner decision #517 (X06-D7) each one's own GitHub issue is its tracker of record, with KEL-102 as the Linear reference.

## Design facts
- FACT (keld-guard, origin/main 29a4cd70): evaluate denies every non-AppProcess principal with KELD-GUARD006 before any grant lookup. The manifest parser ignores `windows`, `audit` and other unknown top-level keys. There is no closed capability registry: any `app.<group>.<action>` string array whose scope matches allows.
- FACT (KEL-102 spec, T4 row): T4 passes the registry-derived webview principal to the media backends and keeps default denial "until a separately approved window-grant slice exists". This corrects the published claim that webview grants arrive with KEL-102/T4. Window-level web grants have no owner, so X04-T2 owns them.
- FACT: the production macOS/Linux media builders currently evaluate against an empty default manifest; KEL-102/T4 owns removing those constructions. The media callbacks evaluate resource `*` because wry exposes no origin. WebView2 exposes a Uri, but the v0 adapter reads only the permission kind.
- FACT (Electron v44.4.5, security tutorial): "By default, Electron will automatically approve all permission requests unless the developer has manually configured a custom handler." Keld inverts this: a missing handler is a deny and a handler can only narrow.
- FACT (v44.4.5 session API): camera and microphone share the permission name `media`. A request carries `mediaTypes` (an array) and a check carries one `mediaType`. The `openExternal` permission (OpenExternalPermissionRequest.externalURL) gates page-initiated external-protocol opens, not main-process shell.openExternal. The permission list mirrors Chromium. Keld has a host broker only for camera and microphone.
- FACT (X04-D4, closed by delegated owner decision): option A is the standing behaviour: exact literal origins, and every other URL is a typed refusal recorded as a declared divergence. Confirm-class tokens and scheme-wide globs are rejected. A bare `https:` entry is inert today because a pattern without `/**` is compared by exact string equality, not because of the authority rule. The shared matcher stays untouched. Option C (a distinct scheme-class capability) is specified under KEL-102 only if a scored cell needs it.
- FACT (F06-D3, closed by delegated owner decision, option A): the first proof adds only the `dialog` and `menu` literals under `app.system` and registers only those channels. That decision, not X04-T1, fixes their spelling.
- FACT: no content-security-policy code exists in any Keld crate or package. arch 03 §2 names the `default` and `static-only` profiles without directive-level definitions. INFERENCE (not receipted): WKWebView offers no response-header hook for file-URL loads, so X04-D3 compares three arms: an injected meta policy, a host scheme handler that sets the header, and the app's own policy only.
- FACT (v44.4.5 protocol API): registerSchemesAsPrivileged "can only be used before the `ready` event", and `request.initiatorOrigin` is not controlled by the requesting page. Scheme privileges are host declarations and bypassCSP is never allowed; F05-T2 owns the matrix.
- FACT: OS-delivered intents (second-instance, open-file, open-url) are untrusted data admitted by the host (F01-T5). Zettlr refutes a one-shot exact-file grant: it adds directory roots and persists them. INFERENCE: under the first-proof legacy profile the Bun main keeps ambient filesystem access, so no scope is minted. The strict contract is parked in X04-T3.
- FACT: feed trust is host-only. The ed25519 key is compiled into the host (arch 06 §4a). PANEL-D14 makes electron-updater's setFeedURL a recorded no-op.
- FACT: all nine v44.4.5 fuses get a disposition in X04-T1, and none is an input to Keld authority. INFERENCE: Keld's signed package plus ExpectedAppIdentity supersede ASAR-only lookup and ASAR integrity. Only the container writer and readers have landed (KEL-19 T1); launch-time verification is partial (KEL-254 In Progress).
- FACT: device permissions (HID, USB, serial, Bluetooth, WebAuthn account selection) have no broker, principal or spec. They are documented as unsupported (✘) and never legacy.
- FACT: keld-compat already allocates KELD-COMPAT-001..009 in the single error-code registry. Any new facade code is allocated there.

## Platform lanes
macOS (WKWebView, WKUIDelegate) is first. The WebView2 and WebKitGTK columns of the permission-hook table are documented gaps until each one carries a primary-doc receipt. The published per-engine counts (14 kinds, 10 kinds) are unverified and will be re-receipted by X04-T1. No platform claim is made without a native run on that OS.

tickets.what_to_build:
Write the mapping spec. Use one row per surface in this census: (1) permission request/check handlers and their structures (PermissionRequest, MediaAccessPermissionRequest, OpenExternalPermissionRequest, FilesystemPermissionRequest); (2) setDisplayMediaRequestHandler; (3) device handlers and events (setDevicePermissionHandler, setUSBProtectedClassesHandler, setBluetoothPairingHandler, select-hid-device, select-serial-port, select-usb-device, select-bluetooth-device, select-webauthn-account, file-system-access-restricted, and the device added/removed/revoked events); (4) weak-isolation WebPreferences, by reference to F02-T4; (5) custom-scheme privileges and protocol.handle, by reference to F05-T2; (6) CSP and file-URL containment that makes webRequest listeners recorded no-ops, by reference to X04-D3/F05-T4; tickets.title: spec(guard): window-level web grants: `windows.<w>.web.<name>` evaluated for the registry-derived webview principal through the single `windows` reader, with a closed web capability vocabulary rejected at manifest load
tickets.current_behavior: keld-guard ignores the `windows` manifest section. evaluate denies every non-AppProcess principal with KELD-GUARD006, and no registry restricts capability names. KEL-102/T4 keeps webview media default-denied until a separately approved window-grant slice exists. KEL-102-D9 authorizes no manifest-schema change. No ticket or Linear issue owns that slice.
tickets.what_to_build:
Write the window-grant slice as a KEL-102 spec amendment task unit. It covers:
(a) keld-guard reads `windows.<w>.web.<name>` through the same single `windows` reader that the F04-A1 amendment adds for `windows.<w>.channels`. There is no second manifest parse path, and the facade holds no vocabulary.
(b) The evaluation principal is the registry-derived webview principal bound to window `<w>`. `/app` grants never apply to a webview.
(c) A closed web vocabulary lives in the generated schema and keld-guard: only names with a host broker (today web.camera and web.microphone) are accepted. Any other `web.<name>` key fails manifest load with a typed KELD-GUARD error naming the fix. New names are allocated under the X05-T2 rule.
(d) The resource stays the `*` sentinel until an engine supplies the requesting origin, and origin-shaped grants do not match the sentinel.
(e) Record the disposition of `clipboard-read` and `clipboard-sanitized-write` (engine-decided ▲ or a web clipboard grant) with the pinned v44.4.5 receipt and Zettlr as the demand.
(f) Name the KEL-102 task unit that implements the slice. F05-T3 consumes it.
tickets.key_interfaces: keld-guard manifest reader and evaluate; Principal::Webview from the host registry; generated permissions schema; X05-T2 capability-name constants.
acceptance_criteria: The spec defines test T-a: a manifest declaring `windows.main.web.hid` fails to load with a typed KELD-GUARD error, and the negative control is stated.
The spec defines test T-b: an `app.web.camera` grant does not authorize a webview principal (deny), and the negative control is stated.
The spec defines test T-c: `windows.main.web.camera` with an origin-shaped scope does not match the `*` sentinel, and the negative control is stated.
The spec defines test T-d: `windows.main.web.camera: ["*"]` allows a webview principal minted for window `main` and denies one minted for any other window, and the negative control is stated.
The spec names exactly one manifest reader for the `windows` section, shared with the F04-A1 channel grants, and names the implementing KEL-102 task unit.
The clipboard permission disposition is recorded with its pinned v44.4.5 receipt.
negative_controls: Removing the closed-vocabulary check lets the `web.hid` manifest load, so T-a fails.
Evaluating webview principals against `/app` grants turns T-b into an allow, so T-b fails.
Letting an origin-shaped scope match the sentinel turns T-c into an allow, so T-c fails.
Ignoring the window id in principal binding makes the other-window case allow, so T-d fails.
A draft that adds a second parse path for `web` grants fails the single-reader AC.
Recording the clipboard disposition without a receipt fails the receipt AC.

repair.epic_title: program(perf): attributed compat-overhead metric registry, the kipc channel-table slice, and bounded hot-path rules (no performance claim before measurement)
repair.epic_body:
## Scope

X05 owns three things and nothing else:
1. **The kipc channel-table slice (X05-T2, first-proof).** A single owner for kipc channel ids, so that first-proof tickets which allocate a new kipc channel do not add another hand-mirrored constant.
2. **Registered compat-overhead metric ids and their admission rules (X05-T1, parked).**
3. **The lane runs that produce numbers (X05-T3, parked).**

Open decision X05-A4 (#417, milestone next, parked behind the facade one-way path) holds the hot-path cost model. It is read as "bounded and attributed rules for facade hot paths", not "allocation-free". The #417 title should be changed to match.

X05 owns **zero Electron API members**. Every member of the pinned v44.4.5 API model is assigned to a family F01..F09 in the compat matrix, so this unit has no member enumeration.

**Moved out of X05 (one owner per atom):**
- The window-state mirror primitive goes to F02-T2, under policy PANEL-D18 (closed). F06-T5 consumes it.
- The renderer floor lift (N pending invokes, send/on events, payload bound) goes to F04-T2 as a KEL-80 slice.
- The sendSync mechanism goes to F04-A5 (open), with the contract from PANEL-D8 (closed).
- The invoke/send/sendSync conformance oracles go to F04-T1.
- Family sequencing and parallelism move to the map-level pull order (X06 corrections D1/D2).

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, grep -F, 2026-10-07; not token-scan counts)

- **drawio-desktop@2edf9fb (FACT):**
  - 0 `ipcRenderer.invoke`, 0 `ipcMain.handle`.
  - 15 `ipcMain.on`, 15 `event.reply`.
  - 13 main→renderer send lines (9 `webContents.send` + 4 `contents.send`).
  - 2 `ipcRenderer.send` in the preload. These implement a multiplexed request/response: `rendererReq` out, with replies on `mainResp` that carry whole file contents.
  - 0 `sendSync`.
  - The lockfile resolves Electron 44.5.1 (declared ^44.2.0).
- **zettlr@e6c7fd8 (FACT):**
  - 186 `ipcRenderer.invoke` in 64 files; 25 `ipcMain.handle`.
  - 6 `sendSync` wrapper sites.
  - The same channel name carries send/sendSync (to on-listeners) and invoke (to a handler) on `config-provider` and `citeproc-provider`.
  - 0 `BrowserWindow.getSize` (the 3 getSize hits are `nativeImage.getSize`); 1 BrowserWindow `resize` listener.
- **electron-quick-start@82dbb35 (FACT):**
  - No IPC at all: no ipcMain or ipcRenderer, and the renderer script is comments only.
  - The preload writes `process.versions` into the page.
  - The lockfile resolves Electron 44.4.3 (declared ^44.4.3).
- **INFERENCE: FACADE-RTT needs a fixture.** The invoke→handle→reply round trip cannot be measured on quick-start or draw.io without injecting code, so it belongs on a committed fixture app. The round trip draw.io actually uses is send→on→reply at document-sized payloads.

## Maturity ladder

- X05 tickets are L0: a spec, a registry, or a lane definition. No X05 ticket scores an Electron member cell.
- Evidence uses the KEL-74 verdict vocabulary Pass | Fail | Unknown | Waived (FACT: keld-compat evidence `Verdict` enum).
- BEHAVIOR_MATCH, CORPUS_VERIFIED and SCAFFOLDED are map labels, not KEL-74 verdicts, and X05 text does not use them.

## Measured today (FACT; never blended with targets or projections)

The no-blend rule is owned by the closed map decision PANEL-D11 (#431) and by the KEL-90/KEL-86 admission rules. The untracked Electron reference document is not an authority. The tracked budget scoreboard's "never blend" line covers split lanes only.

- **Memory:** Windows host-process RSS is 19,552 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB. Electron's smaller process tree won total RSS.
- **First paint:** Windows host-only diagnostic, Keld 469 / Tauri 479 / Electron 275 ms. Electron leads.
- **kipc Windows:** Bun↔Rust diagnostic p50 47.6 µs / p99 101.6 µs, `publication.eligible=false` (KEL-99, Done).
- **kipc macOS:** the Rust↔Rust library arm measures p99 ≈ 9.25–9.6 µs. The macOS and Linux Bun product arms are unmeasured.
- **Compat overhead:** no lane exists in keld-benches.
- **Rejected as claims:**
  - "kipc ~10x faster than Electron IPC"
  - "the mirror removes nearly all round trips"
  - "186 × RTT" (static call sites multiplied by an ineligible diagnostic)
  - "zero allocation per read"

## Linear owners consumed (Linear, fetched 2026-10-07, read-only)

- **KEL-90, In Progress (GYLDLAB).** Owns the result.v2 runner, the existing metric registry and matched full-application measurement. FACT from the KEL-127 description: "KEL-90 owns matched full-application measurements without replacing KEL-129's budget authority". Its admission gates bind X05-T1/T3:
  - generated-app lifecycle fidelity before any comparative metric;
  - at least 30 balanced independent launches;
  - comparator mode tags;
  - "a comparator crash, unsupported operation or correctness divergence invalidates that sample";
  - "not a second benchmarking system".
- **KEL-129, In Progress (GYLDLAB, parent KEL-127).** Budget semantics. Task artifact: the architecture 01 §5.1 ruling landed at 4fbf94bb (#186).
- **KEL-86, Backlog, unassigned.** Multi-level oracle honesty rules.
- **KEL-80, Backlog, unassigned.** Bounded virtual channels and payload bounds. Its body records that the TS write queue has no aggregate pending-call/byte limit, and that its first action is a producer/queue ownership ledger plus a bounded slow-consumer regression.
- **KEL-98, Done (2026-09-20).** Echo codegen. Pattern artifact: bde521c4 (#265). Its spec says the generated file contains no channel table, so it is cited as a pattern, not as the owner.
- **KEL-136, Done (2026-09-11).** The one generated TS app-link transport, 3fb9417a (#221). It forbids a second reader/writer/constant owner.
- **KEL-133, Done.** Receiver semantics.
- **KEL-127, Todo, unassigned.** Program parent.
- **KEL-74, Done; KEL-237, In Progress, unassigned.** Evidence schema and corpus runner.
- **BLOCKER: no open Linear issue owns the kipc channel table.** A search for "channel" and "schema" on 2026-10-07 found none; KEL-13 RFC and KEL-98 are Done. Under the owner decision #517 (X06-D7), the X05 tickets' own GitHub issues are their trackers of record, because the workspace is at its free issue cap; KEL-80 is the Linear reference that carries the links.

## Design facts (labelled; both batch-2 refuter lenses applied)

1. **Channel ids today.**
   - FACT: echo 1 and lifecycle 3 are defined in keld-ipc; fs 2 is defined in keld-native.
   - FACT: the TS transport mirrors 1 and 3, checked by a source-text parity test.
   - FACT: the macOS renderer bridge holds a third hand copy of echo 1, with no parity test and no dependency on keld-ipc.
   - FACT: the architecture 02 §4 destination is u16 handles resolved at handshake from schema names, with `keld gen` emitting the channel table and each channel's required capabilities.
   - Owner: X05-T2.
2. **Electron channels do not consume kipc channel ids.** FACT: Electron channel names are app-chosen strings carried as data under the enumerated per-window `el:<channel>` grant (PANEL-D13, closed). INFERENCE: few new kipc channel ids are needed, so per-family id ranges are refused. They would also put Electron taxonomy into keld-ipc.
3. **Allocation status is "bounded, per-frame allocating".**
   - FACT: the live TS frame reader copies every chunk and allocates per payload, and the Rust link read allocates a vector per payload.
   - Architecture 02 §6's zero-steady-state-allocation rule is a destination, not current behavior.
   - The repo's allocation-free rule governs the Rust kipc, event-loop and guard paths. A TypeScript structured-clone facade cannot be allocation-free.
   - No allocation claim may be made anywhere until an attributed lane shows it.
4. **The write queue is unbounded.** FACT: the TS write queue has no aggregate bound (KEL-80). INFERENCE: any facade one-way loop built before KEL-80's admission budget inherits an unbounded queue. A slow-consumer negative control is therefore required on F04-T2 and in SEND-FANOUT. "The write queue is the only queue" holds only under that budget.
5. **There is no known payload bound for webContents.send.**
   - FACT: `webContents.send` is a host-routed EVENT to a webview principal (architecture 02 §5).
   - FACT: the 4096-byte ceiling belongs to virtual ports (MessagePortMain) and to the KEL-142 minimum-slice payload cap. It is not a webContents.send bound.
   - UNKNOWN: the send bound (frame cap plus engine-injection cap). It is set by the KEL-80 slice through F04-T2.
   - INFERENCE: draw.io's file-content replies make this bound a first-proof prerequisite.
   - The largest one-way payload in the 4-step workflow is an observable to be added to PANEL-P3 (#420).
6. **Serialization failure differs from the docs.**
   - FACT: the v44.4.5 doc says unserializable `contents.send` arguments throw.
   - INFERENCE, read from v44.4.5 source and not yet run: main→renderer send, including `event.reply` and `sendToFrame`, catches and logs the failure, and throws only a TypeError for a non-string channel. Renderer→main `ipcRenderer.send`, `invoke` and `sendSync` let the failure propagate.
   - Routed to F04-T1 as a doc/source divergence entry, settled by one Electron oracle line.
7. **Error and reply oracles.**
   - FACT (v44.4.5 source): invoke rejections read "Error invoking remote method '<channel>': <error>".
   - FACT: a sendSync reply is sent when `returnValue` is assigned, which can happen after the listener returns.
   - INFERENCE: an unanswered sendSync is released only by the reply channel's "reply was never sent" fallback.
   - Routed to F04-T1. The X05 research oracles ("boom", "undefined after the handler returns") were wrong.
8. **The one-pending floor blocks both first apps.** FACT: KEL-142's one-pending/4 KiB floor blocks draw.io (one-way send plus reply with file payloads) and Zettlr (consecutive un-awaited invokes at store setup). The lift is F04-T2's three parts, delivered as a new KEL-80 slice spec. It is not an amendment to KEL-142, which is Done.
9. **The mirror is owned by F02-T2 alone.** The refuter corrections are F02-T2's to apply:
   - each host event carries a complete per-window snapshot;
   - no optimistic write-through of setter values;
   - object getters return a fresh copy on every read;
   - state events and renderer IPC share one ordered link;
   - "generation" is named by its minting owner.
10. **sendSync wording is owned by architecture 02 §5, not KEL-127.** Architecture 02 §5 owns "rate-limited + dev-warned blocking CALL with a deadline"; KEL-127 only says a silent async replacement changes the caller contract. F04-A5's experiment needs an identity arm, because the WKWebView scheme task exposes no frame or content world: page-world and iframe requests must be refused.

## Platform lanes

macOS first for every X05 ticket. Windows and Linux are a documented gap; Windows numbers exist only as diagnostics. The channel-table slice is OS-independent.

## Sequencing

- Pull order is owned by the map: first-proof → next → parked, derived from the draw.io trace.
- FACT: #319 orders migration breadth after the spine because of execution capacity. Drawing agents from the spine before KEL-140 lands is an owner decision; option A (keep the #312/#319 order) is recommended.
- X05-T2 is the only first-proof X05 item. It gates every first-proof ticket that allocates a new kipc channel id. Verified against the repaired map on 2026-10-07, the first-proof tickets that list X05-T2 are F02-T2, F04-T3, F06-T2 and F06-T4.
- X05-T1 and X05-T3 are parked and must not gate any first-proof ticket. The repaired F07-T1 (first-proof) lists X05-T1 only so that its app-world handler per-call cost has a registered metric id. That is a diagnostic with no threshold, and draw.io ships without it, so the edge is not a real gate. F07's repair must delete that edge, and either drop the diagnostic criterion or move it to a parked F07 follow-up that consumes X05-T1. X05-T1 reserves the PRELOAD-HANDLER-COST metric id for it.

tickets.title: spec(ipc): minimum slice of the architecture 02 §4 channel table — one keld-ipc-owned table of kipc channel ids, its entry fields, consumers and live/destination split (no per-family ranges)
tickets.tier: n/a (program ticket; owns no Electron member)
tickets.current_behavior:
FACT (origin/main 29a4cd70):
- echo = 1 and lifecycle = 3 are defined in keld-ipc; fs = 2 is defined in keld-native.
- The TypeScript app-link transport mirrors 1 and 3, checked by a source-text parity test.
- The macOS renderer bridge carries its own hand copy of echo = 1, with no parity test and no keld-ipc dependency.
- No single table lists the allocated ids. The architecture 02 §4 destination (handshake-resolved ids from schema names, with a channel table emitted by `keld gen`) is not live, and KEL-98's spec explicitly excludes a channel table.
tickets.what_to_build:
Write the spec (spec template) for the minimum slice of the architecture 02 §4 channel table. X05-T4 implements it.

The spec defines one channel table owned by keld-ipc. Each entry holds:
- a host-lifecycle-neutral name;
- the u16 id;
- the receive-policy class;
- the required capability, named by reference to the keld-guard manifest vocabulary or marked host-internal (no new capability-name registry).

It lists the current entries (echo = 1, fs = 2, lifecycle = 3) and states the rule by which a new channel obtains an id and an entry.

It names every production consumer that must derive its id from the table: keld-ipc echo/lifecycle, keld-native fs, the macOS renderer bridge, and the TypeScript app-link transport. It records whether the bridge gets the id from the host at construction or through a crate edge, and why.
